matches.note: An unusually unfocused Bob (Bob's Driver absent) is choke-slammed and pinned by Jack. Post-match, Bob no-sells and beats Jack down with a repeated facebuster ("Bob's Fury"), taking twelve security guards to break up; the newcomer Kue tries to join in with his own pool cue and is chased off.

Jak "The Boil" Lancer (managed by Mr. Agony) locks on his own cloverleaf finisher, but Kaurik (Famine, Four Horsemen) reaches the ropes; Lancer improvises a different hold, the "Royal Octopus," for the actual submission.

CWC Northeast Tag Team Champion Major Havok finishes Zack "The Enforcer" Crockett (House of Pain, cornered by Aric Crockett) with "Terror From Above" after ducking an Aric brass-knuckle cheapshot attempt at ringside.
Former New England Champion Johnny Blaze submits "Captain America" Tommy Pride with "Hell's Fire."
Mark Lynch (UKA, wrestling with a knee brace) submits Talon (Da Killer Connection) with "Cry For Mercy" after a top-rope Phoenix Plex.
A chair-heavy brawl; Chris "Wild Thing" Rogers finishes Fidel with a top-rope "Psychedelic Splash" onto two steel chairs laid across him.
The Outlaw (cornered by newly-introduced trainer Todd "The Irish Hammer" Logan) retains over Black Scorpion with a somersault body block, hooking both legs.

CWC Northeastern Heavyweight Champion Randy Cross (not billed for the title itself) beats Nikodemous Segier (UKA) to a Figure Four pin after the Outlaw — wearing a House of Pain shirt — slips out of the sealed cage, cold-cocks Segier with the New England Championship belt behind the referee's back, and unlocks the House of Pain cage afterward. The served text never bills this for Cross's own CWC Northeastern title.
matches.stipulation: No time limit — winner must score the fall with the Figure Four Leg Lock or it doesn't count; the loser forfeits the right to use the hold as a finisher; House of Pain and the UKA sealed in separate cages at ringside

name: NCW Friday Night Fights — 20 February 1998
notes: The Outlaw's own promo confirms the Executive's Club has fully disbanded ("the former Executive's Club successfully chased off the Regulators") and Randy Cross confirms House of Pain has cut loose the Harvester of Sorrow and Da Killer Connection as "dead weight," keeping only Deadbolt (injured, absent) — the main event closes with the Outlaw, wearing a House of Pain shirt, interfering for Cross against the UKA's Nikodemous Segier, a strong signal the Outlaw is aligning with House of Pain though no formal membership change is stated outright.

matches.note: The Oddball (managed by "Maniac" Michael Gates, who trips Gutter behind the referee's back) finishes Gutter (Four Horsemen) with his "Wipeout."
Johnny Dice knocks out Chris "Wild Thing" Rogers with his "Snake Eyes Slam" for the pin.
Kue submits Brian Cairo (wrestling alone since leaving Triple Threat) with the "Double Bank" arm wrench, improving to 2-0; Angel Reaper watches from the aisle without interfering.

A mysterious masked man in black, never identified in the broadcast's own text, silently joins Blaze's corner before the bell. Blaze sunset-flip-rolls up Nikodemous Segier (UKA, managed by Jennifer Camero) for the pin.
matches.stipulation: CWC Rhode Island Title Tournament — Round 1

matches.note: "The Ice" Jake Hetti finishes "Demented" Drake Blackthorne (UKA) with a brainbuster.
matches.stipulation: CWC Rhode Island Title Tournament — Round 1

matches.note: Zack "The Enforcer" Crockett (House of Pain, cornered by the full stable including the Outlaw) spinebusters Talon and dismissively steps on his face for the pin.
matches.stipulation: CWC Rhode Island Title Tournament — Round 1

matches.note: Britainicca (managed by Bonny McLain) finishes Mark Lynch (UKA) with a clothesline after both men trade near-falls; the round-2 bracket sets Blaze vs. Hetti and Zack Crockett vs. Britainicca.
matches.stipulation: CWC Rhode Island Title Tournament — Round 1

matches.note: With House of Pain (Randy Cross, Aric and Zack Crockett) at ringside, a ref bump lets Zack spinebuster champion Angel Reaper and drag challenger Jak Lancer on top for the pin — Lancer becomes the new champion off House of Pain's own interference, not a clean win. Post-match, a masked GRW crossover cameo (Aguayfuero) and the Black Scorpion both run in and are beaten down by House of Pain; Cross offers the new champion a handshake.
matches.stipulation: New York City Championship — no time limit

name: WWA — 25 February 1998
notes: The broadcast's own opening banter block ('we'll see the New York City title on the line as Angel Reaper defends against Brian Cairo... Shaman and Chris Rogers') is a stale, unedited leftover from the prior week's script and describes neither of this show's own actual featured matches — the card that actually airs is read from the Trudeau introductions and play-by-play instead, not the mismatched cold open. A mystery masked man in black debuts silently in Johnny Blaze's corner for his own tournament match — never named or explained in this show's own text, left as an honest, unminted gap.

matches.note: The Outlaw (House of Pain, cornered by trainer Todd Logan) superplexes Griffin (New Regulators) for the pin, then extends a post-match handshake.
Apocalypse scores an upset, scooping the Fifth Element into his own "Nuclear Blast" finisher.
House of Pain squashes Birds of Prey; Big Eliem finishes with his own over-the-shoulder "Da Sista of Mercy."
Jack (Famine, Four Horsemen) chokeslams Kue (House of Pain) for the pin while the Outlaw and Todd Logan watch from ringside.

A masked man wielding a 2x4 (aligned with Anarchy, previously seen interfering 13 and 27 Mar) knocks out both Crocketts from the outside; Britainicca zip-lines in with a fire extinguisher and sprays Anarchy off, who flee with the masked man. No pinfall or decision is ever recorded — Britainicca instead finishes an unconscious Zack Crockett with a "Union Jack Bomb" onto the discarded fire extinguisher as his own receipt. Genuinely unresolved in the held record, not guessed.
Champion Angel Reaper (wrestling under a new t-shirt reading "the CWC's BEST") retains over Shaman (New Regulators, cornered by Mad Coil) with a double underhook suplex bridge.

Steihl refuses to tag in Darken for the entire match, working almost the whole bout alone against Da Killer Connection (Total Anarchy) and finishing Tiburon with "The Steihl." A masked 2x4 man and Anarchy again interfere mid-match, drawing House of Pain out for a ringside brawl that doesn't affect the finish.
matches.stipulation: CWC National and Northeast Tag Team Championships

matches.note: A roughly 37-38-minute battle, both men trading the Figure Four to exhaustion; Cross covers a passed-out Segier for the pin to regain the title, House of Pain entering the cage to celebrate.
matches.stipulation: CWC Northeastern Heavyweight Championship — Steel Cage

name: WWA — 17 April 1998
notes: Randy Cross's own promo confirms the Anarchy stable's manager Havok, a masked man wielding a 2x4, is aligned with (or hired by) Anarchy — the same masked man from the 13/27 March shows' own interference, still unidentified this session.

matches.note: Vinnie "The Bronx" Bomber finishes "Captain America" Tommy Pride with the "B-52 Bomber."

Talon (Total Anarchy) nearly chokes Big Daddy Butler out with a sleeper, but Butler catches his own falling arm on the third drop and rallies, finishing with the "cookie crunch." Post-match, Big Eliem (House of Pain) chokeslams Butler and declares himself "the big man of the NCW."
Annihilation repeatedly super-backbreakers "The Icon" Eric Stanley for the pin.
Sonny Lightning's own salt-throw trick is caught and thrown back in his face; "Untouchable" Ryan Lee finishes with an ankle lock.
Dr. Edgar Von Harrisburg "The Psychotic" rolls up James Royal for the pin.
Capital (newly managed by Simons) finishes Fidel with his own "Capital Punishment."
Shaman (New Regulators) finishes the Mysterious Raven with a double powerslam into the "Thunder Clap."

Commissioner Harrington orders champion Britainicca to defend against the Outlaw after scheduled challenger Zack Crockett no-shows. Todd Logan distracts Britainicca at ringside; the Outlaw finishes with the Outlaw Kick into a rollup to become the new champion, then Logan beats down the fallen Britainicca as the show ends.
Rob Thorne counters Ryan Lee's own "Lights Out" reverse DDT attempt with a Diamond-Cutter-style counter, then finishes with his own STF, "The End of the Road."
Paul Valentine finishes "Lightning" Joe Clapp with his own "Bone Grinder."
Annihilation finishes Capital with his own "Super Back Breaker," moving to 2-0.
A double countout brawl outside the ring; the referee explicitly calls it a double countout. Both men keep fighting through the bell, security unable to fully separate them.
Mad Coil (cornered by the Death Knight) finishes Fidel with the "Avalanche." Post-match, Mad Coil calls out Big Eliem on the microphone, declaring a "war of the big men."

Angel Reaper (not scheduled to appear) watches from the apron for unexplained reasons; the same masked man with a 2x4 seen interfering in earlier shows swings at Stevens, misses, and knocks out Reddy instead. "Rock Hard" Rocky Stevens covers the fallen Reddy for the win — the masked man's own identity and his connection to Angel Reaper remain unexplained in the held record read this session.
Todd Logan (cornered by the Outlaw) and Britainicca brawl out of the ring and up the aisle without ever returning; the referee rules a no-contest.

House of Pain (Jak Lancer, Big Eliem, Chris Rogers) run in and brawl at ringside with Darken and a returning Jack throughout the match's back half, but never reach the ring in time; Steihl (Overlords of the Dark) pins champion Randy Cross clean with a modified Outsider's Edge, "The Steihl," to become the new champion.
Anarchy (Raiden and Chaos) finish Black Scorpion, Chaos holding him for Raiden's top-rope strike.
Vinnie "The Bronx" Bomber finishes Propane with the "B-52 Bomber" into the "Bronx Bomb."
Nik Segier submits Apocalypse with the "Segier Stretch."

Commissioner Harrington fines Thanatos, the Reaper of Souls, $5000 for cutting a promo demanding a match, then adds him to this one on the spot. Bob finishes a battered Big Eliem with a Vader-style corner bounce splash.
matches.stipulation: Big Man Match — pinfalls count anywhere

matches.note: Rocky Stevens abandons his own team, grabs a 2x4 from under the ring, and nails his own partner Shaman with it while Deadbolt fakes an injury to distract the referee; a suddenly-recovered Deadbolt pins Shaman. Post-match, Total Anarchy (minus Chaos) attacks Shaman and Mad Coil; the New Regulators try to help but are outnumbered until security breaks it up — the first sign Stevens has turned.

Chris "Wild Thing" Rogers (House of Pain) attacks champion Angel Reaper before the bell. The masked 2x4 man reappears and drops his board at ringside to distract the referee while Chaos, hidden under the ring, blindsides Rogers with the discarded board; Reaper strikes the distracted referee's back to draw his attention and gets the pin. The masked man unmasks as Havok; Anarchy (Chaos and Raiden) then reveal Reaper and Rocky Stevens as their two newest recruits, hoisting both on their shoulders.

name: WWA — 24 April 1998
notes: The masked 2x4 man from prior shows unmasks as Havok (Anarchy), and the same broadcast reveals Angel Reaper and Rocky Stevens as new Anarchy recruits — a heel turn for both.

matches.note: CWC Northeastern Heavyweight Champion Steihl finishes "The Icon" Eric Stanley with "The Steihl" after a big chokeslam.
Both men's NCW debuts. Flynn Steele finishes the Gambler with the "Steele Driver."
Both men's NCW debuts. Fire Storm (managed by a person billed only "Blaze") finishes "Mr. Extreme" Jimmy Walker with the "Rain of Fire."

With House of Pain (the Outlaw, Big Eliem) and Anarchy (Havok, Rocky Stevens) brawling at ringside throughout, Todd Logan coldcocks champion Angel Reaper with the Outlaw's own CWC Rhode Island Championship belt and locks in the "Irish Sleeper" for the submission, becoming the new champion.

eliminations.note: the "Somersault Whiplash Diamond Bomb"
pinned after House of Pain (Chris Rogers, Aric Crockett, the Outlaw, Big Eliem) ambush him with a chair on the way to the ring
piledriven onto a steel chair

pinned after the Black Scorpion knocks Rocky Stevens (Anarchy) out cold with his own 2x4, then he and the Fan (each briefly emerging from under the ring/crowd) take Raiden down with "The Equalizer" before fleeing

matches.note: Jack wins the first true Big Man match, earning a shot at another big man at the upcoming PPV.
matches.stipulation: NCW Big Man Award Elimination Match — falls count anywhere, no disqualification

matches.note: The Commandant's Own finish the Claymores (cornered by the MacGregors), Payne's "Aerial Assault" into Havok's "Terror From Above."

Todd Logan runs in and DDTs Jeff "The Machine" Keenan behind the referee's back; "The Irish Assassin" Gregory O'Hara covers for the pin. Post-match, Vinnie "The Bronx" Bomber cuts a promo threatening Logan, burning a wooden shamrock.
Big Daddy Butler, returning after a long absence, finishes Intensity with the "Cookie Crunch."

House of Pain runs in en masse to beat down Shane Warner (the Outlaw's own kick, Randy Cross slapping and punching him) before STB (ChiKylin, Flynn Steele) makes the save with chairs; no bell or formal decision is ever recorded.
Flynn Steele works over champion Jack's knee throughout, then counters Jack's "Famine Slam" attempt by shifting his weight for a rollup and the pin to become the new champion.

name: Saturday Night Main Event — 15 August 1998
notes: The broadcast itself calls this "the second official WWA card," confirming NCW has renamed to WWA by this point. Gutter teases a future "surprise announcement" unrelated to the Four Horsemen. Mad Coil confirms leading a group called "Warriors Pride," targeting Johnny Tambo, staying deliberately vague about the group's own goals or membership beyond himself — an honest, unresolved lead. Gutter's own loss to "Raven Crow" (billed a former Four Horsemen member) is referenced in an interview but never shown on-screen this session — not minted absent an actual appearance.

date.source: Dated by the fed's own card preview for this show, which reads "Sunday January 30, 2000" (promotions/wwa/archive/2000-01-30.html); the fed's own title-history ledger dates both title changes staged on this card (the Rookie Ring Championship to Captain Amazing, the Television Championship to Mantis) 30 January 2000; a later WWA broadcast replays this card's World Title and Television Title matches as "1/30/00 footage of WWA Rage In The Cage" (promotions/wwa/archive/2001-01-26.html); and 30 January 2000 was a Sunday. SOURCES DISAGREE: the script itself opens "January 31, 2000 -- Rage in the Cage" in the fed's 2006 archive copy (ragecage00), a Monday, and the copy first served here carried "January 31, 1999" over the same text; the script's own line is read as its posting date or a slip from the 1999 script's identical opening line, and both readings are recorded. The 1999 show (American West Arena, Phoenix) is a different script.

name: WWA Rage in the Cage — 30 January 2000
notes: One night, one row: this id absorbs wwa-2000-01-30, the record first made from the fed's own card preview for the same show (promotions/wwa/archive/2000-01-30.html, "Sunday January 30, 2000"), retired into it. This record's page is the show's own script, which opens "January 31, 2000"; the show is dated 30 January 2000 by the preview, the fed's own title history and a later broadcast's "1/30/00" replay caption (see date.source). The preview's billed names this record did not already credit are carried as billed rows citing the preview. The two title changes the fed's own title history dates to this night (Rookie Ring: Captain Amazing over Bolivian Rat; Television: Mantis in the triple threat with Shaman and Walcott) link here.

matches.note: A back-and-forth opener is broken up when Black Scorpion and the Mimic run in on Crosscheck; Ravage starts down the aisle too as the broadcast cuts to commercial with no finish.
Sir Michael's debut, managed by Lady Rachel. Wins with "The Joust," a top-rope spear.

Jack II — continuing his feud with House of Pain over a friend's death — finishes Zack with the "II Drop" neckbreaker into the "II Seat" submission. Aric Crockett and the Fan run in afterward to punish Jack II further, until Sgt. Payne and Major Havok (the Commandant's Own) make the save.
CPE vs. FEAR. Daring wins with the "Daring Death Drop" off the top rope. Daring cuts a cryptic post-match promo: "The storm is coming, and tonight, someone's going to get rained on."
MidCarder retains with the "HoseHead." Post-match, MidCarder tells Ken Steele on the mic to "leave that washed up stable and quit worrying about what your father thinks."

matches.stipulation: Number one contendership, WWA World Television Championship — three-way elimination
matches.note: Ashley Dunnin submits Ravage first with the "Wildfire" (a modified camel clutch); Nick Bruiser then pins Dunnin with the "Tiger Bomb" off an abdominal stretch to become the new number-one contender. Billy Coleman works the crowd at ringside throughout, cheering Ravage.

matches.stipulation: WWA United States Championship — Triple Threat, first fall wins
matches.note: O'Hara, the champion, forced the match by challenge after refusing to sign for a scheduled Logan/Denrol number-one-contender bout unless it became a three-way for his own title (banning HOP and CPE from ringside). Denrol wins the belt in a comedic finish — Denrol "blows" on Logan, who collapses, and Denrol pins him for the pin and the title, despite O'Hara being the actual champion. Immediately after, House of Pain (Zack and Aric Crockett, Steihl, the Fan, Randy Cross, the Outlaw) runs in and beats down Youthful Rage; Denrol sides with House of Pain against Sniper, who confronts him for "lowering himself" — Denrol strikes his own former mentor and CPE (Lantern, El Porto Spidero) beats Sniper down further before Denrol celebrates the new US Title with HOP.

Steihl blocks an early Randy Cross assault and controls much of the match, but Cross reverses a Steihl small-package attempt into his own for the pin and the title. Post-match, House of Pain (Outlaw, the Crocketts) beats Steihl down further and Cross re-applies the figure four out of spite before releasing him. Lone Wolf then attacks Cross with a crowbar; Jak Lancer runs out ostensibly to stop him but instead locks on the "Boil Lancer." Big Eliem runs in, knocks out both Lone Wolf and Lancer to save Cross — then turns on Cross too, hitting the "Sista of Mercy," tearing off his own House of Pain shirt, and spitting on Cross. Lancer and Eliem both appear to have left House of Pain within the same minute.

name: WWA — 5 February 1999
notes: Upgraded from a thin, ledger-derived stub (2 unresolved match fragments, no winners/stipulations/notes) to a fully match-deep structure by reading the served text end to end. Eight matches, headlined by two title changes: Denrol wins the WWA United States Championship from Gregory O'Hara in a triple threat also involving Todd Logan, and Randy Cross wins the WWA World Heavyweight Championship from Steihl in the main event — both already correctly tracked in reigns.json before this pass (wwa-united-states-r012, wwa-world-heavyweight-r010), confirmed against the served card. The show closes on a major angle: Jak Lancer and Big Eliem both appear to leave House of Pain within the same minute, Eliem turning on Cross moments after saving him from Lone Wolf.

matches.note: Sir Michael, accompanied by Lady Rachel, wins his WWA debut over the former Star Station-X member Misery, finishing with a top-rope "Joust."

Debuting tag team Maximum Overdrive (Williams and Tony Richards) upset the House of Pain's Minnesota Wrecking Crew. Steihl, unscheduled for the show, ambushes Zack Crockett at ringside with a reverse DDT off the apron, then beats down Aric after a tag, allowing Richards to roll Aric up for a fast three-count. Steihl continues the beatdown until security drags him out.

"The Smokejumper" Ashley Dunnin outlasts Lantern in a long, hard-fought bout, finishing with a sidewalk slam after Lantern nearly landed "The Light in the Darkness." The two shake hands after the bell.

Todd "The Irish Hammer" Logan escapes a near-submission to his own Irish Sleeper by smashing the referee's head into Payne's, then rallies and re-applies the hold for the win. Earlier, Logan Samoan-drops Payne into the announce table, taking out guest commentator Ravage. After the bell, Steihl runs in again and locks Logan in the "Painful Pleasure" until Randy Cantley's security crew hauls him off.

A chaotic title match: Denrol runs in with a chair to help the MidCarder, O'Hara and Kris Kasanova run in for Bruiser, the House of Pain (the Outlaw, Aric Crockett, Randy Cross) hits the ring, and the Outlaw superkicks the MidCarder behind the referee's back before Bruiser finishes him with a Tiger Bomb to win the title. Bruiser then accepts a House of Pain t-shirt from Aric and joins the stable, the belt handed to him by Todd Logan. Afterward, Mantis turns on ChiKylin — cracking a mic over his head, hitting the "Nutcracker" off the top rope while Bruiser DVDs him with the "Agony" — and joins the House of Pain as well, dubbing himself and Bruiser "the Blitzkreig." Randy Cross then announces his retirement as WWA World Heavyweight Champion, with the Outlaw giving him a tribute speech.
Mantis wins with the "Shocker," after putting Goldstar through a table with a moonsault.
Ravage, wrestling with stitches from his TV Title win over Nick Bruiser, wins with the "Ragebomb."
A hometown upset — Albatross wins by countout after slamming New Star through the broadcast table and off the ringside steps.
O'Hara wins with the "Leprechaun Leap" (a frog splash).

House of Pain en masse (Randy Cross, Outlaw, the Crocketts, Jon Cole, the Fan, Mantis) storms the ring and beats Bruiser down after the bell is rung for outside interference — the group has decided Bruiser is out of the stable. No winner is declared in the served text.
Griffin ("Lone Wolf"/"Griffin") wins with the "DD Driver."
Darken wins by a choke sleeper.

A back-and-forth classic; Daring reverses MidCarder's own "Reality Check" attempt into a Diamond Cutter of his own for the pin. MidCarder announces his retirement from the WWA on the mic immediately after, thanking Kris Kasanova and Gregory O'Hara and leaving Youthful Rage.
A swerve: Stabler and Statler feign a rivalry, jump Lazer together, and jointly pin him with a double piledriver — revealing themselves afterward as the new tag team "Enfuego."

name: WWA — 19 Mar 1999
notes: Upgraded from a thin, ledger-derived stub (1 unresolved match fragment) to a fully match-deep structure. A dual-arena broadcast — round 2 of the Eastern Region (Boston) intercut with round 2 of the Western Region (Los Angeles) — closing the tournament's second round at sixteen wrestlers remaining. President Mark Harrington announces a ten-man Rookie's Ring battle royal for a new "Rookie's Ring" prize, naming Lance Crash, Carl Goldstar, Albatross, Jon Cole, Timothy Micheals, Ice Tank, Tommy Lazer, Jordan Statler, Steve Stabler and Phoenix as entrants — not yet contested. MidCarder's retirement is a genuine roster departure.

matches.note: Walcott wins the Ring from Crash with the "Pretty Plex."
Mantis retains, keeping the leg hooked through a near-fall to finish with the "Shocker."

A brawl through the arena (concessions, a merch stand, the ladies' room, and out the front doors) ends when an unidentified masked man (later revealed as Raven Crow) blindsides Spidero with a spinning slam; Sir Michael, though also down, beats the 20 count and gets the pin once revived.

matches.stipulation: "Famine rules" (submission/count-back hybrid) — for the Famine role in the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse
matches.note: Fought entirely outside the ring and parking lot. Steihl submits to Jack II's Darken-style dragon-sleeper/camel-clutch combo, then fails to beat the referee's ten count back to the ring after a masked man (unmasked as Raven Crow) ambushes and chains him to a car; Jack II frees him first before the count expires. Jack II retains the Famine role.

name: WWA — 16 April 1999
notes: Upgraded from a thin, ledger-derived stub (1 unresolved match fragment) to a fully match-deep structure. A major, unresolved angle runs throughout: Gregory O'Hara suffers an apparent breakdown, climbs into the rafters muttering that "he is coming," and bungee-jumps off them mid-interview with Johny Morehouse.

name: WWA — 24 Apr 1999

matches.stipulation: Rookie Ring three-way (originally Lazer vs. Walcott before Randy Cross adds Cole)
matches.note: Cole ambushes Lazer before the bell on Randy Cross's orders. Walcott's manager, the Executive, brings a briefcase into play; the referee calls for the bell (a DQ on Walcott) after Walcott chair-shots Cole. The Executive then hands Walcott and Lazer matching "The Fraternity" shirts, revealing a new alliance between the two former rivals. House of Pain (Randy Cross, Outlaw, and the rest) surrounds the ring afterward but lets the Fraternity leave; Outlaw then has Jon Cole thrown out of the stable via the Fan's "Nightbringer."
The Minnesota Wrecking Crew wins with their spiked piledriver combination, aided by brass knuckles and a low blow while the referee is distracted.

matches.stipulation: Originally a handicap match; becomes a tag when Kasanova joins Spidero's corner
matches.note: A fourth Crusade member, an unnamed Masked Crusader, interferes on the outside. Youthful Rage (Ravage, New Star) runs in when the Mimic apologizes and the Crusade retreats — no clean finish. Afterward, Kasanova invites Spidero to join Youthful Rage on the mic, and Spidero accepts.
Jack II wins by submission with the "II Seat," earning a title-adjacent shot at Outlaw the following week.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship vs. WWA United States Championship — Round Robin
matches.note: Ravage wins with the "RageBomb," catching Griffin's Shooting Star Press attempt in mid-air.

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Championship vs. WWA World Television Championship — Round Robin
matches.note: Mantis wins with the "Shocker" after a long back-and-forth (including a New Star "cartoon" insert mocking Mantis as a giant cockroach), advancing in the Round Robin toward the vacant World Heavyweight Championship's Four Corners match.

notes: The go-home show before Pain Games. Jack II calls out House of Pain by name for "killing my brother, Jack," setting up a Todd Logan match with an Outlaw shot on the line. El Porto Spidero joins Youthful Rage in the show's own biggest angle.

matches.note: Blake Daniels' debut win, finishing with a self-styled "Real Deal" (jumping double-knee backbreaker).
Flynn Steele's first match back in the WWA; wins by submission with a banned hammerlock/backbreaker hold (referenced on commentary as previously used by Terry Gordy).
Darken wins with a "Cokeslam" into the "Dark Pogostick."

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Championship number-one contendership; previously recorded on WWA Extreme
matches.note: A bloody brawl; Outlaw wins by choking Shaman out, then gives Shaman his own earned title shot as a gesture of respect.
Todd Logan runs in with a nightstick and attacks both men; the referee calls a double DQ.

A rematch from their first-round tournament meeting. Lantern wins by submission with a spinning toe hold after taking Zack Crockett out of the match on exposed concrete with the "Light in the Darkness."

matches.stipulation: No time limit — for the WAR role in the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse
matches.note: Bob, after briefly dominating, unexpectedly lies down for the pin with no visible cause; the announcers find the finish as puzzling as the audience does. Steihl becomes the new WAR.
Jack II debuts a new fiery alter-ego, "Blaze," mid-entrance (a full character transformation staged as a Horsemen ritual) and upsets Outlaw with the "FamineSlam," a chokeslam variant.
Ravage evens his Round Robin record, finishing with the "RageBomb" after legitimately targeting Mantis's ankle, tweaked earlier in the match.

New Star, visibly distracted throughout by his father's recent death, is counted out after Denrol airs jumbotron footage of himself urinating on the grave of "Mega Mawler" — New Star's father, a retired wrestler — and New Star charges backstage after him.

name: WWA — 30 Apr 1999
notes: An unusually long, ten-match card folding in two previously-recorded WWA Extreme matches. Includes an in-character Outlaw/Darken sit-down interview segment ("Outlaw's Saloon") previewing the vacant World Heavyweight Championship picture.

matches.note: Thornhill finishes Death Warrior with "The Adrenaline Rush" off a superplex setup.

matches.stipulation: Billed for the "Least Interesting Tag Team" title, a novelty stipulation distinct from the WWA World Tag Team Championship; Dr. Slash Hayes, having paid ring announcer Gary Trudeau $5,000 to fill in for the night, is the guest announcer
matches.note: The Sitcom Fathers bring kendo sticks to ringside and finish Black Scorpion with a DDT for the pin.

Gary Trudeau reclaims the ring announcer duties from Hayes mid-show, dumping his payoff cash into the crowd. A weapons-heavy match (kendo... a steel chair, both men colliding with a double clothesline) ends in a double ten-count when neither man answers the referee's count; Troy Walcott runs in beforehand to hit Todd Logan with the "Fratliner" but leaves before the finish.

matches.stipulation: Master Xaviar, under a code-of-honor agreement with Sir Michael, stays backstage rather than seconding him
matches.note: Daniels finishes Sir Michael with "The Love Sick" for the pin. Afterward the Crusade (Black Scorpion) attacks Daniels, but the Fraternity (Chad Goodman, Tommy Lazer, Troy Walcott) runs in to make the save and turn on Sir Michael instead — Walcott, still holding a grudge over "The Journey to Avalon," locks Michael in the "Pretty Predicament" until officials pull him off.

Before the match airs, a backstage segment shows the Preacher of Pain dazed inside a chalked lantern symbol, implying an attack by Lantern. A brutal hardcore brawl follows (a kendo stick, brass knuckles, a table, a baseball bat, the Spanish announce table) in which the Preacher survives a Frankensteiner onto a chair before finishing Coleman with "The Decent" through the announce table to retain.

name: WWA Independence Day Rumble — 2 July 2000
notes: A WWA/FWA title-unification card — the FWA absorbed into the WWA's own banner the same night, per Jim Black's own in-fiction billing and the card's three other unification matches (US/North American, TV, World). The 25-man Royal Rumble opening the card is only partially structured (5 of 25 entrants resolve to registered ids); the WWA Extreme/FWA Hardcore unification followed separately on 28 July 2000 (wwa-2000-07-28), not on this card despite both being part of the same absorption story.

matches.note: Lethal Lottery final to determine the last Birthday Brawl qualifier. 357 puts himself through the ringside announce table on a missed frog splash; both men are counted out of the ring, but Vincible beats the count. Vincible wins by countout and pins the incapacitated 357 again after the bell for good measure.

name: Meltdown
venue: Brown County Veterans Memorial Arena Expo Centre Complex

matches.note: TJ Donaldson's one-night return (his regular tag partner "Amazingly Simple" is a no-show) against the Job Squad. Donaldson powerbombs Warrior onto Spike for a simultaneous pin on both.

eliminations.note: chokeslammed in an alleyway
Ian-Tensifier on the concrete, delivered while Tense was disguised as a homeless bystander
pinned in a bar after Kraven's own No More Tomorrows; a bar patron (a musician cameo, not a wrestler) makes the count in place of a referee
arrested by New Orleans police alongside Phobos after a rooftop brawl with Shaman; the show's own commentary treats this as an elimination only tentatively ("I guess they must be" — Tracer Bullet)
arrested alongside Deimos, see above
flees New Orleans police alongside The Magician using a smoke bomb after a rooftop confrontation with Havoc; never seen again on-page, treated in-story as effectively out
flees alongside Shaman, see above
knocks himself out with a botched swan-dive headbutt into a dumpster after Van Dorn rolls clear; Van Dorn fetches a real referee to make the count
pinned by the masked "War" inside a bar; the bar's own barman makes the count in the absence of a referee
KravenBomb through a shop window
thrown from a rooftop mid-submission-hold, Van Dorn riding him down and off before the landing; unmasked on-page as James Thornhill in the aftermath
speared off a moving motorcycle by Van Dorn on another motorcycle, both crashing through a shop window

ruled eliminated alongside Venny LeTrav for their own safety, verbatim by the referee ("we have decided to eliminate both men from this match"), after a wharf collapses under Bullet's own finisher and drops both men into the water
eliminated alongside Tracer Bullet, see above
Kravenbombed roughly eighty feet from a warehouse gantry into an oyster pool

matches.note: A scattered, no-ring, city-wide battle royal across New Orleans (the fourth show billed under this name in the held record) — winner earns the WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot at Independence Day Rumble against Craven Moore, who appears throughout as a spectator (dinner with Vik Ventressa, a brief brawl when Kraven crashes it) but is never himself an entrant. Jackson Kraven survives as the lone entrant standing, pinning Eddie Van Dorn last after Van Dorn offers him the win outright (wanting to save his own spot for the Rumble instead). All 17 entrants named on-page are accounted for above (16 eliminations + the winner), matching the pre-match commentary's own count exactly. The WWA ran an annual "Bourbon Street Brawl" (2001–2004 in the held record): wwa-2001-06-25's own winner is Craven Moore, this show's (2002) is Jackson Kraven — two different years, two different winners, both correctly on file; no conflation in the registry itself, only in coordination paperwork upstream of this lane, now corrected.

name: Meltdown - July 1st 2002 - The Bourbon Street Brawl!

matches.note: WWA Rookie Championship. Barrett Sinclair defeats champion Justin Bourne, clean pin.

matches.stipulation: No Holds Barred Last Man Standing Match

date.source: The card's own header and its live-from line both read Monday 9 December 2002; 12 December 2002 was a Thursday. SOURCES DISAGREE: the card was filed under 12 December 2002; the dateline settles the day and both readings are recorded.

matches.note: WWA Extreme Championship. Enigma pins champion Chance with a double underhook piledriver onto a chair for a clean title change (wwa-extreme-enigma-2002).

WWA Cruiserweight and WWA Extreme Championships, both on the line. Chance pins double champion Enigma with a frog splash through a table; with no clean way to award a single champion of either belt, the referee rules Chance and Zion joint champions of both (wwa-light-heavyweight-r009, wwa-extreme-chance-zion-2003).

WWA GenX Championship (newly created this show, when Commissioner Raine retires the Cruiserweight and Extreme titles and crowns Zion the inaugural champion). James Beam defeats Zion for the title with the Whiskey Sour, with an assist from a returning Showtime's botched top-rope splash landing on Zion instead of Beam.
Grunge wins by disqualification after Nicholas Adams runs in and attacks him; Joey K also interferes on both men earlier in the match.
Trapper runs in with a pipe attack on Deimos, but Deimos still recovers to pin Shrapnel clean.
Special Enforcer Jackson Kraven interferes throughout; Chance runs in and hits Denrol with the Fortune's Fool, allowing Ventressa to cover for the pin.

Number One Contenders match for a WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot at March Madness; interrupted with no bell when champion Ian Tense runs in and attacks both men with the title belt and a chair, leaving no formal finish.
WWA Fiesta portion. Keru no Akiro's WWA debut; wins by pinfall over Steven Rage (unminted) with the Roaring Elbow.

WWA Fiesta portion. Leviathan attacks Adams before the bell; Nicholas Adams wins by disqualification when Lockdown runs in with a trashcan, and The Cell continue a lengthy post-match beatdown until enforcers Keru no Akiro and Evan Motive (unminted) clear them out.
EWA/WWA crossover portion (EWA Pain Games). Jimmi Zion defeats Justin Bourne, billed EWA-side, with the Amplifier.

EWA Pain Games portion. The inaugural, seven-entrant Pain Games elimination match for the newly created WWA European Championship (El Spastico, Frantic, Jarod Crow, Dr. Dream, and The Psycho are all unminted EWA entrants alongside The Chuckster and Tommy Starr). The Chuckster is eliminated last, by pinfall, when The Psycho hits the Psychosis through a table to become the first WWA European Champion.
The Horsemen (Shaman/Fuel) defeat Keru no Akiro/Evan Motive (Motive unminted) with the Starving Sickness combination (Shaman's backbreaker into Fuel's top-rope legdrop).

WWA GenX Championship. Champion James Beam pins Showtime with a German Suplex, but a WWATron replay shows Showtime's shoulder was up before three; the referee reverses the decision and awards Showtime the title. Already reflected in wwa-extreme-r003.
myZery's WWA debut; wins by pinfall over Jason Andrews (unminted) with the Traumatic Cerebral Stress.

WWA Tag Team Championship. Champions Mal Somers/Dave Harley (Extreme Corporation) vs. The DeLucci Brothers (unminted); after The Cell and Nicholas Adams brawl their way into the match, Phobos and Deimos run in with baseball bats and the referee calls for the bell, ruled a no-contest on-page ("the ref has called this one as a no-contest").
se7en (unminted) defeats Venny LeTrav; Joey K interferes throughout (chair shot on LeTrav right after his Clockstopper connects, then revives the referee for se7en's count).

WWA Television Championship. Champion Grunge retains when the masked Imperceptus (unminted) runs in, suplexes Joey K, and arranges Joey's arm over Grunge for the pin; Imperceptus then approaches Grunge's wife Julie (unminted) backstage and whispers something to her.

Billed as a four-way tag match (X-Corp/The DeLucci Brothers [unminted]/The Cell/Havoc) for the WWA Tag Team Championship, but The Cell (Leviathan/Lockdown) cut a promo and walk out without wrestling, leaving a three-way brawl. Havoc wins when Deimos pins Mal Somers with the Panic Attack, helped by Tiffani Andrews (unminted) pepper-spraying Tony DeLucci earlier in the match.
Billed as an "I Quit" match, but Tracer Bullet wins by pinfall (Pounding the Pavement) rather than a submission call.

WWA World Heavyweight Championship. Kash has champion Ian Tense pinned (the referee's count is broken mid-"three") when Lockdown blasts Kash from behind with a hammer; the referee calls for the bell immediately with no winner announced, and Ian -- now aligned with The Cell -- keeps hammering the bloodied Kash until security intervenes. No title change; Ian Tense's reign continues.
Best-2-out-of-3-falls. Shaman defeats Evan Motive (unminted) 2 falls to 1.

Second half of a Japanese Stipulation Challenge between the two (must pin the opponent, then climb out of the lowered cage). Akiro pins Fuel with the Roaring Elbow and is first out of the cage after both men fall from the top simultaneously.

eliminations.note: Pinned with the BeamSault (asai moonsault).
Pinned with the Whiskey Sour (shooting star press).
Pinned with the Somers-Assault (top-rope somersault legdrop).
Pinned with the Lawbreaker.
Pinned with a top-rope 450 splash.
Pinned with the Cradle Piledriver.
Pinned with the Clockstopper.
Submitted to The Claw.
Removed from the match for medical reasons after Leviathan sent him into the front row off a botched springboard attempt.
Pinned with the Depth Charge.
Pinned after an illegal Lockdown ankle-grab.
Pinned with a schoolboy, staggered first by his own teammate Grunge's kick.
Eliminated together with Lockdown by referee's decision after both brawled outside the ring.
Eliminated together with Dave Harley by referee's decision after both brawled outside the ring.
Pinned with the Vertebreaker, distracted first by a Shaman appearance on the WWATron.
Referee stopped the match on a Sharpshooter after LeTrav's knee gave out; the match's final fall.

matches.note: Main event: a billed 20-man elimination tag reduced to 18 after Steven Rage and Jason Andrews (both unminted) are found beaten unconscious backstage before the match and withdrawn; full elimination order recorded in eliminations[]. The DeLucci Brothers, Se7en, and Primetime Jonny Bedford remain unminted.
se7en (unminted) defeats James Curzon with a springboard-into-pin finisher ("Nevermore").

Tag match: Shaman/James Beam vs. Justin Bourne/Jimmi Zion. Zion pins Beam with a top-rope splash ("The Supernova"); Shaman, who spent the match sabotaging his own partner (slapping Beam instead of tagging him at one point), then chair-shots both Zion and Bourne after the bell.

A 4-on-4 tag brawl, X-Corp (Mal Somers/Dave Harley) and the DeLucci Brothers (unminted) vs. The Cell and Havoc. Both DeLuccis are eliminated by pinfall (Phobos pins Tommy, then Tony) before Dave Harley is disqualified for using a chair on Phobos, ending the match; Havoc continues a chair-assisted beatdown on Mal Somers afterward, aided by an interfering Chance.

A lumberjack match (the University of Oklahoma football team) with a folding chair placed in each corner as the only permitted weapon. Grunge retains the WWA Television Championship, hitting the Lawbreaker onto a chair for the pin. Nicholas Adams attacks Grunge with a mic shot and chokeslam after the bell, and is beaten down in turn by Youth United (Eddie Van Dorn, Imperceptus, and OU quarterback Jason White).

Tracer Bullet and Kash defeat Jackson Kraven and champion Ian Tense (not a title match) when Kash blinds Kraven with mist, causing Kraven to accidentally flatten his own partner Tense with the No More Tomorrows; Kash locks on the Kashmission for the academic pin.

Debut three-way (Commissioner Raine announces elimination rules moments before the bell): Prometheus, Reverend Tweak, and Tommy Starr (both Prometheus and Tweak unminted). Tweak pins Prometheus with the Jabbing A Pin to eliminate him, but the Tweak-vs-Starr finish is left unresolved when Lockdown and Leviathan storm the ring, beat down both remaining men, and offer Starr membership in Devil's Own; Starr answers by chairing both downed opponents rather than the match reaching a bell.
WWA GenX Championship. myZery pins champion Showtime after a Larry Crosier count-out ruling is waved off when both men re-enter the ring; already reflected in wwa-extreme-r004.
Keru no Akiro defeats Fuel with a small package after both men kick out of a string of near-falls.
WWA Television Championship. Grunge retains over James Beam with the Lawbreaker; already reflected in wwa-television-r057.
Jimmi Zion pins Shaman with an Entrapment DDT, reversing a Desert Spike attempt, despite a salt-to-the-eyes cheap shot earlier in the match.

Venny LeTrav vs. Se7en (unminted). Both men brawl to a double count-out when the referee's ten-count runs out on both men outside the ring, then continue fighting through the break with a lead pipe and a baseball bat; both are written off to hospital treatment, Venny with a possibly-broken rib. Served declaring line (Jimmy Rose, on return from commercial): "Venny LeTrav and Se7en just had a match end in double disqualification." No winner declared either way; logged "draw" per this campaign's own double-technicality-finish convention (wwa-2003-05-26's own served double count-out, logged the same way).

Triple threat between three tag-title contenders' own representatives -- Leviathan (The Cell), Phobos (Havoc), and Tommy DeLucci (DeLucci Brothers, unminted) -- with the champion X-Corp (Dave Harley) interfering live before the bell. Leviathan pins Tommy DeLucci with the Trashdriver, aided by a Lockdown-assisted trashcan shot.

Joey K rolls Chance up with a handful of tights for the pin, despite Dave Harley twice breaking up Joey's own offense -- Chance and Harley's own feud over X-Corp's tag-title standing undercuts their teamwork throughout.

Kash submits Tracer Bullet with the Kashmission after Devil's Own (Lockdown, Leviathan, Ian Tense) interferes at ringside; Kash superkicks an interfering Ian Tense by accident on his way to the finish.

date.source: SOURCES DISAGREE: the card's own live-from line reads "Sunday, May 25th 2003", while the fed's own news post dated 24 May 2003 says the transcript is already online. Filed under 24 May 2003; both readings are recorded.

matches.note: Last Man Standing vs. Prometheus (unminted). Neither man answers referee Larry Crosier's standing ten-count after a simultaneous knockout. Served declaring line (Brooke Prescott): "Due to the fact that neither man was able to answer the standing ten count, the match is ruled a double knockout, the result is a DRAW."

A 2-on-1 grudge handicap match (Showtime and James Curzon's own revenge for myZery's GenX title win one week earlier), enforcer K2 (unminted) interfering repeatedly at ringside. myZery pins Showtime with a Ganzo Bomb after Curzon is left unable to continue.

Billed a Last Man Standing match against Reverend Tweak (unminted), resolved instead by a straight three-count -- an internal inconsistency in the fed's own text, not corrected here. Tommy Starr spears Tweak into the ringside barrier for the pin, aided by a distracting Leviathan.

No-disqualification. Shaman pins Zion (fall 1); Zion makes Shaman submit to a leg-lock worked on a bed of tacks and nails (fall 2); Shaman pins Zion with a barbed-wire-wrapped 2x4 shot to Zion's braced knee (fall 3, deciding). Post-match, Shaman abducts the unconscious Zion in a box truck and crashes it into a parked car in the arena lot.

Shaman/Se7en (Se7en unminted) vs. Jimmi Zion/Venny LeTrav. The referee's ten-count runs out on both corners at ringside while all four men brawl outside; the served text explicitly rules it a double count-out. Se7en attacks LeTrav again backstage after the bell, leaving him unconscious amid a smashed table.

WWA Television Championship. With the referee down from an earlier blow, Nick Adams runs in and chokeslams champion Grunge with the Contract Breaker, then drags the dazed Joey K's hand onto Grunge's chest for an illegitimate pin the revived referee counts anyway; already reflected in wwa-television-r058.

Three-way debut match. "The Psycho" Steven Murphy (the fed's own first-ever EWA European Champion) defeats Christopher Vice and Tony Caesar (both unminted) with back-to-back Psychosis slams, pinning Vice.
Jimmi Zion defeats Se7en (unminted) after Se7en breaks free of two straight submission holds; both men trade cheap shots afterward before Zion gets the pin.

WWA Television Championship. Champion Joey K deliberately gets himself counted out for a belt shot to Mal Somers rather than risk the pin, saving his own reign by disqualification; Somers wins the bout but the title stays with Joey K.

#1 contender's match for the WWA GenX Championship. Billed as a three-way with Prometheus, but Prometheus's entrance is scrapped live on-air and the bout goes on as a straight one-on-one; Reverend Tweak (unminted) defeats Fuel with a Shooting Star Press.

Three-way with Devil's Own stablemates Ian Tense and Leviathan interfering at ringside throughout. Zion rolls up Venny LeTrav with a small package for the pin while Lockdown is tied up in the ropes from an earlier double-team spot; Devil's Own beats down LeTrav after the bell, leaving him unconscious.

Shaman serves as special guest referee for this hardcore points match (a foreign-object shot scores one point, a table spot scores five, first past sixteen with a two-point lead wins). Leviathan wins 19-11 with a Hellenic Slam through a table.

Fatal four-way, rebilled a "four way singles tag" live on-air by Terry Valentine on the owner's own orders. Adams, Grunge, and Harley briefly team up to triple-team Enigma, but Enigma escapes and rolls Harley up using the ropes for leverage to steal the pin.

The returning Wes Sanders' own singles feud with Chance never reaches a bell -- the Forsaken Souls (Enigma, Joey K, Se7en) run in and drag Sanders into a four-on-one beatdown of Chance, closing the show with Chance bloodied and taken out by medics.
For the rights to Reverend Tweak's (unminted) own bible. Tommy Starr wins with a Shooting Starr Press.

WWA GenX Championship. myZery is attacked backstage before his own entrance and thrown out unconscious; Shaman is a two-count from pinning him when Devil's Own's own explosive warning pyro interrupts, revealing "The Psycho" Steven Murphy as the backstage attacker. Lockdown then beats Shaman down with a chair (using Murphy as a decoy), has Murphy drag myZery up, batters him unconscious as well, and simply takes the GenX title belt from the timekeeper, declaring himself champion outright -- no bell ever rings to a finish, no reigns.json change follows (myZery's own reign, r004, already correctly runs uncontested through this date).

Joey K squashes myZery with the Making Way (Uranage) for a clean pinfall. Dave Harley, disguised as a Spanish-announce-table announcer, steals Joey K's own WWA Television Championship belt after the bell and ambushes him with a Harley Bomb onto it.

Reverend Tweak (unminted) pins Enigma with an assist from an interfering Chance (a springboard chairshot, then a chair-assisted Fortune's Fool) after Enigma twice accidentally levels the referee. Enigma challenges Chance to a one-on-one blowoff at Independence Day Rumble afterward.

The Cell wins by referee stoppage when Nick Adams is left unable to continue; the rest of Devil's Own (Tommy Starr, Imperceptus, "The Psycho" Steven Murphy) run in afterward and fold a steel chair around Grunge's own head and throat with a boot-assisted stomp.

Handicap match: Wes Sanders and Se7en (unminted) vs. Chance alone after Mal Somers is held up backstage. Dave Harley and a late-arriving Mal Somers even the odds outside the ring; Chance rolls up Se7en for the pin (Se7en was not the legal man, an acknowledged fed-own mistake left uncorrected in the served text).

eliminations.note: Powerbomb into a chokeslam (the "56 Special") onto the pavement -- the first fall.
Busted open with a whiskey bottle behind a bar, then pinned with the NewSplash.
Beaten down by Devil's Own (Leviathan, Lockdown, "The Psycho" Steven Murphy) after rolling into their own Hummer inside a trash can; Lockdown's tire iron sets up Starr's own pin.
Thrown through an ice cream-shop window and pinned there.
Full-nelson face-first slam to the road, after Jimmi Zion had already softened him up in an unrelated beatdown earlier.
Tossed into a nightclub and finished with the Supernova off a DJ booth.
Harley Bombed mid-song during an impromptu X-Corp karaoke bit ("YMCA").
Harley Bomb onto a parked car's own hood, with a Mal Somers assist.
A 900 splash off a third-floor balcony, landing on Starr and Reverend Tweak together after both men had already fallen off a second-floor balcony fighting The Chuckster.
Simultaneous cover with the Tommy Starr elimination above, both pinned in the same three-count by referee Rick Kilgore.
Lassoed to the roof of X-Corp's own modified Extreme-Mobile and dragged into its own rear end when Somers slams the brakes.
The Drill, after Wattsoner attacks Devil's Own alone with a baseball bat.
A moonsault off a fallen TV stand through a pool table inside a bar, after Chance opens him up with a thrown tequila bottle and rubs salt in the cut.
A car-hood-surfing moonsault followed by the Mexican Stretch Bomb.
Eliminated by his own tag partner -- a "rock-paper-scissors" bit that Harley loses, then gets pinned off the result.
Pinned under a couch shoved on top of him inside a furniture store, after surviving an Amplifier (Vertebreaker) and a Gravity Kills.
Zion's own NewSplash off a bar roof onto Leviathan doubles as his own undoing -- Chance follows with a Fortune's Fool onto both men and covers them simultaneously with Leviathan below.
Simultaneous cover with the Jimmi Zion elimination above (see that entry) -- both counted by referee Gary Jones in the same moment.

The match's final fall: after a coin-flip truce turns into a double-cross and a two-story backdrop to the street, Chance closes the show with an 1170-degree splash off a second-floor balcony into a dumpster.

matches.note: The second Bourbon Street Brawl, a scattered #1-contendership brawl across the French Quarter for a shot at Kash's own WWA World Heavyweight Championship at Independence Day Rumble. A 20-man field (Ian Tense scratched, replaced by Mr. Cool; Enigma, previewed a week earlier, never appears). Full order of falls recorded in eliminations[]. Chance outlasts all nineteen others, closing the show with a 1170-degree splash off a second-floor balcony onto Eddie Van Dorn (who had spent much of the match's own closing stretch disguised as an elderly bystander) inside a dumpster.

Se7en (unminted) never answers referee Larry Crosier's outside-the-ring ten count after Zion's Supernatural Stretch submission hold forces him to roll out of the ring rather than tap; Zion is awarded the win by countout.

Fall one of a two-fall contest, for the WWA Television Championship. Lockdown rolls up Harley with a small package for the pin, immediately after a distracting WWATron "K Moments" segment from Joey K costs Harley the cover. New TV Champion (corroborates the already-linked wwa-television-r060).

Fall two of the same two-fall contest, for the WWA GenX Championship, immediately following fall one above. Harley runs Lockdown through a crate of beer bottles propped on an exposed turnbuckle with a Running Harley Bomb for the pin. New GenX Champion (corroborates the already-linked wwa-extreme-r006).

Damian Thorne's in-ring return, against Rev. Tweak (unminted), who attacks him before his entrance finishes and gets the better of the early exchanges. Thorne recovers and finishes with the Career Killer (a sit-out powerbomb) for the pin.

Handicap match, Somers (X-Corp) alone against Wes Sanders and Enigma (Forsaken Souls). Ruled a legal weapon by the ring announcer since it's his own tag-title belt, Somers strips off his shirt to reveal the WWA Rookie Championship (which he addresses by name, "Rookie") strapped to his body, and levels both opponents with it at once for a double pin. Sanders and Enigma beat Somers down after the bell.

Main event, non-title. Kash and Tracer Bullet (partners for the night, having faced each other days earlier) vs. Nicholas Adams and Chance. Tracer abandons the match mid-way to chase the masked ninja who stole Kash's World Heavyweight Championship, leaving Kash to work the finish alone -- he reverses a Chance pin attempt for the win.

Fiesta's own in-ring debut for both EWA graduates. Keith knocks the referee out with a chair (aimed at Knight), then pins Knight with a foot on the ropes and a fistful of tights once the ref recovers.

Both men brawl past the bell and strike multiple referees trying to separate them; the match is thrown out. Served declaring line (Chase): "Looks like a double DQ here." The brawl continues after the bell -- Fuel runs in to help clear the ring, offering Akiro a place in CPE alongside himself and Zion, before Enigma ambushes and beats down Zion in a separate post-match angle.

WWA GenX Championship. Guest referee Joey K repeatedly refuses to count Harley's pins; after Harley puts Curzon through a table with a Harley Bomb, Fate runs in, chairs Joey K, and makes the count herself. Harley retains (corroborates the already-linked wwa-extreme-r006).
Somers and Chance win by disqualification after Wes Sanders frog-splashes the WWA Rookie Championship belt (which Somers wears strapped to his body and calls "Rookie") onto Somers's face.

EWA Graduate elimination submission match (no pinfalls). The Chuckster has Steven Murphy tapping to a figure-4 when Devil's Own (Imperceptus, Lockdown) runs in with Leviathan; ring announcer Gary Trudeau rules it a disqualification for all three men. The brawl continues after the bell -- CPE (David Wattsoner, Shaman) makes the save, and Murphy ultimately drops the Chuckster's head-first onto the exposed concrete floor with Psychosis.
Van Dorn pins Shaman with the Dropout. Tracer Bullet attacks and abducts Van Dorn immediately after, treating him as a suspect in the World Title theft.

WWA Television Championship. Wattsoner pins Lockdown with a spinning fireman's carry piledriver (Pure Agony) using Lockdown's own confiscated brass knuckles. New champion (corroborates the already-linked wwa-television-r061).

Main event, Kash as special guest referee. Fate, trying to hit Thorne with a chair, accidentally beer-blinds Kash first; Kash still calls for the bell against Grunge and Adams's corner once Fate connects with Thorne, ruling it a disqualification for the interference.
First round. Zion pins American Eagle with the Supernova (a reverse Shooting Star Press) after choking him with an entrance cable.

First round. American Eagle (eliminated earlier by Akiro's own interference) runs in, knocks out the referee, and counts the pin himself in a stolen referee shirt -- the served text itself questions the legitimacy ("Is that legal?") -- but the decision is announced for LeTrav and stands on-page. Akiro and Eagle then brawl to a backstage stalemate afterward, unrelated to the match result itself.
First round. Chivo Sanders' own late chair interference (aimed at Keith) is short-lived; Wes Sanders pins Keith clean with a spinning back kick (AKB) after the ref recovers.

PTC Tag Team Championship (a cross-promotion title defended on this WWA card). Homo/Phobic (the Bum Boozler and Shane Stone) retain over challengers X-Corp (Dave Harley and Mal Somers) -- Somers submits.

The Chuckster, still hobbled from Psycho's Psychosis two weeks earlier, schoolboys a stunned Van Dorn for the pin. Van Dorn announces afterward that the loss is humiliating enough to send him training in Japan.

Lockdown is a late scratch (personal leave), replaced by Liam Jenson on the fed's own booker President Warr's arrangement -- the pin, had either side gotten it, would have earned a WWA Television Championship shot at Labor Day Brawl. Jenson carries Starr out mid-match rather than finish; the referee counts all four men out. Served declaring line (Gary Trudeau): "it's referee Tad Simmons decision that this match is a double-countout and a no-contest."

Winner picks the stipulation for the two men's own Labor Day Brawl match. Leviathan has Grunge nearly out on his feet from a Crippler Crossface (aided by an Imperceptus-smuggled illegal chair shot), then deliberately releases the hold and has the referee count himself out rather than finish the pin -- "Now referee, count me out" -- content that he'll beat Grunge under his own chosen rules regardless.
Main event. Adams turns Thorne's own chair against him twice (including a mid-air dropkick off the top rope) before pinning him clean with a top-rope leg drop (the Enhancer).
First round. Somers pins Curzon with a screwdriver tombstone off the top rope, after Curzon briefly turns Somers's own tag-title belt "Rookie" into a weapon against him.
First round. Mal Somers, feuding with Sanders, slides Rookie into the ring for LeTrav's own Somers-Assault-style leg drop; Somers then lays LeTrav across the downed Sanders for the pin himself.

First round. Fuel makes Knight submit to Fire on High (an STF variant) after a chair shot, apparently connected to Matt Keith's own earlier backstage confrontation with Knight, leaves Knight unable to respond to the hold.

Second round. Enigma runs in, chair-shots Chance, and Zion covers for the pin -- Enigma then turns on Zion immediately afterward with a Fall From Grace, unrelated to the match's own already-decided result.

WWA GenX Championship, Harley defending alone in a 2-on-1 handicap match against Forsaken Souls. A brief arena blackout leaves Enigma busted open inside a pentagram drawn in blood, Joey K standing over him with a bloodied bat and no memory of swinging it; Harley covers Enigma for the retention while Joey stands stunned.

During a mid-match arena blackout, an unseen attacker chair-shots Knight bloody while both men lie down; Akiro pins him after, denying any knowledge of the attack. A second, identical blackout attack lands on Matt Keith later the same night (order 2 below) -- both parties spend the rest of the show accusing each other.
Another mid-match arena blackout leaves Keith chair-shot and bloodied; Chance covers for the pin once the lights return, professing no knowledge of the attack himself.
Semifinal. LeTrav pins Zion clean with the Vennysault (a springboard-to-top-rope splash) and advances to face Enigma in the final.

WWA GenX Championship. Harley's mystery opponent, revealed as Matt Keith's own previously-masked "Flunky," is unmasked as JC Swinger (unminted). Harley retains with a Harley Bomb (jackknife powerbomb) onto a steel chair, after tasering Keith with a remote-control toy to remove his ringside interference.

Semifinal. Wes Sanders runs in to break up a clean Somers pin (aided by a knocked-out referee reviving just in time), and X-Corp brawls with Sanders at ringside in response; Enigma recovers and makes Somers pass out in a Dragon Sleeper for the win, advancing to face Venny LeTrav in the final.
Akiro makes Zion pass out in a leg-scissored carotid submission (a version of the Katahajime), Zion's third straight loss.

The Sanders family feud match set up the prior Fiesta, against Wes's brother Chivo Sanders (unminted). Mal Somers runs in anyway (permitted under the no-DQ stipulation) trying to help Chivo; Wes escapes a Chivo powerbomb attempt and pins him with an X-Factor onto Rookie.

WWA Extreme Championship (billed in-fiction as the GenX Title). A fully comedic giant-monster-movie parody segment -- Harley ("Dave Kong"), LeTrav ("Venzilla"), and Curzon ("Bonafried", in a chicken costume with Dead Rabbit as his own second) race across a miniature Tokyo to claim the belt from the top of a collapsing Tokyo Tower. LeTrav grabs it first after tearing free of Curzon's grip, becoming the new champion; see wwa-extreme-r007.
Semifinal. Enigma makes Fuel submit to a Dragon Sleeper (Hypnotic Conundrum), advancing to face the new champion Venny LeTrav in the tournament final.
WWA Television Championship. New champion: Murphy hits Psychosis (a torture-rack Dreamer Driver) after Leviathan and President Warr's ringside distraction, and Warr signals for a fast three-count.

Ends in a double disqualification -- both men Con-Chair-To the referee simultaneously trying to hit each other, and the bell is called for their safety. Served declaring line (Gary Trudeau): "the referee has ruled this bout...A DOUBLE DISQUALIFICATION!!" No winner; the feud continues unresolved.

eliminations.note: Leviathan hits the Poseidon Adventure (standing powerbomb over the top rope); Grunge makes the cover. Eliminates Jenson's team (partner Nicholas Adams never entered).
Grunge hits a T-Bone Suplex and Leviathan follows with a top-rope Frog Splash for a combined three-count; the served text does not disambiguate which man's pin actually counted for which opponent.
Same combined Grunge/Leviathan sequence as the-chuckster's elimination above.

matches.note: SCHEMA DATA POINT -- a genuinely novel shape, recorded as the closest honest fit rather than forced: 'One ring, two cages, four teams, eight men, one pool of beer, one prize' (a Birthday Bash spot). Two side-by-side rings, each in its own cage, joined at a shared beer pool; four 2-man teams enter on a timer (not team-by-team -- individuals alternate in), and a team is eliminated only when BOTH its members are gone. Team pairings per the served text: Grunge & Leviathan; Liam Jenson & Nicholas Adams; Desolation & The Chuckster; Shaman & Tommy Starr. `sides` was rejected for this row because the final two entrants (Leviathan and Grunge) are on the SAME team and the match resolves with Leviathan turning on his own partner -- no `winner_side` value could honestly represent a teammate-on-teammate finish, so `participants`+`winner`+`eliminations[]` was used instead, same escape hatch as an un-sided battle royal. Shaman and Tommy Starr never actually enter the match (see eliminations[] is silent on them by design, per the same 20-man-elimination-tag precedent of omitting withdrawn-before-entry names from participants): Starr forfeits live via an arm injury he cites on the mic, and Shaman is attacked backstage with a hammer and a chair by Khaled (unminted -- er, khaled-wwa) before he can enter; the match is ruled a team elimination for both. Nicholas Adams similarly never enters -- he appears via satellite to bail on his partner Liam Jenson, citing a medical hold -- so only Jenson (who did enter and wrestle) gets an eliminations[] row for that team.
GAROU's WWA debut. Wins with the Wolf Special #2 (a top-rope rana).
Shaman pins Desolation with the Desert Spike (a standing piledriver), despite interference from Desolation's own second Agony (unminted).
matches.stipulation: Round Robin (leg 1 of 3), WWA Television Championship #1 contendership

matches.note: The referee disqualifies both men on sight, before the bell even rings, for brawling backstage through two dumpsters and arriving covered in garbage. Desolation then beats up the referee and Chuckster puts on the ref's shirt to "officiate" an impromptu unsanctioned scrap between Desolation and the actual referee; no bearing on the round robin standings beyond the half-point each side already banked from the no-contest.
matches.stipulation: Round Robin (leg 2 of 3), WWA Television Championship #1 contendership

matches.note: Shaman wins by count-out -- Chuckster is still in the shower recovering from the prior leg's dumpster brawl and doesn't reach the ring in time. Shaman wins the round robin outright (1 win, 1 no-contest) and becomes the new #1 contender for the WWA Television Championship.
matches.stipulation: Round Robin (leg 3 of 3), WWA Television Championship #1 contendership

matches.note: WWA Television Champion Murphy defends nothing here -- explicitly a non-title bout despite the champion's own involvement. Tommy Starr, ostensibly Murphy's ally after helping him beat Leviathan, turns on him mid-match with a pole shot pulled from his own cast, letting Jenson pin Murphy at ringside. Murphy gets a measure of revenge on Starr with the Psychosis moments later, then brawls with a returning Jenson to the back.

SCHEMA DATA POINT: winner_side genuinely unresolved, not a parse gap -- per SCHEMA.md's own honesty-bucket doctrine (sides present, no winner_side parsed = 'unresolved'), used here because the served text itself declares a mutual double-pinfall, not because the finish wasn't read closely enough. Leviathan reverses a Grunge rollup into a dragon suplex; both men land awkwardly across chairs scattered in the ring and the referee counts a simultaneous three-count on both shoulders. Gary Trudeau's own call: "Your winner, as result of a double pin...Leviathan AND Grunge!!" Per the match's own stipulation this means BOTH sides' partners qualify for the Birthday Bash -- Damian Thorne (Leviathan's partner) and Tracer Bullet (Grunge's partner) are both explicitly confirmed through to the PPV main event in the same line, even though Thorne and Tracer spend the finish itself brawling up the ramp, oblivious to their own mutual qualification.
matches.stipulation: the winning side's OWN partner earns a WWA Birthday Bash slot

eliminations.note: Crucifix DDT; Shaman landed on top of the already-down Fuel, both pinned in the same simultaneous three-count.
Pinned simultaneously with Shaman in the same three-count (Chuckster's Crucifix DDT).
450 splash.
A three-quarter facelock/cutter-style move on the asylum's own roof, in the rain; the broadcast declines to name the move directly ("we can't call it that").
Electrocuted with the exposed wiring of a TV set Hunter had already smashed over him.
Uppercut, after Chance was chained up and beaten down (Psycho's own "Greetings from Liverpool" combo).
Depth Charge; Harley's own feet draped over the already-down Mal Somers, covering both men in the same pinfall.
Pinned simultaneously with Harley in the same pinfall (see above).
A leg-sweep counter sent Hunter to the concrete; GAROU fell on top for the pin.
Billed as "The Inmate" at this point in the match — not yet unmasked.
Elevated powerbomb onto a broken bench; "The Inmate" not yet unmasked.
Three-quarter facelock drop in the asylum's own former chapel, after a spear through a wooden cross Leviathan had been tied to.

matches.note: A 12-man, two-locked-group gauntlet plus three "wildcard" entrants, staged inside a disused asylum (no venue/city named — the broadcast itself frames the location as deliberately undisclosed). The final two, Thanatos and "The Inmate," unmask in the closing moments: The Inmate is revealed as the already-registered jackson-kraven (a surprise return, used as his match id throughout above), and Thanatos declares himself Deimos (the already-registered, separately-established deimos) — flagged, not merged; thanatos-wwa is kept as the acting id throughout since he already carries his own separate appearances elsewhere in the held record (see the handoff note). The third wildcard, "Todd Hunter," is never confirmed as any known character — commentary floats three guesses (Randy Cross, Darken, Showtime), none corroborated in the text; recorded as a verbatim label. The match itself never resolves: the last fall is a mutual double pin (both men's shoulders held down at the same three-count) that the broadcast itself questions ("Who won? ... Double pin?") and never answers — Damian Thorne runs in with a lead pipe before a winner is named, beats down both remaining men, and the broadcast cuts away. No winner recorded; genuinely unresolved per the served text, not a parse gap.

eliminations.note: Baited into charging with a mocking "L" gesture; GAROU ducked and pulled the top rope down, sending Desolation over.
Springboard hurricanrana (billed as GAROU's "Wolf Special #2").

The same masked, balaclava-wearing assailant who attacked Polaris backstage before the match pulled the top rope down as Jenson pushed him over — the assailant's identity is never confirmed in the text.
A standing side kick sent GAROU's ribs into the ringside barrier.
Chokeslammed over the top rope to the floor (Jenson's own "Drunk and Disorderly").

matches.note: Winner picks his own opponent and stipulation for Birthday Bash; Jenson chose The Mysterious GAROU in a Texas Dog Collar match with Tommy Starr (ringside for this battle royal, never a competitor in it) as special guest referee.

WWA Television Championship, Psycho (champion) defending against Shaman. Both men brawled to a double countout outside the ring; the referee then additionally ruled the finish a double disqualification, and both men turned on him for it. No title change — same double-technicality-finish convention as wwa-2003-05-26 and wwa-2003-10-13.

Leviathan struck a second referee with a chair after Tracer Bullet had already forced two officials out of the match; Tracer Bullet won by disqualification. Leviathan cut a post-match promo declaring he'd chosen to DQ himself on purpose, saving himself for Grunge at Birthday Bash.

Grunge enters as reigning WWA United States Champion (and is introduced as such) but the match itself is never billed for the title, and no reigns.json change follows — consistent with the existing ledger, which has Grunge's own reign (r033) continuing to Birthday Bash, where it changes hands by a different mechanism entirely (Leviathan pinning TV champion Brad Polaris, per r034's own "how" text). Thorne wins clean with a sitout cradle powerbomb ("Hand of God") after a distraction from a returning Tracer Bullet backfired on Grunge; post-match, Thorne reveals a live shot of Tracer Bullet's own house swarmed by emergency services.

A whole-roster parking-lot brawl for four Birthday Bash contracts, hung above a bolted-in ladder; Kash (the reigning WWA World Heavyweight Champion) and interim Commissioner Bridge (unminted) guard the ring as enforcers rather than competing for a contract themselves. No clean elimination sequence — the brawl is scattered across the parking lot and backstage with no formal falls, so no eliminations[] is recorded. Four winners, each claiming one contract: Enigma (with an eight-man distraction army, unminted), Bonafide/James Curzon (disguised as a referee), Chance (boosted up by his own tag partner Dave Harley, who never grabs one himself), and Matt Keith (last man standing after every other remaining brawler was tied up). Retro-applied per CURATION v59's own winners[]/losers[] doctrine (plural outcomes, used only where a single winner/winner_side genuinely can't derive the result) -- the four winners above each grabbed a contract independently, an outcome the fed's own broadcast declared explicitly ("the four men going to Birthday Brawl are Enigma, James Curzon, Chance and Matt Keith"); the prose account above is unchanged.

A brutal, near-hardcore brawl (chairs, a lead pipe, a monkey wrench, gasoline never lit) that Keith's own gimmick named. Pinned Knight clean with the Tooth Fairy Super Kick, then had his own valet's boyfriend JC Swinger hoist Knight (chained to Keith's own fan-poster prop) into the air and drop him from the rafters after the bell — a post-match angle, not part of the match's own result.
WWA GenX Championship; LeTrav (champion) retains, rolling Bonafide up after Bonafide's own moonsault (attempted with the belt strapped on) missed entirely.

Dave Harley, forced to team with his own real-life rival Enigma, turned on his own partner mid-match with a springboard bulldog; Mal Somers pinned Enigma with the Mal-Function moments later. Kash's WWA World Heavyweight Championship was not at stake (a tag match, not a singles title defense).

name: Countdown To Birthday Bash
notes: A "Countdown to Birthday Bash" hype/highlight special -- interviews, a press-conference wildcard reveal (The Masked Canuck), an X Corp recruitment vignette (Venny LeTrav), and a Commissioner phone-in, with no fresh live in-ring matches of its own. The show also replays three archival clips as "classic Birthday Bash moments" (a 2000 Nelson/TJ Donaldson finish, the 2001 Ventressa/LeBeaux Tron finish, and an approx. 2002 Tracer Bullet-loses-to-Ian-Tense World Title change) -- evidence for those original shows, not structured here per this lane's fresh-vs-archival rule.

matches.note: WWA Television Championship. Polaris's own Birthday Brawl win was briefly ruled nullified by Meltdown booker President Warr on a jurisdiction technicality, then restored by newly-company-wide Commissioner Bridge before this match was even signed -- so the belt was legitimately on the line throughout. Adams reversed a Polaris frog splash into a pin for his own third TV Title reign (already correctly on file, wwa-television-r064, linked to this show's own event).
A bizarre finish: Desolation, having lost a silent staring contest and a crowd-participation clapping bit to GAROU, breaks down sobbing mid-ring and sits down; GAROU pins him for the win.

The first of a new weekly round-robin (Psycho, Khaled, Liam Jenson, and The Chuckster, announced earlier this show) whose leader by Rage in the Cage earns a guaranteed TV title shot. Khaled won with a mobile-phone shot to the head, a Stun Gun facebuster, and a fistful of tights.

Second TV Title League match. Tommy Starr (ringside, never a competitor) planted a foreign object in Jenson's boot mid-match; Jenson knocked Chuckster out with it and finished him with a half crab submission.

Tag-style rules (two men legal at a time, tag to any of the other three). Billed as "The Masked Canuck," a debuting masked Canadian gimmick the broadcast repeatedly almost-names before catching itself ("Denr... The Canadian wonder") -- the same corroborated-by-context standard already used for Trent LeBeaux/tracer-bullet; recorded under his own established id. Grunge (never a formal entrant, sitting out the match by his own choice) and Damian Thorne (also never entered) both ran in during the closing stretch -- Thorne chair-shotting Wes Sanders and hitting a debuting, unminted masked ally of Grunge's (revealed as "Alec Jenson") with the Ganzo Bomb, before finishing Sanders with the Hand of God. With Sanders incapacitated, Tracer Bullet slid in and pinned him for the win.

An involuntary pairing on both sides: Chance and Matt Keith were just named the new WWA World Tag Team Champions earlier this same show (a title reactivation, already correctly on file as wwa-world-tag-team-r038, event-linked to this show -- their first sanctioned defense isn't until 16 Feb 2004, so no title implications here); Jimmi Zion had beaten his own partner Fuel unconscious backstage before the bell, declaring he'd go it alone, only for a bloodied Fuel to show up anyway and blind-tag himself onto Zion's side. Chance pinned Zion with a top-rope moonsault (Fortune's Fool) after Matt Keith had already softened him up with the Deadly Device -- Keith was furious the pin (and the win) went to Chance instead of him.

Somers won with a tombstone piledriver that drove Akiro's head into his own valet, Rookie (a puppet) -- Akiro sold it as a legitimate neck/spinal injury ("couldn't feel his legs"), EMTs stretchered him out.

Enigma won the first fall clean off SEAL's own interference (a neck-snap across the top rope setting up the Fall From Grace); Commissioner Bridge then ruled the finish tainted and ordered the match restarted rather than let the interference-won result stand. In the restart, Joey K reversed a second Fall From Grace attempt and won clean with his own finisher, "Making Way." Recorded as one match with the restart's own result standing.

A genuine WWA-native gimmick (Commissioner Bridge's own invention, a comedy brawl scored in pints of beer rather than falls) against Commissioner Jack "Bridge" Knight -- recurring across this campaign but never separately minted, so recorded here as participants: [dave-harley] only, per the standing single-unminted-opponent convention (sides[] requires resolved ids on both corners; participants is the correct shape when one side never clears the mint bar). Genuinely unresolved: both men get progressively drunker, dissolve into a karaoke duet mid-brawl, and the segment ends with Mal Somers attacking Harley before any bell, fall, or decision is ever made.

WWA GenX Championship, on a breakaway plywood ring rigged to collapse -- Bonafide (champion) retains. LeTrav was legitimately injured selling a fall through the collapsing ring structure (busted open, a suspected concussion per the broadcast's own closing update); Bonafide won clean with a 720-degree splash from the standing platform onto the fallen LeTrav below.

A leg of the ongoing "TV Title League" round robin (Jenson led with four points entering the match, Psycho trailed on three).
