House of Pain fractures immediately after: the Outlaw, Mr. Business and Todd Logan quit on camera to form the New Executive's Club; Cross sets a stipulation match (Outlaw and two Executive's Club members vs. Steele and two STB members) the following Wednesday to decide whether the Outlaw gets his own title shot.
matches.stipulation: Iron Man match, best-of-five-falls, one hour — winner earns a WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot against Randy Cross at the Labor Day PPV

matches.note: A brutal, cage-breaking brawl; Jack hits the "FamineSlam" but the referee is down to see it, and the Outlaw's own opportunistic run-in Outlaw-Kicks Jack before the cover can be made. Both men fail the referee's ten count — the broadcast's own text calls it a double knockout — and the title stays vacant. Post-match, Darken ambushes the celebrating Outlaw with the "Dark Pogostick" outside the ring.

name: WWA — 29 Aug 1998
notes: House of Pain fractures on-camera: the Outlaw, Mr. Business and Todd Logan quit to form the New Executive's Club after Randy Cross openly favors himself over the Outlaw's own failed title bid. Cross sets a stipulation for next Wednesday (Outlaw and two New Executive's Club members vs. Flynn Steele and two STB members) to determine whether the Outlaw earns a title shot. The main event's own WWA Television Championship stays vacant (per this session's own 15 Aug reign correction, vacated 17 Aug in a show outside the held record) after a double-knockout finish; the ledger's own tracked Logan win over Jack for the same vacant title is dated 6 Sep — read as the real deciding rematch at the Labor Day PPV, a show this session did not reach.

matches.note: Malkav Amaranth finishes Tony Vardell with the "Madness Driver."
New Star finishes Canuck with a chain of suplexes into the "Nova Bomb."

Anarchy repeatedly cuts the arena lights to move Chaos and Raiden into position; once the House of Pain and Commandant's Own reinforcements (Jak Lancer, Big Eliem, Major Havok) are all incapacitated at ringside, Chaos and Raiden attack both Crockett and Payne inside the ring itself, powerbombing each onto a steel chair. The referee rules an explicit double disqualification.

Flynn Steele leads STB to the ring but, per Randy Cross's own earlier stipulation, does not wrestle himself; Mantis, ChiKylin and Shane Warner represent STB instead. House of Pain (Randy Cross, the Minnesota Wrecking Crew) interferes at ringside, targeting Steele's own taped ribs and ChiKylin outside the ring; the Outlaw finishes Shane Warner with the Outlaw Kick, and Todd Logan covers for the pin. A brawl involving both House of Pain and the New Executive's Club spills to the floor before security intervenes.
matches.stipulation: The New Executive's Club vs. STB — winner earns the Outlaw a WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot, contingent on Randy Cross retaining at the Labor Day PPV

name: WWA — 2 Sep 1998
notes: New Star challenges Shaman to a Los Angeles street fight at the Labor Day PPV; David Wattsoner attacks New Star with a crowbar afterward and counter-challenges him to a "New York City street fight," a distinction the broadcast's own commentary admits it can't explain. Commentary confirms Anarchy (Chaos, Raiden, Havok) face both the Commandant's Own and House of Pain for the tag titles at the same PPV.

matches.note: Wattsoner (billed "Sniper" for his WWA debut) finishes Patriot with the "Ice Punch" for the pin.

Elixir fells the Fan with a purse from ringside before the bell, clearing the way for the match proper. Segier finishes the Black Scorpion with a submission he calls "the Twist" (a scissors headlock) for the tap-out.
Payne suplexes Mad Coil into a bridge while Mantis simultaneously hits the "Nutcracker" on him, then Mantis clotheslines the incoming Pepper for the pin.
matches.stipulation: TV Title Tournament first round — Lethal Lottery random-draw tag match

matches.note: Butler baits his own partner Big Eliem with an insult on the mic before the bell; Eliem later powerbombs and chokeslams Butler himself mid-match rather than tag in properly, and Bomber covers Butler for the pin. O'Hara sucker-attacks his own winning partner Bomber afterward.
matches.stipulation: TV Title Tournament first round — Lethal Lottery random-draw tag match

matches.note: Aric, openly hostile to his randomly-drawn partner Bob, slaps him for not helping; Bob knocks Aric out cold with a single punch, and Hoser covers for the pin.
matches.stipulation: TV Title Tournament first round — Lethal Lottery random-draw tag match

matches.note: Denrol hits a top-rope bulldog on Warner and Johnny Tambo follows with an elbow for the pin. Moments later Tambo, fed a chair by Jennifer, blindsides his own winning partner Denrol with it. Zack, having lost, then turns on his own partner Warner and is pulled off by security.
matches.stipulation: TV Title Tournament first round — Lethal Lottery random-draw tag match

name: Friday Night Fights — 4 Sep 1998
notes: TV Title Tournament first round, run in Lethal Lottery format (randomly-drawn tag partners across four tag matches; the winning teams advance). Nik Segier's match with the Black Scorpion (accompanied by the Fan) is preceded by a run-in: Elixir fells the Fan with a purse from ringside, clearing Segier's path; Elixir is shown seated with Segier's own wife and his manager GI Jane. Mid-match, backstage cameras show New Star attacking David Wattsoner with a crowbar in the parking lot and stealing his car, escalating their feud from the prior show. All four Lethal Lottery pairings end with a partner turning on his own ally after the bell: Big Eliem chokeslams his own partner Big Daddy Butler before the match even starts fairly (Bomber pins Butler off it); Gregory O'Hara sucker-attacks his own winning partner Vinnie Bomber; Jennifer slides Johnny Tambo a chair to blindside his own partner Father Denrol moments after their win; and a beaten Zack Crockett turns on his own partner Shane Warner after their loss, stopped only by security.

matches.note: Vinnie "the Bronx" Bomber, avenging O'Hara's own post-match attack on him at the Lethal Lottery, runs in and attacks O'Hara; Shaman, uninvolved in the interference, rolls out of the ring anyway and the referee awards the match to O'Hara, who advances in the Television Title Shot Tourney.
Tambo rolls up Vinnie for a quick pin and advances.
matches.stipulation: WWA Television Title Shot Tourney, first round

matches.note: Mantis finishes Payne with a top-rope splash he calls "the Nutcracker" for the pin and advances.
matches.stipulation: WWA Television Title Shot Tourney, first round

matches.note: Denrol finishes Hoser with the "Evil Killer" for the pin and advances.
matches.stipulation: WWA Television Title Shot Tourney, first round

matches.note: Malkav Amaranth runs in and holds the Outlaw's feet down during a suplex attempt, letting Segier roll him up for the pin; the rest of the Executive's Club chases Amaranth off, but he escapes after a Frankensteiner on Mr. Business and a wet willy on Elixir.

Brother Wattsoner (David Wattsoner, accompanying Denrol to this match) yanks the top rope as O'Hara attempts his "Leprechaun Leap" from the top, crotching him; Denrol follows up with the Evil Killer from the top turnbuckle for the pin and advances to the tourney final.
matches.stipulation: WWA Television Title Shot Tourney, second round

matches.note: Tambo counters a top-rope "Nutcracker" attempt by raising his knees, then finishes Mantis with the "Hollywood or Bust" for the win, advancing to the tourney final against Father Denrol.
matches.stipulation: WWA Television Title Shot Tourney, second round

matches.note: The Commandant's Own and the Minnesota Wrecking Crew both jump Anarchy before the bell, working together against the champions early. The Spiritual Warriors are eliminated first when Raiden rolls up Darkbringer for the pin. The Minnesota Wrecking Crew are eliminated next amid a chaotic spell of dueling ringside spotlights, a missed chair shot, and a knocked-out referee. In the final fall, Raiden finishes Sgt. Matthew Payne with the "Somersault Whiplash Diamond Bomb" (countering an attempted Ground Assault DDT) for the pin — Anarchy retains.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship, four-way elimination — Anarchy (champions) vs. the Commandant's Own vs. the Minnesota Wrecking Crew vs. the Spiritual Warriors; last team standing wins

matches.note: Both men trade control of the nightstick and open each other up bleeding; Logan finally locks an Irish Sleeper on an already-knocked-out Jack with the nightstick still in hand, and the referee stops it on a three-count arm-drop test. Logan becomes the new WWA Television Champion.
matches.stipulation: WWA Television Championship — nightstick ladder match (first to retrieve and use a nightstick suspended 12 feet over the ring, pin or submission wins)

matches.note: New Star fails to bribe Vinnie into laying down beforehand. In the brawl proper: Shaman finishes Vinnie with a Thunderclap onto restroom sink tile for the first elimination. New Star, after a car-hood exchange, finishes David Wattsoner with a superkick into a shooting star press for the second elimination. Shaman and New Star fight to a jumbotron dive and back into the arena, where New Star blinds Shaman with a powder throw to the eyes, then finishes him with a garbage-can-assisted leg drop for the win.
matches.stipulation: Chicago Street Fight, four-way elimination, falls count anywhere through the arena and surrounding streets

matches.note: Cross works Steele's taped ribs throughout, repeatedly cheating on the ropes during an abdominal stretch and camel clutch; Steele briefly rallies after Cross taunts him too far, but Cross regains control with a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker, a figure-four leglock, a belly-to-back suplex, and finally a Boston crab that the referee stops as a knockout/submission when Steele's arm drops three times. Cross retains.

name: WWA Labor Day PPV
notes: Chicago's United Center hosts. Opens with Johnny Tambo and Jennifer cutting a promo declaring his alliance of convenience with the STB against House of Pain and naming no specific target yet. The WWA World Tag Team Championship is defended in a four-way elimination match (Anarchy champions vs. the Commandant's Own vs. the Minnesota Wrecking Crew vs. the Spiritual Warriors); Anarchy retains. Backstage, the Vindicators (Blood Cross and Blood Shadow) ambush Flynn Steele with baseball bats ahead of his own main event, but ChiKylin, Mantis and Shane Warner drive them off. Todd Logan wins a nightstick ladder match over Jack to become the new WWA Television Champion. In the Television Title Shot Tourney's scheduled final, an unnamed masked man conjures a wall of fire in the ring mid-match between Johnny Tambo and Father Denrol, accusing Denrol of being "the Dark One" and promising him a "baptism of fire"; Denrol refuses to continue, and President Harrington reschedules the match for wwa-1998-09-12 (where it resolves — see that show). Backstage, Randy Cross is caught handing Mad Coil a wad of cash, played as a running joke about paying Coil to "cut his lawn." Randy Cross retains the WWA World Heavyweight Championship over Flynn Steele in the main event.

matches.note: Fire finishes Sonic with the "Backdraft" (a tumbleweed flip into a leg drop) for the pin. Afterward, Steihl clotheslines Fire and calls him a wannabe; the two trade fire tricks (a flame wall, a corkscrew forearm through the flames) until Steihl retreats without a match taking place.
Mantis finishes Kev Rock with a top-rope fisherman's suplex he calls "the Shocker" for the pin.
Awarded to Pepper by disqualification after Wolf Boy runs in, briefly submits Pepper himself with a body-scissors kneelock, then low-blows the champion Lancer. Title does not change hands on a DQ.

During the match, Gregory O'Hara heckles from the ramp with signs mocking the Brotherhood, then smashes a whiskey bottle over Brother Spy's head when Spy confronts him. Raven Crow trips Tambo, the lights cut out, and Darken appears in the ring manipulating the lighting before vanishing with Raven Crow when the lights return. Fire, perched in the rafters, hurls a fireball at what turns out to be a dummy made up to look like the unconscious Brother Spy — Spy himself is found hanging from the rafters, unhurt by the fire. Denrol, distracted trying to save the dummy, is counted out; Tambo wins and advances to face Todd Logan for the Television Championship.
matches.stipulation: Winner becomes #1 contender for the WWA Television Championship

matches.note: Company president Mark Harrington bars the injured Flynn Steele from competing on doctor's orders, but Steele enters the cage anyway to a standing ovation. Cross and the Outlaw temporarily ally, working over Steele's taped ribs together (including a Outlaw piledriver spiked by a Cross diving elbow, and a double-team torture rack/legdrop combo); the Outlaw then reveals a House of Pain shirt under his own, formalizing the alliance for the rest of the match. STB tries to enter the cage from ringside but finds the door locked and gives up. Darken cuts the cage's chain, enters, clotheslines the Outlaw, powerbombs him, and double chokeslams both Cross and the Outlaw before standing on both men's chests for a self-ordered three count — commentary explicitly disputes that the count should stand ("that doesn't count, the coward jumped them from behind"), no official decision is announced afterward, and Cross's own championship reign continues uninterrupted past this show. Darken exits by slamming Steele into the cage wall on his way out; the Outlaw closes the show challenging Darken to a match with Mr. Business next week.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship — steel cage, first fall wins; three-way among champion Randy Cross, the Outlaw, and Flynn Steele

name: WWA — 12 Sep 1998
notes: Opens with a new "Outlaw Saloon" talk-show segment: the Outlaw interviews Johnny Tambo and Jennifer, offering Tambo an open invitation to the New Executive's Club if he ever turns on House of Pain the way he's turned on the Outlaw's own enemies. Backstage, Malkav Amaranth pies Mad Coil in the face and is chased off; later he hides under the announce desk and bites Terry Valentine's leg. Before Father Denrol's match, a comedic skit has Denrol (dressed as Flynn Steele), Brother Spy (dressed as Mantis) and David Wattsoner (in a cowboy outfit), led out by Cockroach as a mocking "Simply The Bitch," ambushed by the real Flynn Steele, Mantis and Shane Warner; Wattsoner, still not fully recovered from an off-panel "Chicago Street Fight," is knocked out and taken to the medical area. Commentator Eric is given a full name, "Eric Pembrook," for the first time.

matches.note: Fire is distracted by a fiery apparition of Steihl materializing at ringside; Malkav Amaranth rolls him up for the pin.
Mad Coil finishes Gutter with the "Avalanche" (a powerbomb) and continues attacking him after the bell until Shaman runs in from the crowd for the save.
Vinnie, managed by Bill Dove, finishes Aric Crockett with the "B-52 Bomber" for the pin.

Anarchy's own Havok appears on the arena's big screen threatening to burn the Marine Corps colors he holds unless the Commandant's Own leave the ring by a ten count; Payne and Major Havok abandon the match and are counted out, so Anarchy retains. Anarchy then flees the building by limo with the Commandant's Own in pursuit.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — the Commandant's Own challenging Anarchy

name: WWA — 19 Sep 1998
notes: FIRE (Fire Storm) materializes fire from around the ring that briefly forms the shape of Steihl, distracting Fire long enough for Malkav Amaranth to steal the pin. Mad Coil continues beating down Gutter well after the bell before Shaman makes the save from the crowd; Mad Coil and Shaman have a mic confrontation before security separates them, teased as a future singles program. Malkav Amaranth is shown messing with control-room equipment during the Vinnie/Crockett match, a comedic aside with no in-match effect. Angel Reaper interviews New Star, who vows to beat Shaman on Shaman's own turf in the desert. In the main event, Havok (Anarchy's own, absent at ringside) threatens on the big screen to burn the Marine Corps colors, causing the Commandant's Own (challengers) to abandon the ring and be counted out, leaving Anarchy's WWA World Tag Team Championship intact.

matches.note: New Star finishes Sonic with a facelock/neckbreaker combo he calls the "Nova-Bomb" for the pin, in 3:03.
El Porto Spidero, in his WWA debut, finishes Adam Woolcock (managed by Lenore) with the "Fisherman's Buster" for the pin.
Malkav Amaranth finishes Matt Pepper with the "Madness Driver" for the pin. Afterward, Elixir runs in and paintballs Malkav with a gun full of red paint as a prank.
O'Hara finishes Butler with the "Celtic Crush" (a modified DDT) off his own "Leprechaun Leap" for the pin, then cuts a promo demanding a spot in the Best of the Best Tourney.

The Ungentle Giant interferes repeatedly from ringside for the Brotherhood (a reverse DDT and a slam on Big Eliem) without being a legal participant, and Todd Logan does the same for House of Pain, pulling Brent Watson off the apron and stomping him outside the ring. The Outlaw finishes David Wattsoner with the Outlaw Kick for the pin.
matches.stipulation: Six-man tag — House of Pain (the Outlaw subbing in for Todd Logan) vs. the Brotherhood

matches.note: Five unnamed masked men attack House of Pain's ringside contingent as Mad Coil, managed by the Death Knight, has Tambo in a camel clutch; with the referee distracted, Jennifer clocks Mad Coil with her clapboard and Tambo covers for the pin. Tambo retains.

name: Friday Night Fights — 9 Oct 1998
notes: During an Outlaw's Saloon segment with guest Jak Lancer, Lone Wolf knocks Lancer out cold with a thrown rock. Father Denrol runs an unscheduled, self-parodying face-turn skit with Joey Edwards' own step-by-step "kit," interrupted by Brother Duke performing the Brotherhood's recurring "Walkin' Metal" bit; Denrol changes his mind and vows revenge on House of Pain instead. A scheduled tag match pitting the Vindicators (Blood Cross, Blood Shadow) against Steihl and Black Scorpion (billed, without Darken, as the Overlords of the Dark) never gets underway: Darken and Jack ambush both teams, pin Blood Cross in an unsanctioned count, and Darken cuts a promo reclaiming the Overlords of the Dark name from Steihl by force. In the main event, five unnamed masked men attack House of Pain at ringside during the WWA Television Championship match, letting Jennifer clock Mad Coil with her clapboard for the deciding blind-side pin; House of Pain (including Darken and Jack, the Outlaw, Jak Lancer, and Big Eliem) storms the ring afterward, but Tambo and Jennifer escape through the crowd.

matches.note: Segier targets Wattsoner's bad knee throughout and finishes with a figure four leglock for the tap-out.
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament, first round

matches.note: Eliem nearly no-shows, rushing in only at the referee's nine count. Steele finishes with a leg-scissor submission he calls the "Tashaskaira."
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament, first round

matches.note: O'Hara chop-blocks Bob's knee and finishes with the "Leprechaun Leap" for the pin.
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament, first round

matches.note: Two masked "monks" accompanying New Star (later unmasked elsewhere as Chaos and Raiden) distract the referee; New Star finishes Denrol with the Nova-Bomb for the pin.
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament, first round

matches.note: Jennifer's presence at ringside distracts the Outlaw; Jack runs in with a chair, decking the Outlaw and setting up Payne's pin while Johnny Tambo holds the referee's attention. Tambo then hits his own "Hollywood or Bust" on the fallen Outlaw afterward as a receipt, unrelated to the match's own already-decided finish.
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament, first round

matches.note: Randy Cross and the Crocketts appear at ringside, drawing Steele's attention away; Vixen slips O'Hara a foreign object, and O'Hara knocks Steele out with it before finishing with the Leprechaun Leap.
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament, second round

matches.note: Misery, "Shinma" David Briceland, and Elixir all get involved: Misery blinds ringside ally El Porto Spidero and chairs Segier unconscious while Briceland distracts the referee, and Elixir (not under WWA contract at the time, per commentary) runs in to fight off Misery and Briceland. Segier is unable to answer the referee's ten count; New Star wins by countout and advances.
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament, second round

matches.note: Two "monks" escorting New Star are revealed mid-match to be Nik Segier and El Porto Spidero in disguise, sabotaging their own charge in payback for his earlier win over Segier: O'Hara ducks a chair shot meant for him and New Star is knocked out instead, and O'Hara covers for the win. New Star blindsides O'Hara with the tournament trophy afterward as two more "monks" (revealed as Chaos and Raiden) run in against Segier and Spidero, sparking a total brawl the broadcast cuts away from. O'Hara wins the tournament.
matches.stipulation: Best of the Best Tournament final — winner earns a WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot

name: WWA — 28 Oct 1998
notes: Opens with the debut of "WWA SLAM," a new recap show hosted by new VP Stan Jackson (recapping the prior Friday's card without new match content of its own — see that show for primary structuring). Before the tournament proper, Jack (defending President Harrington's own "not a match" ruling) brawls with the Outlaw in an unsanctioned fight at the Outlaw's own goading; House of Pain (Mr. Business, Todd Logan) and the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse (Darken, Steihl) both run in, and Raven Crow and an unnamed second man appear at the top of the ramp, spooking House of Pain into fleeing through the crowd. Jak Lancer is withdrawn from the tournament after an escalating backstage/parking-lot brawl with Griffin (still wrestling as "Lone Wolf") involving a barbed-wire bat and broken glass, ending with Lancer taken out by ambulance. Sgt. Matthew Payne is withdrawn from the tournament after House of Pain (Randy Cross, Aric and Zack Crockett) ambushes him backstage between rounds with a chair and a figure four. The tournament's own championship-caliber finish turns on a double swerve: two of the "monks" escorting New Star to the final are unmasked as Nik Segier and El Porto Spidero, saboting their own escort in payback for New Star's earlier win over Segier, while two other "monks" from an earlier round are separately unmasked as Chaos and Raiden. Gregory O'Hara wins the whole tournament, earning the WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot he cashes in at wwa-1998-11-08.

name: The First Annual WWAmmies
notes: A clip-show awards ceremony at Madison Square Garden marking the WWA's first anniversary, hosted by VP Stan Jackson with rotating guest presenters. Awards: Most Improved Wrestler (Jack, over MidCarder and Mad Coil — Jack, hospitalized, accepts by taped message and calls out the Outlaw, Todd Logan, Mr. Business, and Steihl); Best Feud (a tie announced for Randy Cross and Nik Segier, honoring both the Cross/Darken-Steihl/House of Pain war and the Cross/Segier program); Tag Team of the Year (the Overlords of the Dark, over Mantis/ChiKylin and Anarchy — presenter Mantis, now dressed like F.E.A.R., visibly resents being asked to present; Darken and Steihl fight for real over the trophy afterward and have to be separated); Rookie of the Year (New Star, over Gregory O'Hara and the retiring Johnny Tambo); and Wrestler of the Year (Randy Cross, over Flynn Steele and Nik Segier). Shaman also hands out several joke non-awards (Most Full of Himself: Nik Segier; Biggest Blowhard: New Star; Largest Mouth: Randy Cross; Lamest Stable: Star Station X; Stick a Fork in Him He's Done: Gutter). The evening's two biggest angles: Nik Segier, accompanied by Jennifer, announces his in-storyline retirement from the WWA on the spot and challenges the Outlaw to one last one-on-one match; and Star Station X (New Star, David Briceland, Misery) run a World War II Axis-costume bit, induct a new unnamed member by way of a single heavily-accented line, then moon the crowd before leaving. A hospital-room clip for Jack's own taped acceptance briefly shows Jack II, Darken, Raven Crow, and "the blurred image of War" at his bedside — none named or explained further, left as an honest gap.

matches.note: Big Eliem, with his mother Big Mamma Jamma running interference on the referee, knocks Watson down with brass knuckles; Watson recovers and finishes Mad Coil with his own baseball bat, winning by ten count.

Wrestling masked as "Lone Wolf," Griffin knocks Lancer unconscious; referee Tad Simmons awards the title since Lancer never says "I quit." Mr. Agony unmasks the new champion afterward, revealing Griffin.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship — I Quit rules

matches.note: Flynn Steele lands the Triple S and two Evil Killers land the other way, but Alexandra climbs the cage and distracts both men; Denrol ultimately walks her down and out through the door himself for the win rather than continuing the beating.
ChiKylin and Mantis finish Chaos with a simultaneous top-rope spear/leg sweep combo they call "the Nightmare" for the pin, becoming new champions.
Payne reverses Logan's Irish Sleeper and finishes him with a crucifix shoulder slam he calls the "Ariel Assault" for his first singles title.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship — Logan's third bid to reclaim it

matches.note: Aric Crockett distracts the referee for a Steihl low blow; outside the ring, Darken and an armored ally (revealed after the fact as Bob) fight off the Minnesota Wrecking Crew and Black Scorpion, Bob knocking Scorpion out cold with a single move. Steihl finishes Jack II with a full nelson submission he calls "Delivered Unto Pain" for the reclaimed title.

The Outlaw's own slingshot jackhammer attempt fails when his knee (worked over throughout the match) buckles at the crucial moment, and Segier falls on top for the pin. El Porto Spidero and Jennifer celebrate with Segier afterward; House of Pain (Randy Cross, the Minnesota Wrecking Crew, and the Outlaw himself) shake his hand rather than attack.
matches.stipulation: Grudge rubber match — storyline farewell for Segier

matches.note: O'Hara counters a figure-four setup with a surprise rollup for the pin, becoming the new champion and leaving House of Pain without any WWA title for the first time since the fed's own founding, per commentary.

name: WWA Birthday Bash
notes: Opens with Cold Pain Enterprises' formal debut promo: David Wattsoner declares the Brotherhood dead, rebrands the group CPE, and declares war on both House of Pain and Flynn Steele's newly-renamed F.E.A.R. stable. Every WWA title changes or is defended tonight except the US Championship, which Steihl reclaims for House of Pain from Jack II (standing in for the hospitalized Jack, per President Harrington's own ruling) by submission, with Darken and an armored ally (revealed as Bob) skirmishing outside the ring against the Minnesota Wrecking Crew and Black Scorpion, whom Steihl calls in as backup; Bob knocks Black Scorpion out cold with a single move. Nik Segier wins his storyline farewell/retirement match over the Outlaw in a rubber match, then receives an unexpectedly gracious sendoff from House of Pain (Randy Cross, the Minnesota Wrecking Crew, and the Outlaw all shake his hand). In the main event, Gregory O'Hara upsets Randy Cross for the WWA World Heavyweight Championship with a surprise rollup counter, leaving House of Pain without a single title in the promotion for what commentary calls possibly the first time since the fed's founding.

matches.note: Gregory O'Hara, guest commentating, slips Kasanova a handful of salt during a pre-arranged ringside handshake; Kasanova throws it in Watson's eyes and finishes him with the "Kiss of Death" (a 450 splash) for the pin.

Both men are down when the referee's ten count and the match's own time limit expire together; ruled a time-limit draw. Star Station X (New Star, Misery, the Stormtrooper) then runs in and beats Spidero down until Cold Pain Enterprises makes the save; Spidero joins CPE on the spot.
Thrown out after Black Lotus and Alexandra Korth brawl at ringside and Flynn Steele runs in to spear Denrol. Payne retains.
Steele finishes Mr. Business with a pedigree for the pin.
Gregory O'Hara distracts Logan from the apron; Steele finishes with the "Triple S" off the top rope for the pin.

Cross, visibly off his game and wrestling in street clothes rather than gear, tries the figure four too early; Steele rolls him up for the pin. Cross storms out of the building afterward, brushing off both Jak Lancer and the Outlaw.

Four clean falls occur in order: the Stormtrooper pins Black Scorpion with an Atomic DDT; Raiden piledrives and the Stormtrooper leg-drops Big Eliem for the pin; the Outlaw immediately follows with the Outlaw Kick to pin the Stormtrooper; the Outlaw then catches a distracted New Star (watching Darken's ringside appearance) with a bridged German suplex for the pin, leaving Steihl and the Outlaw against Chaos and Raiden. Darken's continued ringside presence and a chair-swinging brawl involving Chaos, plus Jack II's revenge run-in attacking the Outlaw outside the ring (payback for the US title loss the night before), spiral the match into total chaos; the referee calls for the bell with no team declared the winner.
matches.stipulation: Stable War — House of Pain vs. Star Station X (joined by Chaos and Raiden), four-man elimination tag

name: WWA — 14 Nov 1998
notes: Debut of a new Saturday broadcast, "Saturday Night Extreme," hosted by Eric Pembrook alongside guest commentators John Douglas (a former pro football player) and Juan Guevesos (billed "one of the original luchadors from Mexico" — the same name credited decades later as Nicholas Adams's confidant in 2006, not confirmed the same person but plausible given the shared fed). Reigning WWA World Heavyweight Champion Gregory O'Hara guest-commentates the opening match, secretly feeding Kris Kasanova a handful of salt during a pre-arranged handshake to help him beat Brent Watson. The Butler/Sniper match is left without a finish after Big Eliem's interference draws in Randy Cantley's security force and then the full Cold Pain Enterprises roster; the broadcast simply moves on. El Porto Spidero fights Shinma (David Briceland) to a time-limit draw, is beaten down afterward by Star Station X (New Star, Misery, the Stormtrooper), and is saved by Cold Pain Enterprises, joining the stable on the spot. Denrol's WWA Television Championship challenge against Sgt. Matthew Payne is thrown out after Black Lotus and Alexandra Korth brawl at ringside and Flynn Steele spears Denrol; Payne retains. Flynn Steele, now wrestling under the F.E.A.R. banner (with ChiKylin, Mantis, and Black Lotus), wins a gauntlet through Mr. Business and Todd Logan, then upsets a visibly off Randy Cross — wrestling in street clothes the night after losing the World Heavyweight title — with a rollup counter to a figure-four attempt; Cross storms out of the building afterward, shrugging off both Jak Lancer and the Outlaw. In the main event stable war, Chaos and Raiden (not formally introduced as Star Station X members, but siding with them) join New Star and the Stormtrooper against House of Pain's Big Eliem, Black Scorpion, Steihl, and the Outlaw; four clean falls occur before Darken's ringside appearance and Jack II's revenge run-in on the Outlaw (payback for the US title loss the night before) spiral the match into an uncontrolled brawl, and the referee calls for the bell with no team declared the winner.

matches.note: Stormtrooper squashes Powers with a chokeslam (breaking his own pin at two to keep punishing him) and finishes with an inverted DDT.

name: WWA — 18 Nov 1998
notes: A studio recap show, "SLAM!," hosted by VP Stan Jackson with guest co-host Flynn Steele, recapping the prior Friday's card (Kris Kasanova over Brent Watson with Gregory O'Hara's assistance; David Wattsoner and Big Daddy Butler surviving a Big Eliem run-in until the Commandant's Own broke it up; El Porto Spidero fighting Star Station X to a time-limit draw before Cold Pain Enterprises made the save, folding Spidero into their own ranks; Denrol's TV title challenge against Sgt. Matthew Payne ending without a clean finish after Black Lotus and Alexandra Korth traded blows at ringside and Flynn Steele himself got physical with Denrol over his wife, prompting a rescheduled rematch; and Flynn Steele's own gauntlet run through Mr. Business, Todd Logan, and Randy Cross before a Star Station X vs. House of Pain brawl closed the night with nothing settled). None of this recapped Friday content is structured as matches on this show's own record — see wwa-1998-11-14 for that show's own primary structuring. Johny Morehouse interviews TV Champion Sgt. Matthew Payne backstage, with Major Havok present; Payne warns off any stable interference ahead of his rematch with Denrol. Stan Jackson announces the December 11th "Season Beatings" pay-per-view.

matches.note: Annihilation finishes Destruction with "the Crippler" (a piledriver-type slam onto his own knee) for the pin, then joins Cold Pain Enterprises when Wattsoner throws him a CPE shirt at ringside.
The Spiritual Warriors finish Aric Crockett with Darkbringer's own "Spirit Call" for a quick pin.
Briceland finishes with a "Rack Driver" and the referee stops the match, ruling Butler unable to continue.
Payne's own worked-over knee gives out mid-comeback during a top-rope suplex attempt; Denrol lands on top with a cross body for the pin and the title.

The Stormtrooper blindsides his own partner Misery with the "Germany's Revenge," letting Black Scorpion crawl over for the pin. A mass brawl (New Star, Briceland, and Anarchy for Star Station X; the Outlaw, Mr. Business, Steihl, Todd Logan, and the Fan for House of Pain) erupts afterward, but the Stormtrooper simply walks past both sides without joining either.

New Star lands two low blows the referee misses (a groin claw, a hidden back kick) en route to finishing Cross with a bridged German suplex off the second rope — Cross's third straight loss. The Outlaw leaves partway through the match.

Steihl never submits to Flynn's own "Retribution" hold despite being trapped in it for an extended stretch, but a disguised fan (revealed afterward as Duke Daring) ambushes Steihl's own partner Black Scorpion at ringside as he rushes to help; the referee, amid the chaos, stops the match and rules Steihl unable to continue, awarding Flynn Steele the title in a widely disputed decision. Duke Daring then reveals himself and joins F.E.A.R., which now holds both the US and WWA World Tag Team Championships — House of Pain's last title is gone.

name: Friday Night Fights — 27 Nov 1998
notes: Steihl, defending both the US title and House of Pain's last remaining gold tonight, opens with a taped promo exchange against Flynn Steele. Big Daddy Butler's match against "Shinma" David Briceland ends in a referee stoppage, extending Briceland's own unbeaten start. In the tag match pitting Star Station X's Misery and the Stormtrooper against House of Pain's Big Eliem and Black Scorpion, the Stormtrooper blindsides his own partner Misery with the "Germany's Revenge" for the loss, then walks past both stables entirely when a mass brawl breaks out (New Star, Briceland, and Anarchy for SS-X; the Outlaw, Mr. Business, Steihl, Todd Logan, and the Fan for House of Pain) — his own allegiance left an open question. Randy Cross, dropping his third straight match, loses clean to New Star, who wins with multiple low blows the referee misses. In the main event, Flynn Steele wins Steihl's United States Championship — House of Pain's last title — on a disputed referee stoppage after the champion, submitting to Flynn's "Retribution" for an extended stretch without ever tapping, sees his own partner Black Scorpion ambushed at ringside by a disguised fan revealed as Duke Daring, a wrestler with prior PCWF history against Steele. Duke Daring then joins F.E.A.R., which now holds both the United States and WWA World Tag Team Championships, and House of Pain is left without a single title.

matches.note: Malkav dumps paint on Wattsoner and tries scrubbing off his CPE tattoo with a scouring pad; Wattsoner recovers and, with the Ungentle Giant handing him a chair and Joseph Stock/El Porto Spidero distracting the referee, finishes Malkav with a chair-assisted pin.
Smith finishes Sonic with the "Wolf's Howl" for the pin in his WWA debut.

Their third meeting. Watson nearly escapes first, but Mad Coil beats him to the top, then unties the rope Watson is still climbing, dropping him roughly ten feet back to the concrete floor for the win.
matches.stipulation: Himalayan Pit Fight — first to climb the hanging rope out of a 15-foot pit wins

matches.note: Pinfall sequence: Vinnie pins Keenan; Keenan pins Gutter; Shaman pins Keenan, then Gutter; Gutter pins Keenan, then Vinnie; Gutter's own pin attempt on Shaman (which would have completed his set) is broken up by Keenan. Shaman finally pins Vinnie with the Thunderclap, completing pins on all three opponents (Keenan, Gutter, Vinnie) for the win. Shaman closes with a mic promo warning Black Scorpion, "the hunt begins."
matches.stipulation: Warriors Cage match — each man must pin each of the other three individually; first to do so wins

name: WWA — 28 Nov 1998
notes: Opens backstage with Stormtrooper being brutally beaten down by his own Star Station X stablemates New Star and David Briceland (Misery already down/incapacitated), then further by Chaos and Raiden with Havoc taunting "you don't f*ck with the Star Station" — the beating leaves Stormtrooper unfit for his own scheduled singles debut against Billy Coleman (never fought). Damien "The Wolf" Smith debuts with a win over Sonic, then runs a comedy meet-and-greet bit pairing a fan with a bikini-clad valet (unnamed).

matches.note: Coleman chokeslams Smith with the "Rocky Mountain High," then finishes with the "Aspen Extreme" for the pin.
Gutter subs for the Mimic (sidelined by a contract dispute). Ravage finishes with the "Ragebomb" for the pin in his WWA debut.
Crosscheck, using his own hockey stick throughout, finishes Butler with the "Crosscheck" for the pin in his WWA debut.
After a ladder spot off the entrance ramp, Duke Daring finishes Keenan with a "Daring Death Drop" onto a chair for the pin in his WWA debut.

Duke Scotsman slips Wattsoner a crowbar for a low blow; Wattsoner pins Mad Coil off it. House of Pain (Randy Cross, the Outlaw, Todd Logan) then turns on the beaten Mad Coil, assaulting him further until Randy Cantley's security breaks it up.
matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Title Tournament, first round

matches.note: Joey Edwards distracts the original referee at the three count; Black Scorpion powder-blinds Shaman, and a mystery replacement referee makes an unusually fast three-count for Watson before disappearing. Backstage footage afterward shows the Spiritual Warriors beaten unconscious with "HOP" painted on their backs, explaining their absence.
matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Title Tournament, first round

matches.note: A brutal barbwire-chair brawl; New Star finishes Lancer with a Nova-Bomb onto the barbwire-wrapped chair for the pin.
matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Title Tournament, first round

matches.note: Griffin (still wrestling as "Lone Wolf") superglues Vinnie's hair to the mat, then finishes with a bell shot cushioned by a pillow and a somersault headbutt for the pin.
matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Title Tournament, first round

matches.note: Denrol finishes Briceland with the Evil Killer for the pin, retaining.

Darken unexpectedly turns on Anarchy to help Steihl, chokeslamming Raiden and clotheslining Chaos, before also clotheslining Steihl himself. Star Station X (New Star et al.), House of Pain (the Outlaw, Todd Logan, Mr. Business, the Crocketts), Shaman, David Briceland, and Randy Cantley's security all pour in for a total, multi-stable brawl the show runs out of time on; no decision is reached.
matches.stipulation: The New Overlords of the Dark (Steihl, Black Scorpion) vs. Total Anarchy (Chaos, Raiden)

name: WWA — 5 Dec 1998
notes: Opens with Denrol and Alexandra staging a fake $5 million payoff ambush on Flynn Steele and Black Lotus using two disguised security guards; one unmasks as Denrol himself, but the other — meant to be his own ally — unmasks as Gregory O'Hara instead, who gives Steele his own "Leprechaun Leap" rather than help Denrol, protecting his own Title vs. Title opponent ahead of Season's Beatings. Gutter substitutes for the Mimic (sidelined by a contract dispute) against debuting newcomer Ravage. During the Extreme Title Tournament's own Mad Coil/Sniper match, House of Pain (Randy Cross, the Outlaw, Todd Logan) turns on its own Mad Coil after the loss, assaulting him until Randy Cantley's security breaks it up. Shaman loses his own tournament match to Brent Watson via a suspicious finish (a mystery replacement referee makes an unusually fast count); backstage footage afterward reveals the Spiritual Warriors beaten unconscious with "HOP" painted on their backs, explaining their absence. A promotional vignette for the upcoming PPV shows Star Station X assaulting a Santa Claus figure; the PPV's own billed date is given as December 13th here, contradicting December 11th (per wwa-1998-11-18's recap) and December 15th (per wwa-1998-11-28) on other broadcasts — an unresolved continuity slip, not corrected here. Champion Gregory O'Hara is ambushed by Todd Logan during a ringside interview; security separates them. Denrol retains the WWA Television Championship over "Shinma" David Briceland. The main event, the New Overlords of the Dark (Steihl and Black Scorpion, the name now used in their own ring introduction) vs. Total Anarchy (Chaos and Raiden, aligned with Havoc/Star Station X), spirals into a total multi-stable brawl — Darken unexpectedly turns on Anarchy to help Steihl, then Star Station X, House of Pain, Shaman, Briceland, and Randy Cantley's security all pour in — and ends with no decision as the broadcast runs out of time.

matches.note: The Mimic, debuting in a copycat entrance mocking Vinnie's own look, finishes him with Vinnie's own "Bronx Bomb" for the pin.
A back-and-forth war of a match; Spidero finally knocks Misery out cold with an unopened tequila bottle and the (replacement) referee counts him out.
matches.stipulation: "Misery's Rules" — no DQ, weapons legal, falls count anywhere; win by most pinfalls in an hour or a ten count

matches.note: After a brutal weapons-heavy brawl (chair shots, a ring bell to the knee, a gutwrench piledriver onto a chair), Griffin tries to knock Wattsoner out with a chloroform rag but Wattsoner reverses it onto him instead, then pins him for the win. Wattsoner advances to the tournament final.
matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Championship Tournament semifinal — Griffin still wrestling as "Lone Wolf"

matches.note: Shaman runs in and flying-clotheslines Watson from the top rope, letting New Star cover for the pin; New Star advances to face Wattsoner in the tournament final at Season's Beatings.

name: WWA — 26 Dec 1998
notes: Semifinals of a new WWA Extreme Championship tournament, setting up the final at Season's Beatings the next night. During Spidero/Misery's own extreme-rules bout, Denrol dressed as Santa Claus ambushes Star Station X at ringside with a lead pipe, driving them briefly backstage. Brent Watson enters his own match disguised as a cameraman before revealing himself and attacking New Star; Shaman, now openly feuding with Cold Pain Enterprises, interferes on New Star's behalf, drawing Duke Scotsman out to stop him before security intervenes — Watson chases Shaman off afterward.

matches.note: Jack II hovers ringside throughout, distracting both men, before Flynn Steele runs him off; Daring finishes Business with a tornado DDT for the pin. Jack II then attacks the fallen Business with two chair shots and a piledriver onto a chair, stopped only by a run-in from the Outlaw; Darken disarms the Outlaw and leads Jack II away without further violence.
matches.stipulation: Special challenge match — Daring's open HOP challenge

matches.note: An hour-long hardcore war through the crowd and ringside (barbwire, ladders, tables, a bell shot) ends with New Star powerbombing Wattsoner through a standing chair for the pin. The two shake hands afterward, and New Star offers Wattsoner a Star Station X spot over the Stormtrooper's.
matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Hardcore Wrestling Championship final — inaugural champion

matches.note: Jak Lancer interferes for Griffin (still wrestling as "Lone Wolf"), then Randy Cross and the Outlaw interfere for House of Pain against Denrol; the referee calls for a double disqualification. Neither title changes hands.
matches.stipulation: WWA Television Championship vs. WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship unification match

matches.note: New Star, already carrying a freshly re-stitched arm wound from his own hardcore title win earlier the same night, is caught in a double press and thrown into the cage; ChiKylin pins him while Mantis holds off Briceland's save attempt. New Star loses consciousness from blood loss afterward and is taken out on a stretcher. F.E.A.R. retains.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — Roman Candle cage match (flamethrowers trigger off contact with the cage walls); Havoc substitutes New Star and Briceland in for a supposedly flight-delayed Chaos and Raiden

matches.note: A masked, trenchcoated attacker (unnamed) ambushes Todd Logan in the crowd as a distraction; Denrol, reaching for brass knuckles, accidentally decks O'Hara rather than the intended target, and Steele's resulting near-fall is broken up when Sniper pulls Denrol's leg mid-count. O'Hara finishes Steele with the Leprechaun Leap for the pin and unifies both titles — commentary itself questions whether Steele's shoulder was up. Denrol turns on O'Hara immediately afterward, slapping him and fleeing with both title belts as Cold Pain Enterprises escapes.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship vs. WWA United States Championship unification match; special guest referee Denrol

name: WWA Season's Beatings
notes: Season's Beatings, the WWA's December PPV (its own billed date varied across broadcasts — see wwa-1998-12-05's own notes). Duke Daring's own "any HOP member, anytime" challenge is answered by Mr. Business; after Daring wins, Jack II attacks Business with a chair in revenge for the United States title match Business helped cost him, until the Outlaw makes the save — Darken then appears, disarms the Outlaw without striking him, and leads Jack II away, apparently setting up a one-on-one issue between the two rather than a stable brawl. New Star wins the inaugural WWA Extreme Hardcore Wrestling Championship over the Sniper (David Wattsoner) in an hour-long hardcore war, then offers Wattsoner his own spot in Star Station X over the Stormtrooper's. Denrol's title-unification match (his own TV title against Griffin's Light Heavyweight title, Griffin still billed "Lone Wolf") ends in a double disqualification after Jak Lancer and then House of Pain (Randy Cross, the Outlaw) both interfere — neither title changes hands. Havoc fakes a "flight delay" to keep Anarchy's Chaos and Raiden out of their own Roman Candle cage title defense, feeding New Star and David Briceland into the fire-rigged cage in their place instead; F.E.A.R. (Mantis, ChiKylin) retains after New Star, wrestling a second brutal match in one night on a freshly re-opened arm wound, passes out from blood loss and is stretchered out. In the main event, a title-unification match pits World Heavyweight Champion Gregory O'Hara against United States Champion Flynn Steele, with special guest referee Denrol visibly favoring Cold Pain Enterprises throughout; a masked, trenchcoated attacker ambushes Todd Logan in the crowd (unnamed, an honest gap) as a distraction, Denrol accidentally brass-knuckles O'Hara rather than the intended target, and Sniper breaks up the resulting Steele near-fall before O'Hara finishes Steele with the Leprechaun Leap for a disputed pin (commentary itself questions whether Steele's shoulder was up). Denrol then turns on O'Hara, slapping him and fleeing with both of O'Hara's now-unified championship belts as Cold Pain Enterprises makes its own getaway.

matches.note: Shaman has the match won (about to hit the Thunderclap) when Black Scorpion runs in and reverse-DDTs him for the disqualification; Shaman wins by DQ despite the interference.
The Outlaw catches Pepper's missile piledriver attempt in midair and finishes with a powerbomb for the pin.
Mantis finishes Payne with a headbutt to the groin he calls "the Nutcracker" for the pin.

name: WWA — 6 Jan 1999
notes: Debut of a new studio recap show, hosted by Joseph Stock, recapping Season's Beatings (results only, not restructured here — see wwa-1998-12-27) and airing three original matches plus an O'Hara sit-down interview and a Darken promo vignette. O'Hara's interview covers his backstory (grew up in Kilroy, Ireland, recruited into the IRA around age 9 by a since-unnamed but implied figure, left for the US around 16) and confirms he has been offered — and is turning down — a Cold Pain Enterprises recruitment pitch from Sniper; the masked man who stopped Todd Logan's attack on him at Season's Beatings remains unidentified even to O'Hara. Darken airs an elaborate self-produced promo announcing the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse's own 1999 agenda and formally challenging O'Hara for the WWA World Heavyweight Championship on the Friday Night Fights following O'Hara's own upcoming title defense against Steihl at Rage in the Cage (WWA's next PPV, 24 January 1999, American West Arena, Phoenix, AZ — no matches signed yet as of this broadcast). A new tag team tournament is announced with brackets shown (Lone Wolf/Jak Lancer vs. the Outlaw/Denrol; a mystery slot to be decided by a triangle match among Hot House, Anarchy, and the Spiritual Warriors vs. Flynn Steele/Gregory O'Hara; MidCarder/Kristopher Kasanova vs. David Briceland/El Porto Spidero; Duke Daring/Jack II vs. Steihl/Darken) — not structured here as none of it has happened yet.

matches.note: After being comedically dragged to the ring by Randy Cantley's security, Ravage baits Destruction, finishing him with the "RageBomb" (a jackknife powerbomb) for the pin — his second straight win.

Black Scorpion runs in and "Equalizer"s Coleman without warning; when House of Pain's Aric and Zack Crockett try to help, Black Scorpion "Equalizer"s Zack too and the Mimic locks a Brazilian armbar on Aric. The Mimic finishes the recovering Coleman with Coleman's own "Aspen Extreme" piledriver, declaring "know your role, choose your side" — Black Scorpion has visibly turned on House of Pain.
MidCarder, back from a break and visibly more ruthless, finishes Payne with the "Average Man Slam" for the pin.

Billed simply as "Denrol vs. Steele," the challenger turns out to be Flynn Steele's own son Ken rather than Flynn himself. Denrol counters an early flurry and takes control for most of the match, but Ken reverses an Evil Killer attempt into his own "Lights Out" submission (a Million Dollar Dream variant) for the win. F.E.A.R. immediately rebrands as "the Freaks," beating down Denrol's own CPE reinforcements (Sniper, Brent Watson, Annihilation), spray-painting "FREAKS" on Denrol's chest, and handing him over to CPE.

name: Friday Night Fights — 15 Jan 1999
notes: Opens with David Wattsoner ("Sniper") announcing his in-storyline retirement from wrestling (while remaining CPE's own leader from ringside), booking a final match against the Outlaw and a farewell "dream match" against his own student Denrol, both promised for Rage in the Cage; Denrol and El Porto Spidero give tribute speeches. A Jack II/Mr. Business match is announced by Gary Trudeau but never actually shown on the broadcast, cutting instead to a clip of Gregory O'Hara being bailed out of jail by an unnamed rescuer. In a major swerve, Black Scorpion turns on House of Pain during Billy Coleman's own match, "Equalizer"-ing both Coleman (whom he was ostensibly there to help) and House of Pain's own Zack Crockett, aligning himself with the Mimic's "Know Your Role, Choose Your Side" philosophy; the Mimic finishes off Coleman with Coleman's own "Aspen Extreme" piledriver as a warning. In the main event, the WWA Television Championship match billed simply as "Denrol vs. Steele" turns out to be against Ken Steele — revealed on-air as Flynn Steele's own son — rather than Flynn himself; Ken wins the title outright in his own surprise debut. F.E.A.R. immediately rebrands as "the Freaks" (Flynn Steele now billed "RingMaster"), unveiling grotesque new looks for Mantis and ChiKylin, beating down Denrol's own CPE reinforcements (Sniper, Brent Watson, Annihilation), spray-painting "FREAKS" across the fallen champion's chest, and handing him over to CPE.

matches.note: Aric Crockett sneaks in a weapon shot on Darken; Steihl, unhappy with his own partner, walks out on the match entirely. Darken, hurt from Aric's shot, is counted out after being sent over the top with a thrust-hip toss (thez press), and Duke Daring/Jack II advance.
MidCarder locks in the "HoseHead" on Briceland and Kasanova finishes with a shooting star press for the pin, knocking Spidero off the apron to prevent the save. MidCarder/Kasanova advance.

The Outlaw and Denrol ambush Griffin (still wrestling as "Lone Wolf") with a chair and a bulldog before the bell even rings. After a chaotic brawl, the Outlaw finishes Jak Lancer with the Outlaw Kick for the pin; the Outlaw/Denrol pairing advances.

name: WWA — 20 Jan 1999
notes: The first fully live Wednesday Slam. Opens with Mr. Business calling out Jack II, only to be brutally beaten down by the Outlaw, Todd Logan (using a loaded glove), and Aric Crockett in a HOP-internal power play — the Outlaw's own year-delayed payback for an old betrayal, and a sign (confirmed later in Harrington's own interview) that the Outlaw has become HOP's new leader. A vignette shows Sniper, Denrol, El Porto Spidero, and an unnamed masked CPE recruit arriving by dumpster truck, with Sniper saying he and the masked man "got a FREAK to take care of" — paying off later when the pair beat down and kidnap Duke Daring, stuffing him into the dumpster and driving off with him (unresolved by the end of the broadcast). Recap segments cover Darken becoming WWA World Heavyweight Champion over O'Hara (the ledger dates this to wwa-1999-01-15, though no such match appears in that show's own served text as read — an unresolved discrepancy, not corrected here absent a contradicting primary source), Star Station X's collapse after Briceland split from New Star (who joined the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse), and rumors of a mystery new CPE member and Denrol's own possible CPE exit. Mark Harrington gives a sit-down interview announcing a new three-person Executive Committee overseeing WWA's weekly shows and security, a "Stable Wars" four-team elimination match for the March Madness PPV where losing stables must disband, and naming Kristopher Kasanova and Ravage as wrestlers who've impressed him. A comedic vignette shows Bob shopping for a dress ahead of his own Dress Match at Rage in the Cage. Hot House's own tag tournament match against O'Hara and Ken Steele is voided before it starts when Nick Bruiser sucker-attacks O'Hara (a masked ally in a trenchcoat makes the save); Harrington personally overturns the resulting forfeit ruling and reschedules Hot House against O'Hara and Darken for the following week instead.

matches.note: Lantern finishes Annihilation with a swinging DDT onto a chair for the pin, in his WWA debut.

Kasanova finishes with a top-rope "Kiss of Death" splash to the outside for the pin. El Porto Spidero runs in afterward and beats Kasanova down with a Fisherman's Buster, warning him off cockiness on CPE's behalf.

Cross breaks his own pin attempt to let House of Pain (Mr. Business, Aric and Zack Crockett) run in and beat down Steele; F.E.A.R. (Duke Daring, Nick Bruiser, Flynn Steele) runs in to even the odds. Amid the chaos, Denrol hits a hit-and-run Evil Killer on the recovering Steele, unrelated to either side, before fleeing. No finish is reached.

After a hardcore brawl (a paint can, a wheelbarrow ramp spill, a barbwire bat), Shaman lands the Thunder Clap and covers, but the Outlaw and Todd Logan run in — protecting the Outlaw's own upcoming Rage in the Cage match with New Star — and the referee throws the match out. New Star retains.

name: WWA — 23 Jan 1999
notes: A video vignette has Gregory O'Hara, in a mock jail cell, hyping the WWA's next PPV, Rage in the Cage, billed here as January 31st (a further contradiction to the January 24th date given on wwa-1999-01-06 — an unresolved continuity slip). F.E.A.R. runs a gimmick-reveal angle: Flynn Steele, ChiKylin, Mantis, Duke Daring, and Nick Bruiser enter en masse alongside TV Champion Ken Steele, and ChiKylin's tattoos and Mantis's ornate mask are revealed as fake theatrical props, with Flynn declaring the stunt was just to draw heat since "no one mentioned any of the members of FEAR" before. Kristopher Kasanova is jumped and beaten down by El Porto Spidero after his own win, a message from CPE. Randy Cross's own WWA Television title challenge against Ken Steele is thrown into chaos by House of Pain (Mr. Business, Aric and Zack Crockett) and F.E.A.R. (Duke Daring, Nick Bruiser, Flynn Steele) both running in, plus an unrelated hit-and-run Evil Killer from Denrol on Ken Steele; no finish is reached. The main event, New Star defending the WWA Extreme Hardcore Wrestling Championship against Shaman, is thrown out after the Outlaw and Todd Logan interfere on Shaman's behalf, protecting the Outlaw's own upcoming #1-contender match against New Star at Rage in the Cage; the title does not change hands.

matches.note: Mantis runs in behind the referee's back, dropkicking Darken into O'Hara and then attacking both men; the two brawl to the outside with Mantis and are counted out together, awarding Hot House the win.
matches.stipulation: Tag Team Tournament, makeup first round

matches.note: MidCarder locks in the "Hosehead" on Daring, and Kasanova finishes with a shooting star press for the pin, advancing to the finals. El Porto Spidero attacks Kasanova again afterward.

Ken Steele, hiding under the ring, pulls Denrol under it mid-match to apply his own "Lights Out" submission, delaying his return; Sniper (David Wattsoner) also slides under the ring after him. Karl Flood ultimately rolls up Denrol for the pin off a legal-man mixup, and Hot House advances alongside MidCarder/Kasanova.

name: WWA — 27 Jan 1999
notes: Recaps the prior week's card (not restructured here) and previews the upcoming Rage in the Cage PPV (this Sunday) and Darken's Birthday Bash/Final Friday battle-royal-style PPV (12 February 1999) — neither structured here as future events. Darken, still WWA World Heavyweight Champion, gives a sit-down interview dismissing O'Hara's own claim to a title shot and warning the field ahead of Final Friday. Johny Morehouse interviews newcomer Ashley Dunnin, who publicly asks management to arrange him a match. In the tag tournament's own makeup first-round match, World Champion Darken and US Champion O'Hara — both previously betrayed by earlier partners and forced together as a fresh pairing — are counted out together after Mantis runs in and attacks both men, handing the win to Hot House (Scott "Bad Dog" Haggarty and "Crazy" Karl Flood). Duke Daring and Jack II fall to MidCarder and Kristopher Kasanova in the tournament's own second round; El Porto Spidero attacks Kasanova again afterward. In the main event, a rematch-style tag bout, Ken Steele and Sniper (David Wattsoner) both hide under the ring and get involved — Ken Steele pulls Denrol under the ring mid-match to apply a submission hold — before Hot House upsets Denrol and the Outlaw too, Karl Flood rolling up Denrol off a legal-man mixup.

name: WWA — 3 Feb 1999

matches.note: Both men's WWA debuts. Shaman, working as a guest color commentator this week, leaves the booth to interfere — a low blow on Cole from ringside sets up Albatross's "Life of Agony" crippler crossface for the submission win.

A back-and-forth main event ends in a mass brawl before a finish: Cold Pain Enterprises (Denrol, Lantern, Alexandra) run in on Spidero, then Gregory O'Hara and MidCarder — newly formed as "Youthful Rage"/"Young Guns" — make the save. No decision.

notes: The bulk of the broadcast is a Joe Stock-narrated recap (with commentary from Terry Valentine, Johny Morehouse and others as replay clip commentary) of the "Rage in the Cage" pay-per-view (wwa-rage-in-the-cage-99-january-31-1999-1999-01-31, out of this show's own served content) — those replayed results are not re-recorded here per the anti-double-count rule; they are evidence for that earlier show. The fresh content is two matches, an Outlaw interview, and a Nick Bruiser "Flash of the Week" promo previewing his rookie battle royal opponents.

name: Final Friday

matches.note: Steihl attacks before the bell; Outlaw wins by DQ after Steihl uses a chair repeatedly.
CPE vs. FEAR. Denrol counters a Daring Death Drop attempt into his own "Evil Killer" off the top rope for the pin.
New Star, the former Extreme champion, wins with the New Star Press.
Griffin, wrestling as "Lone Wolf," wins by submission with the "Howling at the Moon" after a chair-assisted beatdown of Albatross's debut opponent.
Payne, last year's runner-up, wins with the "Arial Assault" after Dunnin kicks out of several near-falls.
O'Hara wins with Todd Logan's own "Irish Sleeper," borrowed for the occasion.
Lancer wins with the "Boil Lancer."
Stablemates. MidCarder uses a chair on his own partner before finishing with the "HoseHead."
Coleman wins with the "Aspen Extreme" (a lifted chokeslam-piledriver).
A brawl into the aisle and back, with a table and multiple chair shots. Jack II wins with the "II Slam" off the top rope through a table, despite Outlaw taunting him from ringside.
Denrol pins Coleman (Evil Killer) to make it two-on-one; Outlaw then rolls up Denrol and finally submits Payne with the Irish Sleeper to advance alone — his own tag partner Coleman does not advance.

Griffin ("Lone Wolf") and Lancer jump O'Hara and New Star with barbed-wire-wrapped brass knuckles before the bell. Lancer knocks out New Star with the "Boil Lancer"; Griffin knocks out O'Hara with the "Howling at the Moon." Both advance individually.
Jack II wins by submission with the "II Seat."
A short, almost comedic bout between the two Round 2 tag partners — Griffin ("Lone Wolf") pins Lancer with an airplane-spin slam.
Outlaw wins by submission with the Irish Sleeper.

matches.stipulation: Final Friday: The Apocalypse 1999 Final — one hour, most falls wins
matches.note: Griffin, wrestling as "Lone Wolf," wins the tournament 6 falls to 5 — three of his own early falls came via disqualification for weapon use (a chair, then barbed-wire brass knuckles), which Darken rules count as falls anyway. Outlaw very nearly wins it back with a late brainbuster, but the hour expires just before the three-count. Darken crowns Lone Wolf the champion of the 1999 Final Friday and Outlaw the runner-up.

notes: Darken's own annual novelty tournament and birthday party — not a tracked WWA title, but a one-night, sixteen-competitor single-elimination bracket at Darken's own compound, with wrestlers bussed in and held overnight. Sixteen matches structured across four rounds plus the hour-long final. Big Mamma Jamma is shown being detained (and groped) by arena security in a backstage aside; Jack ("Famine" Jack, hospitalized after the prior week's events) sends a taped acceptance for a "Most Improved" award referenced only obliquely here.

name: WWA — 15 Feb 1999

matches.note: Both men's debuts. Jett wins with the "Immaculater," driving Lovejoy face-first into a steel chair.
Crosscheck pins Black Scorpion with the "Slapshot" clothesline after Coleman and Crosscheck put aside their own earlier feud to team up.

matches.stipulation: "I Love You" match — first to say it loses, thirty minutes, extreme rules
matches.note: Bruiser says "I love you" first after a Ragebomb on a table; Ravage pins him with a second Ragebomb onto scattered thumbtacks for good measure. The WWA's first "I Love You" match. A masked man interferes briefly with a whiskey bottle, unidentified.
Bob, now billed with the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse and wrestling in a purple dress with Bob's Driver at ringside, wins with "Bob's Move" after reversing an Eliem powerbomb attempt.

New Star, the advertised challenger, is ruled out with injuries from Final Friday; Lawrence Mack opens the title to any challenger, and Sniper answers. Jak Lancer runs in to attack Sniper with brass knuckles before leaving; Outlaw climbs the ladder unopposed to retain.

notes: The WWA Extreme brand's own weekly show, distinct from Wednesday Slam and Friday Night Fights. Opens on a MidCarder interview relitigating Darken's own scoring of Final Friday as a screwjob against Youthful Rage, then MidCarder is confronted at the top of the ramp by CPE (Denrol, Lantern, El Porto Spidero); the broadcast closes on a backstage aside of MidCarder burning a CPE letter and shirt, left ambiguous whether it's a rejection or a swerve.

name: WWA — 24 Feb 1999

matches.note: Debut of the tag team Maximum Overdrive against the Job Squad; wins with the "Overdriven" double-team finisher.
The WWA World Tag Team Champions ("the Young Guns") defeat House of Pain's Minnesota Wrecking Crew — MidCarder hits the "HoseHead," Kasanova follows with a Shooting Star Press for the pin.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship — No holds barred
matches.note: Griffin, defending as "Lone Wolf," loses the title to El Porto Spidero after Denrol runs in with a chair. New champion.

A slow-building match ends abruptly when Denrol's own cornerman Lantern inexplicably throws in the towel for him, handing O'Hara the win by default. Denrol cuts a post-match promo setting up a 2-out-of-3-falls rematch with O'Hara at March Madness.

notes: Opens on a backstage contract signing for a March Madness US Title match — Denrol refuses to sign against Gregory O'Hara outright, so Events Director Joe Stock orders a same-night towel-match qualifier instead. Lawrence Mack previews the coming Sunday's WWA Extreme card.

matches.note: A weapons brawl (baseball bat, steel stairs) ends when Crosscheck hits a top-rope elbow drop for the pin.
Walcott locks in the "Pretty Predicament" sharpshooter, but Dunnin reaches the ropes, then pulls out a "steel yo-yo" and busts Walcott open before finishing with a top-rope "Smoke Jump" splash.
After a 450 splash sends both men through a ringside table, Jett finishes Micheals with the top-rope "Immaculator."
A hardcore brawl (steel chairs, a baseball bat, a camera cable, the announce table) climaxes with Coleman hitting a fall-away DDT onto a chair and finishing Black Scorpion with a top-rope moonsault.

Bruiser hides under the ring before ambushing Ravage with a broken 2x4. Denrol wanders out and knocks both men down without clearly helping either side; the House of Pain then runs in — the Fan chokeslams referee Larry Crosier with the "Nightbringer," Todd Logan powerbombs Ravage, and Mantis hits the "Nut Cracker" off the top rope — before Zack Crockett, disguised as a referee, counts the pin for Bruiser and raises his hand. Bruiser retains.

matches.stipulation: Alexandra Korth accompanies Denrol; 30-minute time limit
matches.note: A hardcore brawl (camera cable choke, steel buckets, a chair shot off Denrol's landing on Gary Trudeau) goes the full 30 minutes to a time-limit draw.

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Hardcore Championship, no time limit; Mr. Agony seconds Lancer
matches.note: An extended brawl through the arena (a screwdriver, a barbed-wire bat, a popcorn machine, a glass door) ends on scaffolding roughly 30 feet above the ring: the Outlaw falls, and Lancer hits a Shooting Star Press off the scaffold to pin him and win the title. Both men are stretchered out; before leaving, a barely-conscious Lancer tells the referee "so it was written, so it was done," and the referee hands the belt to the Outlaw instead — the title returned to him on-air the same night. This pass leaves the promotion's own continuous Outlaw reign (wwa-extreme-hardcore-1998-outlaw, 1999-01-31 to 1999-04-09) as recorded rather than inserting a same-night interrupting reign for Lancer; see that reign's own note.

name: Friday Night Fights — 5 Mar 1999

matches.note: Crosscheck advances with the "Slapshot" flying clothesline.
Crockett advances with the "Spinebuster."
House of Pain (Randy Cross, Nick Bruiser, Mantis, the Fan) runs in and injures Eliem's knee; Cole gets the pin, then accepts a House of Pain shirt from Randy Cross, joining the stable.
Aric, cleared to wrestle too soon after a concussion suffered against Crosscheck the prior week, is finished quickly by the "Light in the Darkness" and taken out on a stretcher.
An upset — Annihilation wins with the "Crippler" (a running knee) after a long back-and-forth.
Kasanova wins with the "Kiss of Death" (a 450 splash) after countering a Diamond Cutter attempt.
A squash; Steihl wins with a 450 splash.

matches.stipulation: March Madness tournament, #16 seed vs. #1 seed
matches.note: Lazer's debut, managed by Athena — a much closer fight than the seeding suggested. Denrol wins with the "Evil Killer."

Griffin ("Lone Wolf") regains the title with the "DD Driver," distracted assistance from Ashley Dunnin (in street clothes, working the crowd against Spidero and CPE) proving decisive. Commentary notes Lone Wolf's in-ring style visibly reverting toward Griffin's own old moveset over the course of the match.

notes: The opening night of the WWA's 64-man World Heavyweight Championship tournament (Northern Region bracket), run alongside the separate, overlapping March Madness bracket. House of Pain adds Jon Cole via interference in the night's biggest angle; a House of Pain video package recaps its own championship history mid-show.

name: WWA — 7 Mar 1999

matches.stipulation: Southern Region tournament, round 1 (#2 vs. #15 seed)
matches.note: Spidero wins with the "Cross of Fire" (a 540 leg drop). Post-match, Albatross runs in on the fallen Mr. Business, only for Billy Coleman to run in and knock Albatross out with the "Deuces Are Wild" (a chair-assisted moonsault).

matches.stipulation: Southern Region tournament, round 1 (#3 vs. #14 seed)
matches.note: Lance Crash's debut — an upset win via a superkick that drives a steel chair into Bob's face for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Southern Region tournament, round 1 (#6 vs. #11 seed)
matches.note: A Lady Rachel interference attempt backfires (the Mimic dropkicks Michael's own shield into his face); the Mimic finishes Michael with Michael's own "Joust."

matches.stipulation: Southern Region tournament, round 1 (#7 vs. #10 seed)
matches.note: An unidentified masked man runs in to help Haggarty, double-chokeslamming and powerbombing Ken Steele before Haggarty finishes with a Choke Slam. Steele quits the WWA on camera immediately afterward, rebuffing President Mark Harrington and driving off.

Denrol's own CPE stable (Lantern, El Porto Spidero, a masked man) ambushes and straps Crosscheck to a stretcher before the bell; Denrol is declared the winner by forfeit and retains. Gregory O'Hara then runs in, scares Denrol off, and walks out with the title belt (not itself a title change).

notes: The Southern Region bracket of the 64-man World Heavyweight tournament. Ken Steele quitting on camera is a genuine roster departure, not resolved this show.

name: WWA — 10 Mar 1999

matches.note: Raiden wins cheaply, spitting something into ChiKylin's eyes before a powerbomb pin. Commentary questions whether Raiden is secretly connected to Anarchy.
Black Scorpion wins with the "Equalizer." Afterward, the Mimic (with Sir Michael) cuts a cryptic "crusade" promo at Lovejoy — the first sign of a Black Scorpion/Mimic/Sir Michael faction.
Shaman's return from a long absence, working singles (his own Maximum Overdrive partner Tony Richards isn't involved). Wins with the "Thunder Clap" spinning powerbomb.
Phoenix's debut. Outlaw, managed at ringside by Randy Cross, wins by DQ after MidCarder runs in and hits Outlaw with a chair.
The Commandant's Own upsets the Young Guns for the titles — Payne pins Kasanova with the "Arial Assault" after a long, evenly-fought match.

notes: Round 2 of the Southern Region bracket, plus a title-changing main event. The show opens on a recap montage of round-1 finishes. Corrects the ledger's own dated event for the WWA World Tag Team Championship change (see reigns.json note on wwa-world-tag-team-r007/r008): the fed's own title-history ledger cites 1999-03-12, but this show — a Wednesday Slam, staged and dated internally as such — is the one that actually stages the Commandant's Own's title win; the next chronological show (1999-03-12, a Friday Night Fights) references the upset in the past tense, confirming it already happened by then.

name: Friday Night Fights — 12 Mar 1999

matches.note: Chaos wins by countout, throwing Watson into the ring steps with a helicopter toss.
Daring wins with the "Daring Death Drop" off the top rope.
Goldstar, entered as a late replacement for the injured/unavailable Jak Lancer, wins by submission with the "Scream of Defeat" after his manager Elena knocks out the referee with a chair mid-hold.
Mantis wins with the "Shocker" (a second-rope fisherman's suplex).

notes: Round 1 of the Eastern Region bracket. Nick Bruiser cuts an interview promo challenging Ravage to a rematch. House of Pain (Randy Cross, Outlaw) records a video promo threatening Denrol over his win of their TV Title. The broadcast's own served text is incomplete: a sixth match (Misery vs. an unnamed opponent, teased as Sgt. Payne) is introduced but the document cuts off mid-entrance with no result — an honest gap, not resolved here.

name: WWA — 21 Mar 1999

matches.note: Rematch. Coleman wins with "Deuces Are Wild," a chair-assisted moonsault, and mocks Albatross and CPE on the mic afterward.
A brawl through the arena, food court, and a restroom — Jack II finishes Logan (blaming House of Pain for "Jack's" death) by dunking his head in a toilet before pinning him.

notes: A short two-match episode of WWA Sunday Night Extreme; the announcers note the tournament itself is dark this week.

name: WWA March Madness 99

matches.note: Nick Bruiser enters with a new bodyguard, Rage. Mantis wins with the "Nutcracker" (a flying headbutt).
Steihl wins with a 450 splash ("Rememberance of Pain").

A huge Crusade-vs-House-of-Pain brawl erupts outside as the Mimic and Outlaw fight; Jon Cole bails from a planned three-on-three before the bell. Outlaw wins with the Outlaw Kick after both men kick out of the other's finisher once.
Darken wins by an unnamed cross-face choke, forcing Griffin unconscious.

matches.stipulation: Rookie's Ring ten-man battle royal (over the top, guest commentator Rick Harrington)
matches.note: Timothy Micheals is taken out (and stretchered) by one Phoenix clothesline. Phoenix eliminates nearly everyone else, then — after finishing off Lance Crash with the "Phoenixbomb" and reaching a apparent win — voluntarily steps over the top rope and eliminates himself, leaving Lance Crash the winner and first Rookie's Ring holder, to the announcers' bafflement.
Darken wins with the "Dark Pogostick" (a bounced-head slam repeated three times).
Outlaw wins with the Outlaw Kick.

A long comedic match built around Denrol watching WrestleMania XV with Joe Stock on a side platform (including an extended "99 Bottles of Beer" singalong with the crowd) rather than wrestling. Shaman wins by DQ after Denrol repeatedly chair-shots him once the referee has already warned him — Denrol retains the title, as a DQ finish carries no title change.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament Final — winner earns one of four spots in a future Four Corners match for the vacant title
matches.note: A brutal main event; Outlaw wins by count-out after driving the ring steps into Darken's face. This crowns Outlaw the 64-man tournament winner and a Four Corners qualifier — not the title itself, which stays vacant pending that later match. House of Pain and Darken shake hands and help Outlaw from the ring afterward.

notes: March Madness, the WWA's own PPV closing the 64-man World Heavyweight tournament: Regional Finals, a ten-man Rookie's Ring battle royal, the Final Four, a United States Title defense, and the tournament final, which crowns a Four Corners qualifier rather than a new champion outright (the title stays vacant, per the fed's own build toward a later four-way match; consistent with wwa-world-heavyweight-r011's own later 1999-05-09 won date). The show closes on Youthful Rage's own rebirth: MidCarder's retirement is formalized, Ravage and a returning New Star (dealing with his father's cancer diagnosis in-story) both join Gregory O'Hara and Kris Kasanova as a reconstituted four-member stable.

name: WWA — 2 Apr 1999

matches.note: Interference from both House of Pain (the Mimic) and the Crusade watching ringside goes nowhere; Ravage wins by DQ after Crash uses a chair on the referee, retaining the belt.
Lazer wins with the "Lazer Cutter" (an inverted DDT).

A long, evenly-matched bout fought alongside a massive multi-faction brawl outside (House of Pain, the Crusade, Griffin/Dunnin/Rage, and Youthful Rage all fighting at once). Bruiser and O'Hara collide head-on going for simultaneous cross-bodies; Bruiser recovers first and falls on top for the accidental pin.
Denrol retains, finishing with the "CPE Elbow" after an "Evil Killer."
A time-limit draw — the Commandant's Own retain by default.

matches.stipulation: Six-man tag, House of Pain vs. the Crusade
matches.note: Jon Cole bails from the House of Pain trio before the bell, leaving Outlaw, Mantis and Logan. A masked, unmasked El Porto Spidero runs in mid-match to attack the Crusade with a chair, cryptically warning the Mimic ("you can't mimic what you can't see") — a swerve against his own former CPE allies. Logan pins Sir Michael for the win.

notes: Opens on a returning "Outlaw's Saloon" talk segment (Outlaw interviews Denrol, escalating to a shove and slap before security intervenes) previewing the Round Robin toward Pain Games, and an interview with the Commandant's Own that provokes Youthful Rage into a same-night title match. El Porto Spidero's own heel/face status is left genuinely ambiguous by the swerve in the main event.

name: WWA — 7 Apr 1999

matches.note: Micheals wins with a superkick.
Lazer wins with the "Lazer Cutter."

A makeup match for a cancelled Sunday Extreme card. Coleman, wrestling in honor of his late father, wins with "Aspen Extreme" and calls out New Star/Outlaw (whoever holds the Extreme Title) for a future shot.
A dominant Rage win — a ladder-assisted elbow drop through three stacked tables, then a boot-on-chest pin.
