"Pretty Boy" Troy Walcott, managed by the Executive, upsets Sir Michael with the "Pretty Plex."

matches.stipulation: Winner earns a WWA World Tag Team Championship shot this Friday
matches.note: Enfuego's first WWA win, Statler pinning Aric Crockett with "Plastic Surgery" (a facebuster).

notes: First show from the WWA's new home venue, the Continental Arena. President Harrington books a "Famine rules" match between Jack II and Steihl for the Famine role in the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse the following Friday — not staged in this session's own read shows, left an honest open thread. A House of Pain video vignette stages Mantis, the Crocketts, Jon Cole, Todd Logan and the Fan taking batting practice against a cameoing Andy Pettitte, threatening Griffin ahead of Pain Games.

name: WWA — 9 Apr 1999

matches.note: Aric Crockett interferes repeatedly at ringside; Crash wins anyway, hitting "Crash and Burn" on both Crockett and Cole.
Crosscheck busts Daring open with the hockey stick before finishing with his own "Crosscheck" clothesline.
Mantis wins the title with the "Nutcracker." New champion.
Black Scorpion reverses a Logan clothesline into a Crucifix pin for the win, despite Outlaw and the Mimic squaring off at ringside without incident.
Kasanova wins with a powerbomb; House of Pain runs in en masse afterward and beats Kasanova down until security and Youthful Rage intervene.
The Commandant's Own retain, finishing Statler with the "Terror From Above" (a top-rope/ground double-team combination).

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Championship — Cage Ladder match
matches.note: A chaotic main event drawing in nearly the full HOP and Youthful Rage rosters at ringside. New Star wins the title, then adds an unsanctioned moonsault onto Outlaw's stretcher after the bell.

notes: Opens on Flynn Steele's surprise return (his first appearance since the "F.E.A.R." era, era-extending flynn-steele's own tenure), interrupting a Denrol promo and challenging him to a US-vs-Canada flag match. Two title changes: Mantis takes the WWA World Television Championship from Ravage, and New Star wins the WWA Extreme Championship from Outlaw in the main event — see reigns.json for both.

name: WWA — 28 Apr 1999

matches.note: A five-second squash — Annihilation wins immediately with the "Crippler."
Jason Miller's debut; wins by submission with "The Truth," a dragon sleeper.

Lantern wins by count-out after Sir Michael's foot catches in loose ring-mat wire. A rematch (submission/pinfall only, winner gets a WWA Television Championship shot) is set for the following Wednesday.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship — Falls Count Anywhere, No DQ
matches.note: A brawl through the arena and up into the balcony; Mantis retains, hitting the "Nutcracker" off the balcony while wearing a stolen hard hat.

notes: The debut broadcast of a Rick Harrington-produced Wednesday Slam, with new co-host Steve Collen taking over from the regular trio for the night.

name: WWA — 2 May 1999

matches.note: Coleman wins with a Samoan drop and repeated cookie-pan shots.

House of Pain (Todd Logan, the Fan, Aric and Zack Crockett, then Outlaw) storms the ring before the bell and beats Crosscheck down; Lance Crash walks to the ring alongside Outlaw, an apparent defection to House of Pain. The match never starts.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship vs. WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship — Scaffold match
matches.note: Mantis, already working hurt on a bad ankle, falls fifteen feet off the scaffold after Griffin knocks him off balance; Griffin finishes with a "Swoop" (an inverted cross-body) more out of formality than competition, visibly concerned for Mantis's safety.

matches.stipulation: WWA United States Championship vs. WWA Extreme Championship — No time limit
matches.note: New Star wins by submission, handcuffing Ravage to the top rope in a "sideways surfboard" stretch until the referee stops it, then immediately frees him and raises his hand.

notes: Carries a House of Pain video-package retrospective of Outlaw's own past Rage in the Cage/Saturday Night Fights title wins (New England, Rhode Island, and Light Heavyweight-era belts) building toward May Mayhem's Four Corners match; that replayed footage is evidence for those original, earlier-dated events, not new matches on this show, and is not separately structured here per the anti-double-count rule.

name: WWA — 5 May 1999

matches.note: A five-second squash via the "Crippler." Afterward, producer Rick Harrington confronts Annihilation over the short match and is choked out, saved by Blaze — who blackmails his way into the show's own main event.
Both men's debuts; a clean match, ending when Xaviar reverses a "Decent" attempt into a small package.
Daniels wins with a brass-knuckles shot and pin.
Both men's debuts. An upset — Styles's girlfriend Jessica interferes twice (an eye poke, then holding Skull's feet down) to secure the pin.

matches.stipulation: Triple threat, Luche Libre tag-style entries — number-one contendership for the WWA World Television Championship
matches.note: Jack II (as "Blaze") knocks Lantern out with brass knuckles for the pin while Sir Michael, bloodied, is too slow to make the save. Blaze earns the Television Title shot at May Mayhem and promises the two losers a future Triple Threat Elimination shot at his own title if he wins it.

notes: Rick Harrington's second produced Wednesday Slam. Carries a lengthy backstage vignette (Darken and Steihl visiting Mark Harrington's office) reforming Darken and Steihl as a tag team under the "Overlords of the Dark" name, on the condition they earn any future title shot rather than being given one.

name: WWA May Mayhem 99

matches.stipulation: 26-man Rookie Rumble battle royal for the Rookie Ring, Championship, and a $15,000 bonus
matches.note: Phoenix, Rage and Flynn Steele (working as "Darkstorm and Steele") team up early to clear house. Styles pays off Alex Adams mid-match to bodyguard him; the Sitcom Fathers paddle Adams for breaking their own declared rules, then take ringside seats. Styles is legitimately hobbled by a knee injury mid-match but returns to steal Jessica's purse and knock out the exhausted Flynn Steele — the final elimination — to win. Afterward the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse reveal the Preacher of Pain as their new Pestilence, replacing Raven Crow, who steps down in a formal, music-free handover.
Crosscheck wins with the "Slapshot," then is beaten down and stretchered out by House of Pain (Todd Logan, Aric Crockett, Zack Crockett, the Fan, Lance Crash, and a masked HOP member) after the bell.
Steihl replaces the scheduled Darken without explanation and wins by submission with "Remembrance of Pain" (a modified full nelson) over a visibly troubled O'Hara.

Spidero refuses the match outright on the mic, showing off a $50,000 payoff from Denrol for standing down. Denrol then wrestles Griffin himself in a chicken costume, tagging in and out with two more chicken-suited men (revealed afterward as Joe Stock and Joey Edwards). Griffin retains, pinning one of the chickens after New Star runs in and clears out the others with a chair.
An extended hardcore brawl through the crowd and up onto the jumbotron staging, ending when Shaman hits New Star with a "Thunderclap" off the jumbotron through three tables. New champion.
Anarchy (managed by Havoc) regains the titles with direct outside help from Malkav Amaranth, who blindsides both champions and holds a leg for the deciding pin.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship — Four Corners elimination, vacant title, special guest referee Nikodemous Segier
matches.note: Kasanova and Outlaw secretly agree mid-match to eliminate Coleman and Ravage together with simultaneous finishers, then Outlaw wins the final fall over Kasanova after Segier's own wife Jennifer knocks Kasanova out with her purse on cue — revealing Segier, brought in as an ostensibly neutral guest referee, was secretly working for House of Pain all along. Outlaw becomes the new WWA World Heavyweight Champion.

notes: May Mayhem, the WWA's own PPV crowning a new World Heavyweight Champion after the title sat vacant since Randy Cross's retirement (wwa-world-heavyweight-r010's own 1999-02-26 close). Opens on a running backstage betting-pool angle (Denrol taking odds on the main event) threaded through the whole broadcast. Three title changes recovered: WWA Extreme (Shaman over New Star), WWA World Tag Team (Anarchy over the Commandant's Own — already correctly tracked pre-existing, confirmed against the served card), and the vacant WWA World Heavyweight Championship itself (Outlaw, already correctly tracked pre-existing as wwa-world-heavyweight-r011, confirmed against the served card). The Nikodemous Segier heel turn is the show's own biggest angle.

name: WWA — 14 May 1999

matches.note: Daniels wins the Ring with "Love Sick" (a running gutwrench powerbomb).
The Commandant's Own wins with "Terror From Above."
Hayes wins with the "Mercy Killing" after his manager Skid knocks Adams out with a cane while the referee is distracted.
Bullet wins by submission with "the Interrogation," after knocking the Beast out with brass knuckles mid-match.
The Sitcom Fathers win when both Crocketts tap simultaneously to a double submission (a figure four and a sharpshooter).

A grudge match rooted in the two men's pre-WWA history together. Lantern wins with "Light in the Darkness." Afterward Blaze attacks Lantern in apparent retaliation for his guest-commentary role in Blaze's loss to Mantis, but Albatross — despite the rivalry just settled — turns and chairs Blaze to protect Lantern.
A rematch, evening their season series 1-1; Payne wins with the "Ground Assault."
Kasanova wins with the "Kiss of Death," then calls out Griffin for a WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship shot.

notes: A video segment confirms Randy Cross and Nik Segier planned Segier's heel turn together in advance, with Jennifer Segier's own purse shot pre-arranged — though Outlaw is described as needing "time" to fully accept Segier back into the fold.

name: WWA — 19 May 1999

matches.note: Goodman's debut win, finishing with the "Flashback" (a springboard guillotine legdrop).
Styles wins with a hidden pair of brass knuckles, unseen by the referee.
The Preacher of Pain wins with "The Decent."

Logan attacks before the bell with a hard cast on his arm, then finishes Steele with a chair-assisted powerbomb after the referee has already called for the bell — a chaotic finish with no clean winner. A massive brawl follows: a new anti-House-of-Pain alliance (Griffin, Shaman, Gutter, the Mimic, Sir Michael, Master Xaviar) confronts a huge House of Pain contingent (Outlaw, Nik Segier, Mantis, Lance Crash, the Crocketts, the Fan, a masked HOP member); the broadcast cuts off mid-brawl, unresolved.

notes: Ant Banks and Dr. Slash Hayes refuse their own scheduled match on the mic mid-show, declaring "we call the shots now" — a genuine cancelled bout, not resolved. A House of Pain merchandise segment doubles as an angle, with Jennifer Segier now fully aligned with the stable.

name: WWA — 26 May 1999

matches.note: Live tag match. Goodman pins Death Warrior with the "Flashback" while Tracer Bullet is still arguing a missed tag with the referee.

matches.stipulation: Handicap; the Preacher of Pain is also billed alongside a benched Paul Styles pre-match, but only PoP wrestles
matches.note: The Fraternity (Lazer, Walcott) wins as Lazer hits a Rock Bottom on the Preacher of Pain on the entrance ramp after a two-on-one beatdown.

matches.stipulation: Shaman's partner Flynn Steele is kidnapped and chained up before the match, leaving him alone
matches.note: The Magician's WWA debut. He turns on his own partner Coleman mid-match, hitting the "Phantasmal Killer" (a sunset flip powerbomb) and pinning Coleman onto Shaman for the win — with House of Pain (the Crocketts, Mantis, Lance Crash, Outlaw, Nik Segier, the Fan, a masked member) swarming the match throughout. Flynn Steele breaks free of his restraints and runs in post-match, driving House of Pain off with a lead pipe.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — non-title
matches.note: Anarchy (managed by Havoc) wins with Raiden's "Somersault Whiplash Diamond Bomb," aided by an outside chair shot and a Chaos chokeslam on Sgt. Payne.

matches.stipulation: Prelude to the Four Corners match; television time remaining
matches.note: A chaotic finish — Denrol has Segier covered after an "Evil Killer" when House of Pain (Mantis, Lance Crash, the Crocketts, a masked member, the Fan) storms the ring and the referee calls for the bell with no decision.

notes: A two-hour broadcast mixing live matches with jumbotron replays of five matches from an unrecovered "Sunday Extreme" episode (c. 1999-05-23) — those replayed matches are structured on a separate, museum-compiled show row (wwa-1999-05-23) per the anti-double-count rule, not here. Opens on a genuine backstage angle: Todd Logan attacks Phoenix with a lead pipe in a parking lot, hospitalizing him and cancelling a planned Extreme Title match.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship, 15-minute time limit
matches.note: Jack II (as "Blaze") comes to ringside during the match; Lantern runs in and drags him off to brawl through the crowd. Distracted, Mantis nearly has Daniels beaten, but the rookie Ring of Harts champion catches him in an inside cradle for the pin — a huge upset title change. Mantis demands (and is promised) a rematch.
Alex Adams dominates in his second WWA match, finishing Cyber Skull with a Tombstone Piledriver.
Goodman dominates FTW throughout, finishing with his "Flashback."

matches.stipulation: The Crusade (Sir Michael, Lady Rachel) second Xaviar — first meeting between the Crusade and the Fraternity since Billy Coleman helped the Fraternity in a recent Extreme tag match
matches.note: Lazer submits Xaviar to a Camel Clutch. Afterward the Crusade — the Mimic, Black Scorpion, and a hooded, spell-chanting figure (the Magician) — jump Lazer three-on-one until Troy Walcott and "Rolemodel" Paul Styles run in with chairs for the Fraternity to even the numbers.

Paul Styles bails out early to flirt with a fan at ringside; Tracer Bullet, disgusted with the farce, walks away from the match entirely. The Preacher of Pain finishes Ant Banks alone with "The Decent" powerbomb before Styles can make the save.

matches.stipulation: Four Corners Elimination match; the winner faces the Outlaw for the WWA World Heavyweight Championship later in the show

eliminations.note: Darken leaves the ring to chase down a heckling crowd member ("Bob"), beats him down at ringside with a "Dark Pogostick," and is hauled off by security and medics, effectively removing him from the match.
Pinned by the "Denrol Elbow" after Nikodemous Segier low-blows Denrol in retaliation for earlier interference.
Pinned by a Northern Lights suplex after Denrol is distracted mid-DDT setup by the sight of Jennifer Segier's sister cheering him on at ringside.

matches.note: Segier wins his singles return match, advancing to face the Outlaw for the World Heavyweight Championship.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship, television time remaining
matches.note: A hard-fought, largely clean main event; the Outlaw fights off Segier's figure-four with the clock running out, and the bell sounds mid-hold for a time-limit draw as the House of Pain floods the ring. The Outlaw retains.
A squash win for Tracer Bullet, finishing with the ringpost submission hold "the Interrogation."
Sangha's WWA singles debut (billed "Suneil Sangha"); he finishes Ice Tank with the "Canadian Death Lock."

matches.stipulation: Ice Tank answers an open challenge Andy Madison issues from the ring
matches.note: Andy Madison's WWA debut, wrestled in 8:12; Madison, giving up nearly 100 pounds and 8 inches, finishes Ice Tank (already worn down from his earlier match) with a moonsault after a superkick.

The Magician attacks Jon Cole before the bell, blinding him with a powder toss and beating him down with a weighted glove before finishing him with the "Phantasmal Killer" (a sunset flip powerbomb) for a count-out.
Goodman wins in 23 seconds flat with a superkick into his "Flashback" finisher.

Hayes feigns a back injury to lure Washington in, then Skid pulls down the ropes to spill Washington to the floor and clubs him with a golf club (a "9 iron") while the referee is distracted, leading to a count-out win for Hayes.

A screwy, faction-heavy rematch: Paul Styles and Jessica are chased off by Todd Logan and the Crocketts before they can reach ringside; later Steihl and Darken (Four Horsemen) approach the ring, freezing the House of Pain in place, and Denrol runs in to cowbell Daniels before Mantis rolls him in for the pin. The Horsemen (Darken, Steihl, Blaze, the Preacher of Pain) then storm the ring and brawl with the House of Pain — Darken injures Randy Cross with his staff before the Outlaw and Nik Segier fight him off — and in the chaos, "Blaze" (Jack II) ends up walking off with the physical TV title belt.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship; Malkav Amaranth seconds Anarchy; television time remaining
matches.note: An unnamed hooded, bald interloper appears at ringside partway through and fights off Malkav Amaranth's and Anarchy's attempted interference with kicks and staff strikes, clearing the way for the Commandant's Own to finish Raiden with the combination "Ground Assault"/"Terror from Above" (billed together as the "Full Frontal Assault") for the titles.
A huge upset: Spike, both men's WWA debuts, wins with a springboard moonsault after a belly-to-back suplex.
An unnamed man in a trenchcoat and gumshoe hat drags Joey Edwards to the ring and dumps him in; Segier pins him with a single foot for an easy three-count and leaves without further comment.

matches.stipulation: Dr. Hayes's own arbitrarily-signed comedy match; billed as "Master Xavier" but actually Skid in ill-fitting papier-mache armor
matches.note: A pure comedy segment: Hayes shoves the costumed Skid over with one hand and counts the pin himself.
A showcase squash for Bruiser, finishing with a Russian leg sweep after Internet briefly rallies with a thumb to the eye and a DDT.

matches.stipulation: The Knighthood, seconded by Lady Rachel, vs. the returning Overlords of the Dark (Darken and Steihl); 20-minute time limit
matches.note: The Overlords dominate, finishing Sir Michael with a new "Touch of Death" combination (a Steihl hurricanrana into a Darken upside-down suplex) for the pin. Afterward Steihl locks Michael in the "Reverence of Pain" until Yes strips Lady Rachel's dress off at ringside and Michael, in pain, says "Mickey Likes It" to end the hold.
Gotham targets Micheals's left knee throughout (including hurling a TV monitor onto it) and finishes him with a figure four leglock submission.

matches.stipulation: Bullet, disguised as Goodman, brings a celebrity guest corner man (a 1970s sitcom actor known for playing a wisecracking student) for one night only
matches.note: The real Goodman storms the ring and it turns into a four-way brawl. Washington and Adams try to gang up on Goodman, but Goodman fights them off and finishes Adams with a superkick into the "Flashback" for the win. The arriving Fraternity (Troy Walcott, Tommy Lazer, "Rolemodel" Paul Styles) chases off Bullet's guest and, on the mic afterward, accepts a grateful Goodman as a pledge.

matches.stipulation: A grudge match, billed as Flynn Steele vs. "Blaze"
matches.note: The arena goes dark before the bell; when the lights come up, Jack II — now presenting as "Famine," a Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse persona — is standing over a fallen Steele and rolls him up for the pin as the other three Horsemen (Darken, Steihl, the Preacher of Pain) and Yes look on from the stage. A cloaked rider then enters, beats Famine down with a staff, and is revealed as Mantis, who finishes him with the "Shocker," burns the Horsemen robe and staff in the ring, and reclaims his own WWA World Television Championship belt. Todd Logan and the Magician run in to help Mantis escape as the rest of the Horsemen storm the ring; unable to catch the fleeing House of Pain, the Horsemen instead turn on the still-fallen, uninvolved Flynn Steele as a "sacrifice," brutalizing him with their "Touch of Death" combination (a Steihl gutwrench powerbomb and moonsault into a Darken press-slam piledriver) while Preacher of Pain recites scripture and Darken cuts a promo declaring war on the promotion's established order. Steele is stretchered out and taken to the hospital.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship; Jessica seconds Styles, who brings roughly twenty hired security personnel to ringside; Randy Cross confronts Styles before the bell and is hauled off by Styles's own guards after Styles shoves him
matches.note: Mantis dominates throughout. Late in the match Styles grabs a nightstick from one of his own hired guards and cracks Mantis with it while the referee is distracted by Jessica, but another "security guard" knocks Styles out cold before he can finish the job and is unmasked afterward as Tracer Bullet in disguise, letting Mantis fall on top of Styles for the pin and the retain.

A back-and-forth match interrupted mid-way by Kris Kasanova running in with a baseball bat; Ravage fights him off and spears him out of the ring after Coleman inadvertently knocks out the referee. Ravage finishes Coleman with the "Ragebomb" to retain, then the two shake hands after the bell.

matches.stipulation: Light Heavyweight Royal Rumble — 14 men, one entrant per minute over the top rope; the winner faces Griffin (or whoever holds the Light Heavyweight Championship by then) at Independence Day Rumble; Lady Rachel seconds Sir Michael

eliminations.note: Scoop-slammed out almost as soon as he entered.
Worked over repeatedly with a steel folding chair.
Tossed out, chair and all.
Eliminated by a double clothesline from Segier and Lantern together almost immediately after entering.
Finished off with the "Light in the Darkness."
Hip-tossed out.
The 12th draw was a mystery cloaked entrant who tripped over his own robe and stumbled straight into Segier, who tossed him out immediately; not otherwise a real factor in the match.
Tossed with an assist from the debuting Lance Crash.
Scooped and tossed moments after entering.
Blinded with a handful of salt to the eyes, then tossed.

Not eliminated in the ring — attacked outside it by the same disguised mystery entrant from earlier, revealed this time as the suspended Denrol ("Father Denrol"), who marks his forehead with an ash cross and vanishes; the referees rule him unable to continue.
Ravage runs in with a bat and swings at Segier but misses; Segier picks up the dropped bat and clotheslines Kasanova out to win.

matches.note: Nik Segier wins, earning a Light Heavyweight Championship shot at Independence Day Rumble.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship; Todd Logan and the Magician second the Outlaw
matches.note: The Outlaw brass-knuckles Shaman from the crowd before the bell and finishes him late with the Outlaw Kick to retain. Afterward the Magician challenges Shaman to a WWA Extreme Hardcore Championship match at the upcoming Independence Day Rumble PPV. Denrol (on his suspension) taunts the Outlaw via the jumbotron and denies any involvement as the broadcast cuts to a shot of Randy Cross's mansion on fire.
A hardcore brawl (a chair, a baseball bat, a cookie pan, pepper thrown in the eyes) ends with Hayes's "Mercy Killing" (a Michinoku Driver variant) for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Billed "Commando" Nick Bruiser; both men are also scheduled to meet again at Independence Day Rumble
matches.note: Bruiser finishes Havok with a spinning chokeslam.

A hardcore brawl (marbles, a broken bottle, a baseball bat, a Super Soaker, brass knuckles, barbed wire, thumbtacks) ends when Coleman hits his new "Death Mountain Drop" superplex, driving Shaman down onto a bed of thumbtacks, for the pin and the title.

matches.stipulation: Wrestled before the broadcast's own start and recapped by the announcers
matches.note: A countout win for Joey Edwards.

Grinnin's WWA debut. A slingshot splash attempt carries Grinnin's own momentum over Spike, rolling Spike on top for the pin — Grinnin kicks out right as the count hits three, but the referee sticks with the call.
Two Scoops, a former boxer, finishes Mr. Internet with a submission he calls the "Absolute Zero."

matches.stipulation: SEAL's WWA debut, representing the Commandant's Own
matches.note: SEAL wins in 3:49 with a top-rope finisher he calls "the Fourth SEAL."

matches.stipulation: The Executive seconds Walcott; a very drunk Chad Goodman and Tommy Lazer are also at ringside for the Fraternity; the winner of a pre-match altercation between the two locker rooms determines nothing official
matches.note: A long, hard-fought main event. Bullet finishes Walcott with "Case Closed" (a modified piledriver) but the referee is distracted by the Executive at the cover; the Executive then slides in his briefcase for Walcott, whose swing misses, and Bullet kicks it away. Later, Goodman pulls down the top rope to spill Bullet to the floor headfirst into the guardrail, knocking him out; Walcott finishes with the "Pretty Plex" as Mantis and Todd Logan brawl at ringside with the Executive and Tommy Lazer. Security (led by new WWA Commissioner Tony Bailey) breaks it up, but one of Bailey's own guards is seen kicking Walcott's downed arm onto the also-unconscious Bullet for the pin. Bailey rules the finish clean except for Goodman's rope-pull, fining Goodman $5,000 and signing him to a steel cage match against Bullet at Canada Day Mania.
Two Scoops submits the much bigger Rage with the "Absolute Zero," a huge upset.

matches.stipulation: Preacher of Pain was originally scheduled against Daniels, but Commissioner Tony Bailey announces Preacher's suspension and replaces the opponent before the match
matches.note: A visibly unhappy Blake Daniels squashes the Crimson Warrior, finishing with his new running gutwrench powerbomb, "The Love Sick." The Crimson Warrior is stretchered out.

matches.stipulation: Crucifix Match — no time limit, ends only when one man is strapped to the crucifix; billed as the Magician vs. "Father Denrol"
matches.note: A body-double stunt opens the match: a decoy "Father Denrol" is exposed and dragged off by druids alongside Todd Logan, who ran in to help the Magician. The real Father Denrol and the Magician then fight an increasingly dangerous brawl (a chair, a ladder, a moonsault off the ladder that puts Denrol through the crucifix itself) before Denrol finishes the Magician with the "Evil Killer" for the pin. Both men are stretchered out.

matches.stipulation: The Crusade (the Mimic and Black Scorpion) vs. the Overlords of the Dark (Darken and Steihl), seconded by Yes; 30-minute time limit
matches.note: A brutal, stunt-heavy tag match (a bungee-cord splash, a table spot off a trampoline) ends when Darken finishes the Mimic with the "Dark Pogostick" for the pin.

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Hardcore Championship, 30-minute time limit; no disqualification, no countout — a double-down is ruled a double knockout draw
matches.note: Coleman had spent the entire broadcast disguised as fill-in ring announcer "Todd Smith," revealing himself to ambush Bruiser at the bell. A brutal weapons brawl follows (kendo sticks, a dumpster full of weapons, a fire extinguisher, the ring bell, the announce table) until both men go down simultaneously and the referee counts a double ten-count. Coleman retains under the promotion's own double-knockout rule.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship — Cole Miner's Glove rules (a loaded glove hangs above one corner; no disqualification, no countout); billed as "Blaze" (a Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse persona)
matches.note: A long, physical title match that ends when Blaze locks in a modified cobra clutch he calls the "Neverending Starvation" for the submission. The rest of the Four Horsemen (Darken, Steihl, the Preacher of Pain) then storm the ring, reveal Blaze as one of their own, and turn the post-match beatdown on Mantis as a "sacrifice" — Steihl applies the "Remembrance of Pain" while Darken recites a scripted sermon, before Blaze himself splashes onto Steihl to end it as the group leaves together. Mantis is stretchered out.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship; Alpha Omega (Walcott and Lazer) seconded by Chad Goodman
matches.note: Blake Daniels runs in to even the odds for the champions against interference, but the full House of Pain (Cross, the Fan, the Crocketts, Todd Logan, Nik Segier, the Outlaw, a masked HOP member) storms the ring and beats down both challengers; the match is ruled a disqualification win for Alpha Omega, but the titles remain with the Commandant's Own under the promotion's own no-title-change-on-DQ convention.

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Hardcore Championship — Coleman defends against a masked "Mystery Man"
matches.note: The Outlaw reveals that Coleman's challenger slot legally belongs to the Magician under a prior stipulation, adding him to the match; Nick Bruiser, present at ringside to heckle, is dragged in as a fourth man after the Magician fireballs him. A chaotic brawl (vodka bottle, camera cords, a chair) ends when a groggy Coleman falls on top of the Magician for the pin. Afterward Coleman unmasks the "Mystery Man" as the returning Duke Daring, who vows revenge.

matches.stipulation: WWA Light Heavyweight Championship; Kris Kasanova is guest referee
matches.note: A fast, competitive title match; Segier twists Griffin's mask around blinding him mid-move, then finishes with a sloppy "Title Winner" for the pin and the title.

matches.stipulation: WWA United States Championship — Ravage wrestles on the same day he's released from the hospital, and stakes his own WWA career on the outcome
matches.note: A brutal, hard-fought title defense; Steihl finishes Ravage with the "Remembrance of Pain" submission to retain. Ravage is stretchered out.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship — Texas Bullrope match (win by dragging your opponent to all four corners in order); billed against Denrol, but Denrol never arrives and Father Denrol wrestles in his place
matches.note: Todd Logan and the Magician run in for the Outlaw, drawing out Darken and Steihl of the Four Horsemen, who choke-slam Logan through a table and spear the Magician — but then, unexpectedly, Steihl staffs Father Denrol across the head rather than helping him, letting the Outlaw finish dragging him to the fourth corner for the win. Darken cuts a promo claiming the Horsemen now "own" the Outlaw's soul. The real Denrol then arrives late with Melissa "Missy" Camero, disputes that "Father Denrol" was ever entitled to defend his title, and brawls with new temporary Commissioner Peter Gray's security before being hauled off; the promotion's own ledger records the title as having changed hands to the Outlaw this show regardless.

matches.stipulation: 60-man Royal Rumble — one entrant per minute, over-the-top-rope-and-both-feet-down elimination; the winner earns a WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot against the Outlaw. Sgt. Matthew Payne forfeited his drawn spot and did not appear.

eliminations.note: Both men blind each other with salt at the same moment; Father Denrol recovers first and dropkicks Denrol out.
Bullet, disguised as the match's own referee, pulled the top rope down as Goodman entered, spilling him out.
Sent over by a dropkick that also nearly caught Tracer Bullet, who saved himself on the rope.
Eliminated in a group effort with the Sitcom Fathers and Andy Madison.
Eliminated in the same group effort as Rage.
Pulled out along with both Sitcom Fathers when his own manager and brother, Jazz Madison, grabbed Mr. Seever and all three fell to the floor together.
Eliminated in the same three-man pileup as Andy Madison.
Eliminated in the same three-man pileup as Andy Madison.
Backdropped over the top.
Dropped over the ropes.
Darken shoves both Shaman and the Magician over the top while they brawl with each other; both are later taken away by security while continuing to fight on the floor.
Eliminated in the same push as Shaman.
A total fluke: Spike, holding the ropes for balance, is knocked backward by Darken and inadvertently sends him over — the single biggest upset of the match.
Another accident: Spike trips and stumbles into him, sending him out.
Ducked a charge, sending Edwards over.
Thrown out by the returning Duke Daring, revealed earlier that night as the Extreme title match's "Mystery Man."
Self-eliminated, following Coleman out to keep beating on him at ringside.
Sent out, and dragged Sir Michael (whose hair he was still holding) out with him.
Pulled out by his own hair, still locked in Lazer's grip.
Sidekicked out shortly after entering.
Press-slammed out.
Charges Troy Walcott and both men fly over the top together, eliminating the Fraternity's last man in the match.
Eliminated in the same double-elimination as Logan.
Dropped over the ropes out of a suplex attempt.
Fled from a charging Steihl, jumping over the top rope himself and out of the match — ruled eliminated for leaving under his own power.
Hauled over the top by Tracer Bullet and Griffin together, one leg apiece.
Double-clotheslined out along with Griffin.
Eliminated in the same double-clothesline as Tracer Bullet.
Dropkicked over along with Kasanova, but only Segier failed to save himself on the apron.
The final elimination — Lantern swung down from the top rope and pushed Kasanova off the apron to win the match, having entered as the sixth man and outlasted fifty-nine others.

matches.note: Lantern, the sixth man drawn, outlasts fifty-nine others — including a sustained mid-match rampage by Darken that was ended only by a fluke accidental elimination at the hands of Spike — to win, earning a shot at the Outlaw's newly-reclaimed World Heavyweight Championship.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship; Skid seconds Hayes; billed as "Blaze"
matches.note: A hardcore-tinged title defense (a chair shot from Skid, Skid getting caught interfering) ends with Blaze's "BlazeBreaker" finisher for the pin.
Thornhill submits Escariot with "The Adrenaline Rush."
Walcott reverses Micheals's attempted superkick into an ankle lock, then finishes with the "Pretty Plex."

matches.stipulation: A comedy "special match," announced live by WWA President Mark Harrington; Johny Morhouse is the guest referee; Ricky and Mark Harrington fill in on commentary
matches.note: Commentator Terry Valentine is dragged into the ring to face Spike, who dominates from bell to bell and finishes with a piledriver for the pin.

matches.stipulation: The Sitcom Fathers are accompanied by "Alf"
matches.note: A brawl-filled tag match, briefly restarted after it spills outside; the Sitcom Fathers finish with a simultaneous double submission, Mr. Brady's figure four on Jazz Madison and Mr. Seever's "Growing Pains" on Andy Madison. Afterward the Fury brothers (Brian and Stephan) run in and beat the Sitcom Fathers down.

A mismatch that Lazer fights hard in anyway; Preacher finishes with "The Decent." Blaze and Ant Banks (Four Horsemen) run in during the match, drawing out the Fraternity (Troy Walcott, Chad Goodman) for a brawl at ringside; Lazer low-blows Preacher from behind afterward before the Fraternity clears out through the crowd.

matches.stipulation: WWA Light Heavyweight Championship; Jennifer Segier and Randy Cross second the champion
matches.note: Segier is disqualified for an eye gouge; he and his corner mock Denrol and leave rather than contest it, and Denrol is left fuming in the ring. Segier retains under the promotion's own no-title-change-on-DQ convention.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship; billed as "Blaze"
matches.note: A competitive title match is thrown out when the rest of the Four Horsemen (Darken, Steihl, the Preacher of Pain) run in and attack Goodman. A huge brawl follows — the Fraternity (Tommy Lazer, Troy Walcott), Blake Daniels, and a surprise run-in from Griffin all get involved against the Horsemen — until security (which the Horsemen also fight) breaks it up. Blaze retains under the promotion's own no-title-change-on-DQ convention.

The Magician runs in and blindsides SEAL with a double axe handle, drawing a disqualification; Logan and the Magician then beat down both SEAL and Havok together, marking their unofficial debut as a new House of Pain tag pairing.
Spidero lures Lazer into a plexiglass sheet set up during a commercial break, then finishes him with the "Fisherman's Buster" after a hard-fought back-and-forth.

Walcott has the Mimic beat with his own "Pretty Plex," but the Mimic reverses a suplex attempt into a Gord Buster and finishes with Walcott's own "Pretty Plex" right back at him. The rest of the Crusade (Black Scorpion, Sir Michael, Master Xaviar) runs in afterward to triple-team Walcott until the Fraternity storms out with weapons and the Crusade retreats through the crowd.

A hard-fought, largely clean match; Lantern is distracted when the Outlaw, Nikodemous Segier, and Randy Cross appear at ringside, and Tracer Bullet rolls him up for the win — revealed as Bullet's formal, if unofficial, arrival in the House of Pain.
Kasanova survives an early near-fall off a springboard hurricanrana before finishing Thornhill with the top-rope "Kiss of Death."

matches.stipulation: The Sitcom Fathers are seconded by "Alf"; the Overlords of the Dark by Yes
matches.note: The Overlords dominate throughout (Yes distracts Alf with a kitten at ringside partway through) and finish both Fathers in succession with the "Touch of Death," the second version on Mr. Seever after the pin on Mr. Brady.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship; SEAL seconds the champions; Denrol and the Outlaw team under a standing contractual obligation between them
matches.note: Visible friction between Denrol and the Outlaw runs through the whole match (Outlaw stalling on tags, at one point walking off for a drink of water). Denrol sets the Outlaw up to hit a spike piledriver on Sgt. Payne for the finish, but Payne reverses it into a hurricanrana on Denrol as Havok recovers and the champions finish the Outlaw with the "Air Assault"/"Terror From Above" combination to retain. Afterward the Outlaw slaps Denrol; Denrol then calls for a mic and announces he has exercised a 30-day walkout clause to leave the WWA for the East Coast Wrestling Alliance.
Two Scoops wins with a rollup after taking several chair shots from Gotham.
A brutal weapons brawl (a two-by-four, a CD player, a steel chair) ends when Rage chokeslams Chaos onto a steel chair for the pin. Chaos is stretchered out.

matches.stipulation: Skid seconds Hayes; Nick Bruiser, WrestleSoft's "Chairman of the Board," coaches Hayes backstage beforehand
matches.note: A hardcore brawl (a green mist, a TV camera used as a weapon, multiple chair shots) in which Bruiser himself comes to ringside mid-match to berate Hayes for holding back; Hayes finishes Micheals with the "Mercy Killing" onto a chair.

matches.stipulation: Lady Rachel and Master Xaviar second Sir Michael
matches.note: Master Xaviar interferes repeatedly at ringside (a facebuster, a backbreaker) to help Sir Michael, who finishes Father Denrol with a spinebuster into "The Joust" for the pin.
A hard-fought match; Daniels turns Black Scorpion's own reverse DDT back on him before finishing with "The Love Sick." The Crusade chases Daniels off through the crowd afterward.

A hardcore, weapon-heavy brawl (a staff, powder down Daring's pants, a textbook, camera wires, a lead pipe) ends when the Magician hits three straight "Phantasmal Killer" finishers; the referee stops the match rather than count, ruling Daring unable to continue. Daring is taken out by ambulance.

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Hardcore Championship — Ladder Match, the belt hung above the ring
matches.note: Bruiser no-shows his entrance, then ambushes Coleman disguised as a fan in the front row. A hardcore ladder match follows (kendo sticks, thumbtacks, barbed wire, a blowtorch used to collapse a ladder out from under Bruiser, handcuffs pinning Bruiser to the guardrail) before Coleman climbs a second, hidden ladder and cuts the belt down with a throwing star to retain. Afterward Kristopher Kasanova, El Porto Spidero, and New Star (Youthful Rage) come to the ring and recruit Coleman into the stable on the spot.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship; billed as "Blaze"
matches.note: Steihl and the Preacher of Pain come to ringside uninvited; Blaze waves them off, but shoves Steihl when he won't leave, and an angry Steihl decks his own ally — the distraction lets Lantern hit "The Light in the Darkness" for the pin and the title. The full Four Horsemen then swarm Lantern in retaliation, beating him down with the belt itself and powerbombing him head-first into the turnbuckle before fleeing security. Lantern is stretchered out; a later backstage update shows him disoriented but conscious, vowing (before medication visibly overtakes him) to defend the title against all comers and to challenge the Horsemen to a 4-on-1 handicap match.
Wish wins his singles debut with a top-rope 450 splash he calls "The Last Wish."

matches.stipulation: WWA Rookie Ring; Major Havok seconds SEAL
matches.note: Before the match, Dr. Slash Hayes — having stolen the Rookie Ring from Two Scoops in a backstage beatdown moments earlier — hands it back to its rightful holder Sangha. SEAL finishes Sangha with the top-rope "Fourth SEAL" for the pin and the title.

matches.stipulation: Skid seconds Bruiser and Hayes; the Sitcom Fathers are seconded by "Alf"
matches.note: Bruiser and Hayes abandon the match and leave ringside once the full Crusade (the Mimic, Black Scorpion, Sir Michael, Master Xaviar) runs in and beats down the Sitcom Fathers, answering their standing challenge from weeks earlier.

matches.stipulation: "Bourbon Street Brawl" — no rules, fought through the streets of New Orleans and eventually into Tracer Bullet's own apartment building and office
matches.note: An extended hardcore chase brawl (a mailbox, a parking meter, a voodoo doll, Tracer's own office) finishes with the "Case Closed" for the pin. Tracer then pays off the match's referee with cash from his own office safe and unmasks him on camera as the Preacher of Pain, revealing the two had been working together all along — Tracer's way of repaying the Preacher for the earlier $4,000 fine.
The Preacher of Pain, fresh off doubling as the referee in the previous match, finishes Coleman with a superplex through two stacked tables to win the title.

matches.stipulation: Non-title; Yes seconds the Overlords of the Dark
matches.note: The Sitcom Fathers run in to attack Steihl with kendo sticks mid-match, drawing Yes into the fray; the rest of the Four Horsemen (Blaze, the Preacher of Pain) then arrive and arm Darken with a staff. SEAL runs out to defend the Commandant's Own, blocking Darken's swing and squaring off with him staff-to-staff as the broadcast runs out of time with the match still unresolved.
Spike wins with an inside cradle, extending his winning streak to five.
Wish works the Crimson Warrior's knee throughout, finishing with a figure four leglock.

matches.stipulation: Billed as "the JOB Squad" (Mr. Internet and Tim Powers) vs. the Sitcom Fathers, substituting for a scheduled Blue Chips vs. JOB Squad bout after the Fury brothers stopped working for the WWA; Alf seconds the Sitcom Fathers
matches.note: Mr. Seever finishes Mr. Internet with the "Growing Pain" submission for the win.

matches.stipulation: The Mountie's WWA debut, billed as Inspector Max Quinn
matches.note: A total squash; the Mountie finishes with the "Maple Leaf Massacre" ankle lock.

matches.stipulation: Non-title; Todd Logan and the Magician's official tag-team debut, hastily booked as a replacement main event after Shaman is pulled with an injury by WWA trainer Tyson Lenol (voiding his scheduled match with the Magician)
matches.note: A hard-fought upset over the champions; the Magician finishes Major Havok with a spike piledriver off Logan's piledriver setup. Afterward the full Four Horsemen (Darken, Steihl, Blaze, the Preacher of Pain) run in and destroy the ring — choke-slamming the Magician, beating down Logan, Havok, and Payne with staves Yes retrieves from under the ring, and wiping out both security and the medical staff. SEAL runs out to make a save and briefly holds his own against Darken and Steihl before Steihl staffs him down as the broadcast runs out of time.

matches.stipulation: Disguise Match — both men disguise themselves and hide among the first three rows of the crowd; no disqualification, falls count anywhere; played out intermittently across the whole broadcast; billed as Bruiser's final WWA match
matches.note: Bruiser is unmasked from a fake-woman disguise first (drawing a free shot for Tracer); the brawl spills through the arena, down a flight of stairs, and eventually back to the ring, where Tracer finishes with "Case Closed" for the pin.

matches.stipulation: The Executive and Tommy Lazer second Walcott
matches.note: Walcott, mid-match, takes a phone call from his own mother at ringside before finishing Lovejoy with "The Fratliner."
A back-and-forth match; Spidero finishes with the "Cross of Fire" tornado DDT off the top rope.

Shaman runs in during the match and press-slams Goodman into the Preacher on the floor; the referee throws the match out. A brawl follows involving the Preacher's own druid manager, ended by Randy Cantley's security.

A hard-fought match, briefly interrupted mid-way by Blaze and the Preacher of Pain coming to ringside and arguing openly with Steihl and Darken over the Horsemen's own leadership — leaving the Overlords visibly unfocused. Logan and the Magician finish Steihl with a combined powerbomb/body-splash for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Gauntlet Match, opponent 1 of 3; Walcott ambushed Master Xaviar backstage earlier in the show with a chair and the "Fame-Asser"
matches.note: Walcott finishes with "The Fratliner" almost as soon as the bell rings, still selling the earlier backstage attack.

matches.stipulation: Gauntlet Match, opponent 2 of 3; Lady Rachel seconds Sir Michael
matches.note: A long, competitive match (baby powder to the eyes) that Walcott finally closes out with "The Fratastrophe," a reverse superplex.

matches.stipulation: Gauntlet Match, opponent 3 of 3 — Black Scorpion's final WWA match
matches.note: The Mimic runs in and attacks Walcott (an "Equalizer" and a "Fratliner") before a decision, and the Crusade escapes through the crowd; the gauntlet is nonetheless ruled complete in Walcott's favor.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship; Tad Simmons referees; the stipulation, set by the Outlaw, requires Kasanova to serve as Nikodemous Segier's butler for two weeks if he loses
matches.note: A chaotic main event — El Porto Spidero and Nik Segier brawl at ringside, and Todd Logan and the Magician fight Billy Coleman and New Star at the entrance, while Lantern (that night's eventual challenger) repeatedly distracts the referee at ringside. Kasanova accidentally knocks the referee out cold with a punch meant for Lantern; the Outlaw finishes Kasanova with a chair shot and a belt shot, but before he can get a cover, Darken runs in, hits the "Dark Pogostick" on the Outlaw, and press-slams the fallen Kasanova on top of him. The recovering referee counts the pin in Kasanova's favor for the title, over the Outlaw's own attack. Darken cuts a promo afterward vowing to eventually take the Outlaw's life as well as his title.

matches.stipulation: Billed as the JOB Squad vs. the Knighthood; Lady Rachel seconds the Knighthood
matches.note: Sir Michael finishes Mr. Internet with the top-rope "Wizard's Warp" for the pin.

Griggs finishes with a top-rope "Shooting Star" (a frog splash) after a back-and-forth match. Troy Walcott, Tommy Lazer, Blake Daniels, and Chad Goodman are shown watching from the crowd, Goodman apparently taking notes.

matches.stipulation: Loser Leaves Town — settling a grudge carried over from an independent promotion
matches.note: Viper finishes with the "Viper Bite" (a cobra clutch slam) to win and end Ant Banks's WWA run; Viper reveals afterward that Banks had held him down in their earlier shared promotion.

James Wish and Johnny Griggs run in mid-match and attack both men — Griggs hits a "Shooting Star" on Thornhill, Wish hits the "Last Wish" on Spidero — before any decision, announcing themselves as a new tag team afterward.

matches.stipulation: WWA Rookie Ring; Sarah seconds Wish
matches.note: A close, hard-fought title defense with several near-falls on both sides; SEAL retains with a top-rope "Blockbuster."

name: WWA Labor Day 99: Working Man's Pay Per View 99

matches.stipulation: Mask vs. Career; Walcott also defends the WWA World Television Championship
matches.note: Two masked "goons" (later revealed as Aric and Zack Crockett) interfere for the Mimic, drawing out the Fraternity (Tommy Lazer, Johnny Griggs, Chad Goodman) for a wild ringside brawl before head referee Rick Kilgore restores order. Walcott survives a figure-four and finishes the Mimic with a schoolboy rollup. The Mimic unmasks afterward as "The Painmaker" Randy Cross, revealing the whole run had been a House of Pain deception; the Crocketts and the rest of HOP swarm the ring afterward, with Randy Cross declaring the House of Pain "back."

matches.stipulation: Non-title; Nik Segier is the guest referee
matches.note: Segier deliberately refuses to count several early pin attempts by either man; when Denrol charges him, Segier sidesteps and Denrol accidentally levels his own valet, Melissa "Missy" Camero, who is taken out on a stretcher as a precaution. Kasanova wins with a low blow followed by an inside cradle, which Segier — distracted by the Missy incident — finally counts.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — Tag Team Turmoil, round 1 of 6; Lady Rachel seconds the Knighthood
matches.note: Master Xaviar injures his own knee on an accidental collision with Dudeman; Tito rolls him up using the bad leg for leverage to advance Rush.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — Tag Team Turmoil, round 2 of 6; Alf seconds the Sitcom Fathers
matches.note: The Sitcom Fathers use kendo sticks (with the referee's attention diverted to the injured Master Xaviar) to take over, finishing Tito for the pin.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — Tag Team Turmoil, round 3 of 6
matches.note: The debuting Dynamic Dudes catch the Sitcom Fathers off guard; Tito and Dudeman spray Mr. Brady in the face with a hot-sauce-loaded water gun for good measure as Radmeister finishes the pin.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — Tag Team Turmoil, round 4 of 6
matches.note: Radmeister finishes James Wish with the "Hang Ten" for the pin.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — Tag Team Turmoil, round 5 of 6
matches.note: The Overlords survive a determined Dynamic Dudes push; Darken finishes with the "Dark Pogostick."

matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — Tag Team Turmoil, final; both teams already worked one round each
matches.note: Steihl finishes the Magician with an inverted powerbomb to win the titles, crowning the Overlords of the Dark champions once again — despite the House of Pain's own earlier boast that they would leave with the belts.

matches.stipulation: WWA Rookie Ring — Battle Royal; Goliath was excused by President Harrington and did not appear

eliminations.note: Tossed early.
Rocker Dropper, tossed.
Eliminated in a joint double clothesline with Julian.
Reverse DDT, then tossed.
Clotheslined over; briefly saved himself on the rope earlier in the match.
Eliminated in a joint double clothesline with Brandon Desire.
Eliminated in the same double clothesline as Rattlesnake Ryan.
Doomsday pulled the top rope down as Inaki launched himself at Shaku Endbringer.
Eliminated in a joint double press slam by Inaki Hotaka and the Flamer.
Hauled over the top from the apron after a botched elimination attempt on the Flamer.
Armbar into a toss over the top — the final elimination, winning the match and the Rookie Ring.

matches.note: The Flamer outlasts a large rookie field to win the Rookie Ring.

matches.stipulation: For the "Famine" spot in the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse; billed as Blaze vs. Viper
matches.note: Viper finishes Blaze with the "Viper Bite" to win the match and the Famine role, and the rest of the Horsemen seal the beaten Blaze in a casket and wheel him to the back.

matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Hardcore Championship; Chad Goodman was pulled from his own scheduled challenge earlier in the show after an attack by Zack Crockett, and Shaman stepped in instead; Billy Coleman then interjects himself mid-match

eliminations.note: Pinned with "The Decent" delivered onto a huge ladder Coleman himself had set up.
Finished off after the Preacher's own mysterious "druid" manager — revealed the same night as Viper, the new Famine — locks Shaman in the "Viper Bite" to help set up the pin.

matches.note: The Preacher of Pain retains the Extreme Hardcore Championship, teasing a "Mr. Future" mystery man behind the Horsemen's recent moves afterward.

matches.stipulation: An impromptu 2-on-1 handicap match, called for on the mic by Goodman after the Crocketts attacked him (and interviewer Eric Pembrook) backstage earlier in the show, costing him his own Extreme title shot
matches.note: Goodman finishes both former tag champions in succession with back-to-back "Flashback" springboard neckbreakers.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship; Randy Cross seconds Segier
matches.note: Segier finishes Lazer with a double underhook faceslam into a submission he calls "Segier's Hammer." Afterward, NYPD officers arrest Lazer on the ramp for stalking Segier's wife, Jennifer, under a restraining order.

matches.stipulation: WWA United States Championship; Nik Segier corners Tracer for one night only; Steihl also wrestled twice already tonight in the tag turmoil
matches.note: Tracer finishes Steihl, visibly fatigued from the turmoil match, with a double underhook DDT to win the title — this served show's own account places the title change here, a month earlier than a separate WWA title ledger record of the same Bullet-over-Steihl transition (dated 1999-10-05); left as a flagged discrepancy on the affected reign rows rather than silently resolved.

matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship; the Outlaw is the guest referee
matches.note: The Outlaw counts unevenly all match, seemingly favoring Lantern, but Kasanova survives and finishes Lantern with a top-rope face slam after both men brawl atop the turnbuckle. Afterward the Outlaw attacks the celebrating Kasanova; Lantern appears to help him before decking Kasanova himself, and the full House of Pain and Youthful Rage rosters brawl in the ring. The returning Albatross, unseen for months, runs in to clear both factions off Lantern and pulls him to the back.
A total squash; Doomsday finishes with a chokeslam-type move he calls "Death is Darkness."

matches.stipulation: Inoki Hotaka's (billed "Inaki Hotaka") WWA Fights debut
matches.note: Hotaka finishes with a running kick he calls "The Dragon's Touch."
The Flamer retains with a top-turnbuckle finisher he calls "The Burn Down," afterward calling out Julian for a First Blood hardcore match that Sunday.

matches.stipulation: Trampoline Match — mini trampolines set up in each corner
matches.note: A high-flying match; Griffin finishes with a "Swinging D.D. Driver" off one of the trampolines.

matches.stipulation: Albatross seconds Lantern, newly reunited as a duo
matches.note: Lantern finishes with "The Light in the Darkness."

matches.stipulation: No disqualification; Coleman himself issued this challenge for Darken's spot in the Four Horsemen
matches.note: Darken finishes with the "Dark Pogostick." Afterward, Steihl (dressed as a "Kane" parody) helps Darken hoist the beaten Coleman up, bound, on the giant apocalypse-seal prop as a humiliation.

date.source: Dated by the fed's own period cards. The card of 28 March 1999 announces "WWA Pain Games, April 18th, Live from the SkyDome in Toronto, Canada" (promotions/wwa/archive/1999-03-28.html); the cards of 2, 7, 9 and 16 April 1999 build to it (1999-04-02, 1999-04-07, 1999-04-09, 1999-04-16); the card of 24 April 1999 opens "Tonight is the aftermath of the Pain Games" and reviews it (Billy Coleman's tournament win, the new US Champion Ravage) (promotions/wwa/archive/1999-04-24.html); the card of 9 May 1999 calls Coleman and Kasanova the winners of the Pain Games tournament and World War 3 battle royal (1999-05-09.html); and 18 April 1999 was a Sunday. The document itself prints no date. The fed's later lists put it a year early: its PPV archive page for 1998 lists "Pain Games" under "April 1998" (promotions/wwa/archive/pay-per-view-archive-1998.html) and its older PPV list (ppv/ppv.htm, Wayback capture of 30 June 2003, in the workshop's WWA captures) reads "Pain Games 98"; no 1998 card builds to it, and the period cards above settle the date.

name: Pain Games
notes: Dated 18 April 1999 (see date.source); the document prints no date. The May Mayhem it draws a spot in a "Four Corner's Match" for is 9 May 1999 (wwa-1999-05-09). In the Chicken Box match staged here Denrol's United States Championship reign (wwa-united-states-r012) ends and Ravage's (wwa-united-states-r013) begins; the fed's own later title history dates the change 19 April 1999, a day after the card, as the two reigns note. Match 3 holds the Extreme title up after the draw, its new champion to be the winner of a Bruiser v Outlaw match; that match is not in this document, and the card of 24 April 1999 calls New Star "the Extreme Champion". A scheduled Baseball Bat Handicap match (House of Pain vs. Griffin, six on one) never gets a bell: Denrol declares it a no-contest before it starts and launches the next match instead -- not structured, recorded as a plain fact.

matches.note: New Star pins Sniper (David Wattsoner) after a powerbomb through a standing steel chair, in a brawl using chairs, a ladder, barbed wire, and a table. The show's own text bills New Star as the belt's "first WWA EXTREME HARDCORE WRESTLING CHAMPION" -- in tension with the Extreme/GenX Championship's own already-tracked pre-2001 lineage (reigns.json's wwa-extreme block, continuous since 2000), which has no recorded vacancy or restart at this point. Not merged into that ledger given the primary source's own contradictory framing; flagged for the coordinator rather than resolved unilaterally -- see this session's own digest.

name: March Madness 2001

matches.note: TJ Donaldson runs in and punches New Star; the referee calls for the bell and Gary Trudeau announces New Star the winner by DQ, despite New Star being the one struck by the outside interference -- recorded exactly as the source states it, a document-level inconsistency (interference against a competitor ordinarily awards his opponent the DQ) rather than silently corrected.
Cross wins when the referee stops the match after Cage passes out in the Painmaker leglock, unable to keep his arm up for a third count.

matches.stipulation: One fall, 20-minute time limit, for sole possession of the WWA World Tag Team Championship (co-champions entering, having held the belts jointly since Rage in the Cage)
matches.note: Arlechino pins Wanderer with the Punchline, becoming the tag titles' sole champion.

matches.stipulation: Ladder match, for a contract naming the #1 contender to the WWA United States Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Moore retrieves the contract, hanging above the ring, after knocking Kraven off a dueling ladder with a kick to the head.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat, all three men legal at once, no tags, countout rescinded by WWA president Johny Morehouse, for the WWA United States Heavyweight Championship (Jones defending)
matches.note: Jones (defending) retains, pinning Walcott with a tilt-a-whirl Juvi driver after Shaman's interfering elbow drop breaks up an earlier Walcott cover. The Magician runs in mid-match to attack Shaman and Walcott, until TJ Donaldson (at ringside supporting Walcott) spears him out to the floor.
Cross pins New Star with a Pedigree to win the tournament.

matches.stipulation: For the WWA World Heavyweight Championship (Bullet defending)
matches.note: Bullet (in a full-body black vinyl disguise, briefly casting doubt on his own identity) retains, pinning Donaldson with the Pounding the Pavement on the third attempt, after both men crash through the French announce table off a top-rope elbow. Mid-match, a hooded figure caught lurking behind Bullet is unmasked by his own light-up goggles as Villain, who is punched from the ring.

notes: Backstage, Craven Moore breaks into New Star's locker room and assaults a wrestler identified only as "Stryker" before leaving with New Star's manager "Invection" -- no bell, not a match, and both figures are too thinly identified in this document alone to mint; not structured here. Several previously-listed appearances[] rows (chance-wwa, pyro-wwa, the-scorpion-wwa, jackson-wwa) named entities who do not appear anywhere in this document's own text and have been removed as inaccurate for this show.

name: Friday Night Fights — 9 Mar 2001

matches.note: A newly-scheduled addition after Vik Ventressa demands and gets added to the match backstage. Ventressa pins Spike with the Ventressicator, ending Craven Moore's reign, after Jackson Kraven blindsides Moore with a chair at ringside while the referee is distracted.

Kraven pins Mantis after Craven Moore runs in from the crowd, knocking Kraven's downed opponent's referee-distracting interference aside and blasting Mantis with a garbage can, letting Kraven make the cover. Afterward, Mantis grabs a mic and quits the WWA on air, berating Johny Morehouse.

Nelson refuses to wrestle, announcing on the mic that he quits; Johny Morehouse threatens to sue him for breach of contract unless he goes through with the match. Nelson lies down and White Ninja pins him, Morehouse making the count himself after shoving Nelson down.
Cage pins Shaman with the Shockwave.

Wanderer runs in and directs the referee's attention before chair-shotting TJ Donaldson; the DQ is awarded against Arlechino's side. Wanderer then chair-shots Arlechino too, turning on his own tag partner.

matches.stipulation: For the WWA United States Heavyweight Championship (Jones defending)

name: Friday Night Fights — 16 Mar 2001

Villain wins by submission, locking in a toehold half crab after both men kick out of their own finishers (Kryptonite reversed, a T-Bone suplex answered with a top-rope Diamond Dust).

notes: Backstage, an unseen attacker leaves Tracer Bullet and Tim Powers laid out between segments -- commentary speculates openly (TJ Donaldson, Troy Walcott, Villain, and Johny Morehouse are all floated as suspects) but the show's own text never resolves who did it; not structured as a match, recorded as an open plain-fact angle.

name: Friday Night Fights — 23 Mar 2001

matches.stipulation: March Madness 2001 Tournament, quarterfinal (Western Regional Championship)

A large masked man runs in early to soften up TJ Donaldson for Cross, then leaves before being identified. Later, Villain -- ostensibly Cross's own ally, amid visible tension between the two -- runs in and attacks Cross instead, drawing the bell; the DQ is awarded to Cross.

Opens with Johny Morehouse denying any role in the ongoing backstage attacks on Tracer Bullet, in his own executive office (no bell, not a match, recorded as a plain-fact angle).

name: WWA — 6 Apr 2001
notes: "The Best of Fights" -- a two-hour clip retrospective hosted by Johny Morehouse, no live matches. Every bout aired is a replayed clip package from an earlier show (5 Dec 1997 through the 10 Nov 2000 War Games main event already structured on its own airing date), per the fresh-filmed-vs-archival-replay rule; the only fresh content is Morehouse's own framing narration between clips. No matches[] recorded on this show for that reason, same disposition as wwa-2000-12-30's WWAmmies ceremony; its pre-existing appearances[] array (mechanically drawn from those replayed clips) is left untouched, consistent with that same precedent -- auditing that labeling is outside this pass's scope.

matches.note: A Y2K1 Tour dark match shown on Blast Off's debut, not clip footage of an earlier broadcast. Riley O'Neil, debuting as "Kahn," wins with the Sobered.

A Y2K1 Tour dark match shown on Blast Off's debut. Steihl, re-debuting under the ring name "Kuz I. Saidso," submits Wile with a modified surfboard, billed here as "Three Most Painful Words in the English Language" (formerly "Remembrance of Pain").

name: WWA — 12 Apr 2001
notes: Most of this show recaps an earlier WWA PPV not in the held record (an uncollected show) — per the anti-double-count standing ruling, that recap content is not structured into matches[] here; only the two fresh Y2K1 Tour dark matches shown live on this broadcast are.

name: WWA — 17 May 2001

matches.note: Spike (We The People, uninvolved in the match) runs in and belt-shots Fury, letting the Victor cover for the pin. matches.stipulation: For the WWA World Television Championship (Spike defending)

notes: Opens as "Blast Off," a studio recap-and-preview show reviewing the previous Monday's Meltdown (14 May 2001) in prose and promo clips -- that Meltdown episode is not itself in the held record, so its recapped matches (Fury vs. the Joker, a four-way with JC Swinger/Tim Powers/Tal/Jace Brooks, Casey Twist vs. Joey Edwards, an impromptu Shaman vs. Brian Jones screwjob, Vik Ventressa vs. Jackson Kraven, Arlechino/Wanderer vs. the Veteranz, and New Star/Villain vs. TJ Donaldson/Shawn Cage) are recap-only evidence for an unheld broadcast, not structured here. The show then goes live from Roanoke, Virginia for its first live "Blast Off" episode proper -- only that live segment's three matches are structured above. A backstage angle has the Joker ambush Casey Twist during an interview, broken up by an unnamed, unminted man who promises to make the Joker pay -- no bell, not a match.

name: WWA — 27 May 2001

matches.stipulation: Texas Death Match, for the WWA World Television Championship (O'Neil, billed as Kahn, defending)
matches.note: No pinfalls count; the loser is whoever cannot answer a ten count. Both men crash off the stage through a table, and later through a burning table (Swinger spinebusts Kahn through it; Kahn's own pant leg catches fire diving off a crate onto Swinger). Kahn barely beats the final ten count to retain.

Post-match, "Superstar" Johnny Griggs -- revealed as the masked man who earlier saved Twist from a Joker ambush on Blast Off -- attacks Joker and cuts a returning promo; James Wish then confronts Griggs from the crowd. No bell for either confrontation.

The brawl leaves the ring for the backstage area and the parking lot (a water cooler, a coffee urn, a limousine roof, a wooden bench all get used); Arlechino answers referee Greg Jones's ten count after a hotshot through a shattered bench leaves Wanderer motionless.

Trapper (unbled) and Craven Moore/Jackson Kraven's makeshift pairing fight on until the Nyte Shift's Jonny Nyte is busted open by his own brother Glenn's mistimed Nytemare, closing the match; the Veteranz retain.

Mark Harrington books Star Station-X into a Bourbon Street Brawl in response. Filed under the wwa shard per its own pre-existing accession (collection 0079); the existing michael-stryfe-wwa record (a PWF-era wrestler, later a WWA TV Champion) already establishes this precedent. notes: The pre-show recap package ("lets take a look at how this match came about") replays three archival clips setting up tonight's main event -- Shawn Cage vs. Vik Ventressa (Ventressa's original WWA World Title win), Jackson Kraven vs. Vik Ventressa (the ambulance-crash finish, already on file as wwa-world-heavyweight-r025), and Matthew Warr vacating the title and setting up a "special 3 way cage match" -- none structured here, evidence for their own original shows. The card as actually contested is a straight two-out-of-three-falls match, not the three-way originally teased. Craven Moore's on-air retirement press conference is a real-departure angle, not a match; the clip shown alongside it of his original WWA Television Championship win (dated in-text to early 2001) is likewise archival, not fresh tonight.

notes: This show's own text explicitly bills The Horsemen tag team (Shaman and The Magician) under the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse code-names "Pestilence" and "Famine" ("Pestilence and Famine, otherwise known as The Magician and Shaman"), and James Thornhill wrestles the Rumble as "War" -- the same vignette framing carried over from May Mayhem 2002. This directly recontextualizes this lane's own pestilence-wwa mint (from wwa-2002-06-09) as possibly being Shaman under a mask/persona rather than a wholly separate wrestler; not resolved here. "White Ninja," the 22nd Rumble entrant, unmasks at ringside as Harley Trapper (trapper-wwa) after his own elimination -- structured directly under his own id rather than as a separate mint, consistent with this being a one-off, resolved gimmick, not a persistent alternate identity. A pre-show video package and several mid-show references replay clips from the 1998-2001 Independence Day Rumbles and the Bourbon Street Brawl (Jackson Kraven's own number-one-contender win) -- archival, not structured here. Kade Williams's long return promo and the Craven Moore prank-call vignette are angles, not matches. The Independence Day Rumble's own eliminations are extensive (30 entrants); only the more clearly stated falls are structured above, not the complete sequence.

A six-man Survivor Series elimination tag; the third Horseman, masked as "Death," is unmasked in continuity as Darken Steihl. The Horsemen win; the full elimination sequence is not confidently resolved from the served text and is not recorded here.
For the WWA United States Heavyweight Championship (Dorian defending). Tense wins with the Ian-Tensifier to become a two-time US Champion.

Main event, for the WWA World Heavyweight Championship (Moore's second defense of the night), with special guest referee Randy Cross. Moore retains after Denrol passes out in the Sequel (a full-nelson camel clutch) and Cross counts three arm drops. Post-match, Cross turns on both men, reforming the Minnesota Wrecking Crew/House of Pain alongside Damian Thorne.

notes: Merged with the former placeholder row wwa-labor-day-brawl-2002 (collection 0010): the fed's own "Gamblers Table" prediction column (wwa-the-gamblers-table-labor-day-brawl.html) previewed this exact card — Craven Moore vs. Tracer Bullet for the World Title, Jackson Kraven vs. Denrol — as "the hottest Pay-Per-View of 2002," confirmed word-for-word against the served card once found in the chase corpus (collection 0079).

date.source: The card's own date caption reads "Friday January 9, 1997", but 9 January 1997 was a Thursday and 9 January 1998 a Friday. The fed's own title-history ledger dates the four-corners tag tournament won by the Executives Club on this card (the first World Tag Team Championship change) to 9 January 1998, its own site archive catalogues the card as jan09-98, and the tag team the card says debuted "last Friday night" (Blood and Guts) first appears on the card of 2 January 1998. SOURCES DISAGREE: the caption's year against the ledger and the archive filing; both readings are recorded.

No fall is ever counted. Angel Reaper wins by disqualification after House of Pain's Harvester of Sorrow runs in and cold-cocks him mid-match.

Cross retains, submitting Lynch with the Figure Four. Commissioner Mark Harrington lowers separate steel cages around each man's own stablemates beforehand to guarantee a clean match; the match's own loser gets the final open slot in that night's Rumble (it goes to Lynch).

36 entrants, drawn numbers, thirty-second intervals. Johnny Blaze (drawing #33) outlasts the field, eliminating the Outlaw last with a fallaway slam to win the vacant New England Championship. The final four are Blaze, the Outlaw, Aric Crockett, and Black Scorpion. The full 36-man elimination-by-elimination order is not structured here — genuinely dense simultaneous-brawl chaos through most of the match's own middle stretch — but every entrant's own participation and the winner are read directly from the served text.

Fourteen lumberjacks ring the ring, seven to a side per the broadcast's own (twice-given, slightly garbled) rundown: Mr. Business, the Executive, the Judge, Randy Cross, and the whole of Triple Threat for the Outlaw; Harvester of Sorrow, Deadbolt, Darken, Black Scorpion, the Fan, Michael Blackheart, and Bob for Blaze. Dr. Love wins and becomes the new champion, submitting Morris with a modified figure four ("the Scalpel") after landing his superkick, "the Needle."

Maim & Torture (defending) enter already worked over after Jim Black's Fortune 500 attacks their manager, Dr. Slash Hayes, backstage. For control of the WWA presidency, with Tracer Bullet wrestling as Mark Harrington's chosen representative (Harrington having lost the office in a conspiracy angle the week prior). Havok wins by pinfall with a top-rope splash he calls "Terror From Above," becoming WWA President.

A non-title match (Mantis's own WWA World Television Championship not at stake). Mantis wins by pinfall with the Shocker.

Steihl (defending) wins and retains by disqualification after Shawn Cage runs in and shatters a mirror over Steihl's head — outside interference on Satome's behalf, per the broadcast's own "Steihl escapes with the DQ win."
