matches.note: WWA Extreme Division. The Magician wins by pinfall over Bolivian Rat with a second Phantasmal Killer (flash powder assisted), Nick Bruiser too late for the save.

name: WWA — 24 Mar 2000
notes: The billed main event, Captain Amazing vs. Mantis for the WWA World Television Championship, never happens: two masked men powerbomb Amazing before the bell on Mark Harrington's orders and Harrington cancels the match on the spot — no match row recorded for it.

matches.note: Donaldson wins by pinfall with the Contradiction, upsetting Sangha to advance to the final.
New Star runs in mid-match and blinds the Magician with a blood-filled pistol; Rage wins by pinfall with the "Flaming Fury" moments later.
Satome wins by pinfall, catching a diving Thornhill (leaping from the top of the cage) with a Diamond Cutter.

The referee, revealed after the bell to be Tracer Bullet in disguise, pumphandle-powerbombs Donaldson; Rage wins by pinfall and is crowned the WWA March Madness 2000 champion, earning the Extreme Championship ladder-match slot and a WWA World Heavyweight Championship shot at May Mayhem. New president Major Havok later adds Donaldson to the ladder match as compensation, and books Tracer Bullet & Mark Harrington against Troy Walcott & Nikodemous Segier for the following show.

Steihl (defending) and Cage brawl out of the arena and into the venue kitchen, where both men end up frozen inside a walk-in freezer alongside the referee; the finish is shown only at the very end of the broadcast, after the rest of the card, when the freezer is opened and the referee counts a pin — Cage over Steihl — making Cage the new champion.
matches.stipulation: WWA United States Heavyweight Championship — No Disqualification

matches.note: Challenger Mystique voluntarily unmasks before the bell (revealing an ordinary face) and rebrands himself "Tenshi"/"Angel" for the rest of the match and after — the mask-vs-title stake is therefore moot by the time the bell rings; only the title is won. Angel wins by submission with a Judo triangle choke, ruled a legal hold by new WWA president Major Havok over Denrol ally Ricky Harrington's protest.

A four-corner match for the vacant/undisputed Extreme Championship. Bruiser climbs the ladder and retrieves the belt while the other three are still brawling on the outside, becoming WWA Extreme Champion.

Segier (World champion) escapes a folding-powerbomb Shocker attempt and pins Mantis (Television champion) from a small package; Segier leaves with both belts. Post-match, Dr. Slash Hayes's Random Acts of Violence (Maim & Torture) attack Segier, and Mark Harrington, Ricky Harrington, and Tracer Bullet appear to promise more of the same.
matches.stipulation: Title for Title — WWA World Heavyweight Championship vs. WWA World Television Championship

matches.note: No disqualification, no countout; wins by the loser being unable to answer the referee. Black wins after two Fade to Black finishers onto a steel chair, sending Havok out on a stretcher.
Winner earns a WWA United States Championship shot (a stipulation the on-screen authority figure, The Don, adds mid-match). Dumars wins by pinfall with the Dumars Drop through the broadcast table.
Captain Amazing (defending) has Hotaka in an ankle lock when TJ Donaldson runs in and knocks both men out with a chair; the referee calls for the bell with no winner.
Both men reverse a counter into a simultaneous cover, and the referee counts both men's shoulders down together — a declared double pin, no winner.

eliminations.note: Pinned together with ArchAngel in a triple-count after Shawn Cage — revealed here as "Famine," a new third Horseman alongside Mantis and Steihl — helps finish both men off.
Mantis & Steihl leave the ring and the arena immediately after their win, and are counted out and eliminated without another team ever facing them.

The Torture Chamber (Pitt & Mannheim) are eliminated by Allied Chaos (Kyle Niker & Connor Pearce) after Pearce strikes Pitt with an FWA tag title belt; the served text does not make clear which man was legally pinned.
Donaldson runs in alone (not as part of a team) and is pinned almost immediately with Pearce's "Chaos Factor" springboard moonsault.
Maim pins Pearce with the Mercy Killing after Torture spears him; Allied Chaos are eliminated and Maim & Torture (the Random Acts of Violence) become the new WWA World Tag Team Champions.

matches.stipulation: Tag Team Turmoil — WWA World Tag Team Championship

matches.note: Any pinfall makes the pinner the interim "champion," but only escaping the building with the title wins outright. Shaman (defending) loses and regains the interim fall repeatedly against Mr. Cool, Jimmy Stryker, The Magician (briefly disguised as one of the match's own celebrity-chicken referees), Nick Bruiser, and TJ Donaldson, across a brawl that runs through the kitchen, the dining area, an air duct, the upper concourse, and the parking lot (where TJ Donaldson, having escaped by motorcycle, is clotheslined and pinned by Shaman just outside the building). Shaman rolls out through a closing garage door for the real, final win and retains the title.

Segier (defending) survives interference from The Don's FWA/Dark Tide faction (The Don himself, Maim, Torture, Dehibilitator, and Jim Black all get involved) until Tracer Bullet, Mark Harrington, and Buck "the Hustler" Floyd run in and clear them out. Segier applies a modified figure four; Rage's shoulders go down from the damage and the referee counts the pin. Segier retains.
Goodman, ordered by manager Brent Wentworth to help Kasanova win, instead turns on him and wins by pinfall with the Fratliner.

The Trickster wrestles disguised as "the Masked Indian Guy" after his May Mayhem loss to Steve Dumars, revealing himself only after winning by pinfall over both Mr. Cool and TV champion Suniel Sangha (the title itself not at stake).

A one-sided beatdown: the Dehibilitator repeatedly powerbombs and piledrives Bruiser onto unfolded steel chairs and through a table, ending with a top-rope powerbomb onto two chairs; Bruiser is stretchered out and the Dehibilitator wins by pinfall.

Donaldson, over the weight limit, is admitted to the match after a loophole (weighed in kilograms rather than pounds). Amazing (defending) attempts to prove a point by suplexing Donaldson despite the weight gap; both men collapse together and the referee counts the fall for Donaldson, who becomes the new (and first over-240-pound) WWA Light Heavyweight Champion.

Cage (defending, newly christened "Famine" of the Four Horsemen) wins by pinfall with two consecutive Shockwave finishers, then insults Dumars further post-match by hitting his own Dumars Drop through a table.

Fought backstage amid a parallel brawl among allies on both sides (the Magician and ArchAngel seconding SEAL; Steihl and Shawn Cage seconding Mantis) — those side battles are not scored as part of this match. Mantis wins by pinfall with the Shocker in a pile of metal staging equipment.
matches.stipulation: No Holds Barred, Falls Count Anywhere — for the "Death" position in the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse

matches.note: Billed a non-title match, with a secret guest referee (Brian Jones) working for the Don's benefit. Jones fast-counts a fake submission from Black out of Tracer's Interrogation, then, once the hold is broken with no bell, smashes a pane of glass over Tracer's face and immediately counts a legitimate pinfall for Black.

Maim & Torture (defending) retain with help from special guest enforcer Denrol, who turns on the challengers mid-match — fast-counting a Segier near-fall down to two, chair-shotting and Evil Killer-ing both Shaman and Segier, and fast-counting the actual finish after a Maim Mercy Killing on Segier. Troy Walcott runs in for the post-match save, but the title result stands.
The Torture Chamber (billed on this show as WWA regulars booked into the new CWL) win by pinfall, Pitt superplexing Watts from the top rope.
Dr. Love's debut match. Love wins by pinfall with a superkick he calls "The Needle."
Rage's CWL debut. Sangha (defending) retains by pinfall off a low blow the referee doesn't see.

Booked by promotion authority The Don to have Maim & Torture (WWA champions, defending) drop the belts to Allied Chaos (FWA champions) and unify them — Maim and Torture refuse the order on-page instead. Torture submits Connor Pearce with the Threshold (a dragon sleeper/body scissors); Maim & Torture win and hold both sets of belts. Post-match, Dr. Slash Hayes buys the pair's contract back from the Don for one Canadian dollar, and has Maim finish the Don off with a Mercy Killing.
matches.stipulation: Unified WWA World Tag Team Championship

matches.note: Floyd wins by pinfall with a reverse flying clothesline he calls "The Scratch," becoming new FWA North American Champion and earning a title-unification match with Shawn Cage's WWA United States Championship.

Segier (already WWA World Heavyweight Champion) challenges Extreme champion Shaman with help from a table and chair slid in by The Don; Segier wins by tapping Shaman out to the Segier Stretch, adding the Extreme title to his own.

Winner was billed a US title shot, complicated afterward when Pitbull (the CWL World Champion) claims a rules loophole makes him the rightful #1 contender ahead of Kasanova. Kasanova wins by pinfall with the Kiss of Death (450 splash).
Wile (defending) retains by submission with the Canadian Death Lock, after a planted fan runs in and bronco-busters the Trickster.

A non-title match; Torture Chamber, originally the third team in a scheduled three-way, are attacked backstage by the Dehibilitator and unable to compete. TJ Donaldson wins by pinfall over Torture with a powerbomb-into-senton he calls the "Oxymoron."

No title at stake. Shaman ambushes New Star before the bell and dominates almost the entire match inside the pit (barbed wire, a barbed-wire bat, a piledriver, a top-of-the-cage dive through a table New Star rolls off at the last second). New Star is cabled out of the pit by a rescuer (Stryker) before being finished off; per the match's own win condition (getting your opponent out of the pit), the broadcast credits New Star with the win. Shaman attacks New Star again during the following commercial break.

A non-title tag match (Jim Black's WWA World Heavyweight Championship not at stake). SEAL and Mantis both run in against Jim Black's side at different points; Tracer Bullet pins Jim Black with "Pounding the Pavement" after Mark Harrington's interference is neutralized.
Amazing wins and becomes the new champion by submission, applying a figure four leglock to Wile's already-worked-over knee.

Goodman accidentally levels the referee with a clothesline meant for Rage; the Dehibilitator, sent by manager Brent Wentworth, attacks Goodman while the referee is down. Rage wins by pinfall with the Flaming DDT once the referee recovers.
Booked by Brent Wentworth as retaliation against Chad Goodman's friends. The Dehibilitator beats down both men; Wentworth himself counts the winning pinfall on Tito in place of an official referee.

Segier wrestles disguised as "Nikrol," a mocking Denrol impression, after the real Denrol (retired from WWA competition) baits Kasanova into the match instead. Segier/Nikrol wins and retains, pinning Kasanova with the Evil Killer after New Star runs in and canes Kasanova from behind.

A full roster of WWA/CWL light heavyweights surround the ring as lumberjacks. Bullet wins and becomes the new champion, rolling Donaldson up with an inside cradle. The served text's own closing announcement misstates the title as the "United States Championship" — an apparent slip in the document itself, since the match's own introduction, entrances, and in-match commentary are unambiguous that this is the Light Heavyweight title.
matches.stipulation: Lumberjack Match — WWA World Light Heavyweight Championship

name: WWA — 21 Jul 2000
notes: The billed United States Championship defense (Buck Floyd vs. Shawn Cage) never becomes a match: Cage ambushes Floyd before the bell with a chair and a Shockwave and leaves; the promotion's own authority figures state afterward that the title did not change hands from the attack. No match row recorded for it.

matches.note: Thornhill wins by pinfall with the Adrenaline Rush.

Shaman wins and becomes the new champion after Militia members Bastion and Inoki Hotaka run in and hit Amazing with a powerbomb/neckbreaker combo ("Call to Arms"); Shaman lays an arm across Amazing for the pin.
Buck Floyd pins Rage with a top-rope reverse flying clothesline ("the Scratch") while Rage is perched on Tracer Bullet's shoulders.
Segier & Kasanova win by disqualification after Jim Black strikes the referee with Stick.

Shaman (defending the TV title) wins by pinfall with the Thunderclap, taking Dr. Love's CWL International Championship as well. Post-match, Shaman chokeslams commentator Fat Tony to the floor; The Highlights (Lenny Rhodes & Scott Shields) then ambush Shaman with a dropped refrigerator and a figure four, and challenge the winner of the tag title match.
matches.stipulation: Title vs. Title — CWL International Championship / WWA World Television Championship

matches.note: Jones (defending the Canadian title) wins by pinfall with the Boston Massacre, unifying the two titles under his name; Floyd shakes his hand afterward.
matches.stipulation: Title Unification — WWA Canadian Heavyweight Championship / WWA United States Heavyweight Championship

matches.note: The match is first ruled a no contest when TJ Donaldson is knocked out (Gary Trudeau: "as a result of a concussion this match is a no contest"); WWA owner Mark Harrington then restarts it, installing manager Showtime as Amazing's emergency partner. Once medically cleared, TJ returns to ringside, sneaks into the match, and helps Amazing finish Hotaka with the Oxymoron; Amazing & Donaldson retain. Shaman runs in post-match and powerbombs Amazing.
matches.stipulation: WWA/CWL Unified World Tag Team Championship

matches.note: Climb a ladder to unhook a suspended steel crutch and force a submission. New Star wins, choking Segier out with a kata-hajime after his valet Sabbat runs in and drops a leg on Segier's arm across the crutch.
matches.stipulation: Triple Threat Ladder-Crutch Match — #1 contender for the WWA World Heavyweight Championship

matches.note: The Dehibilitator (defending) is eliminated from realistic contention when Troy Walcott (the match's mystery eighth entrant) chokeslams him through the top of the cage; the climbing rope later snaps, forcing the field onto a ladder set up on the cage roof. Shawn Cage reaches the rafters just ahead of Lyle Wile and shoves the glass display case into Wile's face to become the new champion.
matches.stipulation: Caged Extreme Championship Climb — first to reach and touch the belt, suspended above the cage from the rafters, wins

matches.note: A 60-minute-limit match, changed mid-card by new WWA president Cross to No Disqualification/No Countout for the world title match to follow. Cross wins by pinfall after Jim Black passes out in the Painmaker Figure Four (Mark Harrington having pulled Cross off a broadcast table Black tried to put him through with the Black Out). Post-match, a cloaked "Dark Man" is revealed as Cross himself, unmasking a second figure as Don Valentino, confirming Cross, Black, and the Don were allied all along; Cross assumes control of the WWA and turns on Harrington.

Bullet (the 2000 Independence Day Rumble winner) becomes the new champion, pinning Mantis after driving him face-first into the mat with a spinning fall-forward slam. Bullet then proposes to Melissa "Missy" Camero in the ring; she accepts.
matches.stipulation: No Disqualification, No Countout — WWA World Heavyweight Championship

matches.note: Ventressa wins by pinfall after blinding Rage with a paintball gun and knocking him off a ladder.
Shaman's Militia allies kidnap Rhodes's tag partner Scott Shields beforehand, leaving Rhodes to face Shaman alone. Shaman wins by pinfall with the Punished.
Kasanova wins by submission with a crucifix armlock.
Floyd wins by pinfall with a powerbomb.
A non-title match (Jones's WWA United States Heavyweight Championship not at stake). New Star wins by submission with Death (a kata-hajime choke).

President Randy Cross adds the no-DQ/falls-count-anywhere stipulation mid-match after seeing Harrington's early advantage, then sends Fortune 500 (Brian Jones, Todd Logan, Jake Spade, Jackson Kraven) to ringside against him. Tracer Bullet, Buck Floyd, Kris Kasanova, and commentator Johny Morehouse run in to even the odds; Harrington wins by pinfall over Aric Crockett and becomes sole owner of the WWA.
matches.stipulation: Handicap, No Disqualification, Falls Count Anywhere — for 100% ownership of the WWA

matches.note: Love wins by submission, locking the Needle (a superkick, used here as a hold) on David Drake.
The Victor pins Hotaka after Ventressa's ringside allies (Mickey and Karl Ravage) shoot Hotaka in the face with a paintball gun.
Shaman (defending) retains by pinfall with the Thunderclap.
Bullet (defending) retains by pinfall with Pounding the Pavement, after Buck Floyd runs in and cane-strikes Jones mid-match while chasing off an interfering New Star.
Moore wins by submission with the Moorelock (a reverse-powerbomb-into-submission hold) from the second turnbuckle.
Dehibilitator wins by pinfall with Total Dehibilitation (a top-rope powerbomb-style move).

Drake wins by disqualification after Trickster shoves the referee down and attempts a second Nose Drive on the floor, missing when Drake moves. After the bell, Drake spikes an unprotected Trickster with a tombstone piledriver on the floor; Trickster storms off in a rage.

Before the bell, New Star's valet Sabbat and manager mace SEAL backstage and New Star drives him through a locker-room bench with the Death sitout powerbomb; SEAL is taken to hospital (no bell rung for this segment — angle only). New Star then wins the barbed-wire match, pinning Nelson with Death off the top of a ladder brought to ringside by Nelson.

Shawn Cage (defending) and the other three each bring ringside vehicles loaded with weapons (a front-end loader, a forklift, a dump truck). Floyd pins Jones with a pool cue shot after an electric-chair drop through a table earlier in the match; Floyd becomes the new champion. Post-match, Shaman chair-shots Floyd with a chain, and Jones powerbombs Floyd through a table before New Star runs in and beats Floyd down with a kendo stick; Daniel E. Nelson then joins New Star, the two aligning as "Death & Pain."
matches.stipulation: WWA Extreme Championship — first fall wins

date.source: The card's own dateline for the show reads "November 19th, 2000" (the Birthday Bash of that year, whose own announced card reads "Sunday November 19, 2000"), and the fed's own Television Championship ledger dates the title change staged at this show to the same day.

matches.note: Mantis runs in near the finish and eliminates the leading Daniel E. Nelson by pulling him under the bottom rope; the timekeeper prematurely rings a bell for Nelson, but the WWA rules the bell mistaken (Nelson never actually went over the top rope) and restores him as a survivor alongside Amazing, Donaldson, and Shaman.
matches.stipulation: World Cup Battle Royal — over the top rope, both feet must touch the floor; the last four survivors advance to the semi-finals

matches.note: Kraven wins and becomes the new champion, pinning Jones after two Wall Street Crashes onto a steel chair; he continues brawling with Jones through multiple referees' attempts to separate them after the bell.

Amazing submits Nelson to a Kryptonite for what a substitute referee (subbing in after Shaman knocked the original ref out) counts as a pinfall win for Amazing & Shaman; WWA president Johny Morehouse overturns the result in the ring afterward, ruling the substitute referee was never sanctioned to finish the match and awarding the win to Nelson & Donaldson on the technicality.
matches.stipulation: World Cup Battle Royal Semi-Final Tag — winning team advances to a singles final for the World Cup

matches.note: Bullet (defending) retains, pinning New Star with Pounding the Pavement after both men kick out of each other's finishers (Death and Pounding the Pavement) earlier in the match.

Nelson wins by knockout after roughly 28 minutes, applying a Sharpshooter until Donaldson (his knee and head both worked over across the night, including two ringside-stairs shots) passes out rather than submitting.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Cup Final — winner earns a WWA World Heavyweight Championship match at Rage in the Cage

matches.note: A pre-broadcast dark match, recapped in clips once the show goes on air. Moore wins by submission with the Moorelock after a stun gun into a powerbomb.
Amazing wins by pinfall after the Dehibilitator (dressed as a nerd/doctor gimmick) runs in and clobbers Matthews with a clipboard.

Knight hits his Morningstar finisher but SEAL kicks out; the brawl spills onto the stage, where Knight is thrown through a table, and SEAL then executes the Fourth Seal on both Knight and a masked ally through two more tables. No bell, referee count, or official winner is shown on air; SEAL cuts a post-match promo, but the document never declares a result, so none is recorded here.
matches.stipulation: No Disqualification (declared mid-match by the referee)

matches.note: Kraven wins by pinfall with the Wall Street Crash; referee Rick Kilgore is knocked out mid-match (a Kraven superplex on Drake lands on him) and is revived just in time to make the count.
Kasanova wins by pinfall with the Kiss of Death, earning a title match against Shaman the following week.
matches.stipulation: #1 contender for the WWA World Television Championship

matches.note: New Star and Nelson work together against Bullet for most of the match; Nelson pins Bullet with a schoolboy rollup off a suspiciously fast three-count from Valentino, who is shown afterward pulling a payoff of cash from a duffel bag. Post-match, Valentino, New Star, and Nelson triple-team Bullet until TJ Donaldson runs in (his in-ring WWA return) and is in turn beaten down, until SEAL and a bandaged Malachiah Knight run in and brawl with everyone as the broadcast ends.
matches.stipulation: Triple Threat, non-title (Tracer Bullet's WWA World Heavyweight Championship not at stake); special guest referee Don Valentino

name: Friday Night Fights — 3 Nov 2000
notes: Buck Floyd (having won the WWA Extreme Championship the previous Friday and been powerbombed through a table by Brian Jones and beaten down by New Star and Daniel E. Nelson afterward) announces his in-ring retirement on this show and vacates the Extreme Championship; no new match results from the segment.

matches.note: Love wins by pinfall after the Victor runs in and chair-shots Hotaka behind the referee's back; Love then dumps his manager Nurse Candy Hart on air.
Kraven wrestles hurt after being lead-piped by Brian Jones backstage earlier in the show. Moore wins by submission with the Moorelock.
Othock (managed by Ian Kurt, in his WWA debut) wins by pinfall with a bronco buster he calls the Abomination, after knocking Drake out with the ring bell behind the referee's back.

Before the match, Vik Ventressa ambushes Shaman backstage and spikes the title belt into his chest after a Ventressicator on the concrete (angle, not a match). Kasanova wins and becomes the new champion, pinning the hobbled Shaman with the Kiss of Death.

Brian Jones is attacked backstage before the match (a plate-glass window shot from a masked assailant) and enters hurt; Nelson later handcuffs Jones to the cage wall mid-match. TJ Donaldson powerbombs New Star off the top of the cage through the ring itself; New Star is knocked out and Nelson (now captain in his place) surrenders the match rather than continue three-on-one.
matches.stipulation: War Games — entrants enter on a staggered timer; ends only when a wrestler submits or a team's captain surrenders for the whole team

matches.note: Daniel E. Nelson is announced as the twelfth entrant but never appears (a jumbotron video shows him skipping the match entirely). The Victor and Vik Ventressa win and become the new champions, last eliminating TJ Donaldson.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Tag Team Championship — 12-man tag team rumble, eliminated over the top rope with both feet touching the floor

matches.note: New Star and Sabbat win after Sabbat shoves the referee down mid-count following an elevated bulldog on Melissa Camero, while Tracer Bullet is tangled in the ropes by the neck and unable to break it up.
matches.stipulation: Intergender Tag Team, no-DQ by prior agreement between New Star and WWA officials

matches.note: Nurse Candy Hart, having pretended to leave Dr. Love for Drake as a planted-spy angle, turns on Drake mid-match and chokes him with a stethoscope while Love hits the Sexbomb; the referee rings the bell for a no-contest rather than award either man a decision.
TJ Donaldson wins by disqualification after a mysterious man dressed as Captain Amazing in black ("the Dark Amazing") runs in and attacks him.
matches.stipulation: Jace Brooks's WWA in-ring debut, managed by Dirk Popple

matches.note: The Victor & Vik Ventressa (defending) retain by disqualification after Shaman chair-shots both Vik Ventressa and manager Karl Ravage; Shaman and Hotaka leave without further incident, calling their issue with the champions settled. Craven Moore runs off a post-match Militia beatdown of Brian Jones later in the show.
Jones wins and becomes the new champion, pinning Kraven with the Boston Massacre (a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker).

Nelson wins by pinfall with New Star's Death, rolling Mantis up while the referee (having been knocked briefly unconscious) misses that Mantis had a foot on the bottom rope; a replay after the bell shows the blown call.
Samson wins by pinfall with his finisher, "The Living Legend."

Manager Dirk Popple trips Brooks mid-match, seemingly by accident, letting the Dehibilitator take control; Dehibilitator wins by pinfall with a piledriver after slapping Brooks (Popple, not Brooks, throws the slap).

Moore wins by disqualification after Jones smashes a TV monitor into his face; per the standard title-doesn't-change-hands-on-DQ convention (Jones is not pinned or made to submit), Jones (defending) retains the title.

Nelson's cornerman Lackey nearly throws in the towel repeatedly but holds off; Melissa Camero distracts Lackey with a kiss and throws in Nelson's towel herself, handing Mantis the win while Nelson is caught in the Interrogation. Mantis then backbreakers his own towel-man Greg after the bell.
matches.stipulation: Towel Match — a cornerman throwing in the towel ends it

matches.note: Referee Rick Kilgore is knocked out by a Shaman boot mid-move; Daniel E. Nelson, confronting Missy Camero at ringside, accidentally chair-shots Tracer (the intended target was Missy) while trying to threaten her, and the recovering referee counts Shaman's pin. Shaman becomes the new champion. Mantis attacks the fallen Tracer afterward, warning him he has until Rage in the Cage to reclaim the title before Mantis takes it from Shaman himself.

A masked heel calling himself "Villain" (dressed to mock Captain Amazing) repeatedly interferes — brass knuckles, a fake three-count disguised as a referee, a distraction fight with Amazing — and is dealt with mid-match by both men rather than ejected. TJ wins by pinfall, knocking Black out with a new finisher he calls Neuphoria before pinning him; Amazing overturns Villain's earlier fake fast count and calls the finish clean.

Dr. Love is eliminated first (a Victor/Drake double-team piledrives him onto a frying pan). Vik Ventressa, despite fighting off several non-entrant interferers (Mr. Internet, Joey Edwards, Tim Powers, Spike), is eliminated next by the Victor after a paintball shot to his hurt knee. Kraven and Moore are both eliminated in two rapid pinfalls that the show's own commentators explicitly say they can't sort out (Kraven spears Moore through a storefront window for one count; David Drake immediately pins "the wreck of" the two men for a second) — the document does not resolve which man went out on which count. The Victor wins in the final two over Drake, pinning him after a Victory (a fireman's-carry powerbomb) off a picnic table.
matches.stipulation: Mall Brawl — a falls-count-anywhere elimination brawl staged through a shopping mall; the last man standing becomes the #1 contender to Brian Jones's WWA World Television Championship at Rage in the Cage

matches.note: A rematch after Shaman's chair-shot-assisted title win the week before; president Johny Morehouse books it inside a cage specifically to rule out outside interference. Tracer wins and becomes the new champion, climbing out of the cage after a blockbuster off the top of it. Manager Ian Kurt reveals afterward that he now represents both Tracer and Shaman.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Heavyweight Championship, Steel Cage — win by pinfall, submission, or escaping the cage

matches.note: Walcott wins by knockout, locking on the Trojan Reigns until Dehibilitator, having lost too much blood, passes out. New Star, Sabbat, and Stryker attack the fallen Dehibilitator afterward and throw him off the entrance ramp (angle, not a match).
Ventressa wins by submission, locking the Sharpshooter on Spike.
matches.stipulation: Handicap — Vik Ventressa alone against four of the six members of We the People (two of the group's six, including Crimson Warrior, are eliminated from the match beforehand by a pre-match game of rock-paper-scissors)

matches.note: Love wins by pinfall with the Sex Bomb after manager Nurse Candy Hart distracts the referee.
Archelino & Wanderer win and become the new champions, Wanderer submitting Wile with a camel-clutch variant he calls the Everlasting Pain.

Brian Jones (defending) handcuffs himself into taking Kraven out of the running with a Wall Street Crash; Vik Ventressa runs in and bungee-hoists the Victor bodily into the rafters, removing him from the match. Moore and Kraven end up racing each other over the top of the cage together and fall at the same instant; a replay shows Moore's hand touching the floor a fraction before Kraven's body does. Moore is ruled the winner and becomes the new champion.
matches.stipulation: Fatal Fourway, Steel Cage — first to escape the cage wins; WWA World Television Championship

matches.note: The Magician wins and becomes the new champion, pinning Shaman after both men fall through a table following a ramp-area dive; Shaman appears to have the pin himself moments earlier but voluntarily throws the title belt down rather than accept a win he felt he hadn't earned clean.
Cross wins by submission, locking on the figure four after both men crash through the ring canvas together from the top of the cage earlier in the match.
matches.stipulation: Steel Cage — win by pinfall, submission, or escape

matches.note: Villain wins by pinfall with a move he calls Kryptonite.

The match runs through a string of falls whose exact tally the broadcast itself narrates inconsistently (commentary at one point calls it a three-way tie at one pinfall each, immediately after a sequence that reads as Nelson having been pinned twice) — recorded here without trying to reconcile that ambiguity. Tracer Bullet (defending) is credited with an early pin over Nelson (forced by Mantis dragging Tracer's arm across him); Nelson then pins Mantis with a rollup; Mantis pins Nelson with a double-powerbomb DVD. The clear, unambiguous finish: Mantis pins Tracer Bullet with a Hangman's DDT he calls the Evil Killer, and Gary Trudeau announces Mantis the new champion on that fall alone. Mantis then hits the Evil Killer on Nelson as well, after the bell.
matches.stipulation: Endgame — a tag-style triple threat inside a steel cage, only the two legally tagged-in men may wrestle at a time; WWA World Heavyweight Championship

matches.note: Hotaka wins by pinfall with the Dragon's Touch.

Wanderer & Archelino win by pinfall, Wanderer hitting Joey Edwards with a slingshot clothesline he calls the Superstar Clothesline; the champions Lyle Wile and the Trickster run in afterward and beat down both new #1 contenders.
matches.stipulation: #1 contenders for the WWA World Tag Team Championship

matches.note: Drake wins by pinfall with the Drake Slam (a full-nelson slam).

Shaman's own Militia stablemate Inoki Hotaka turns on him mid-match, and the rest of the Militia run in and attack Shaman; the referee calls for the bell. The document's own commentary states plainly that Shaman wins by disqualification despite being the one assaulted by his own stablemates — an inconsistency in the source's own logic, recorded here as written rather than silently corrected. WWA president Johny Morehouse announces afterward that Shaman will face a mystery opponent, the Magician, at Rage in the Cage.

Both men attempt simultaneous neckbreaker-drop finishers, collide in mid-air, and land in a pile the referee counts as a double pinfall; the match is ruled a draw, leaving the #1 contendership unresolved.
matches.stipulation: #1 contender for Tracer Bullet's WWA World Heavyweight Championship at Rage in the Cage

matches.note: We the People members (Spike, Joey Edwards, Crimson Warrior, the White Ninja) repeatedly interfere at ringside. The Victor wins by pinfall with the Victory (a fireman's-carry powerbomb).
Archelino wins by pinfall with a crucifix rollup, a promising sign ahead of his and Wanderer's WWA World Tag Team Championship match against Trickster & Lyle Wile at Rage in the Cage.
Jones (defending) retains, pinning Ventressa with the Boston Massacre after manager Bruce King illegally assists an abdominal-stretch hold from ringside.
matches.stipulation: WWA World Television Championship, Lumberjack rules (We the People members Joey Edwards, Crimson Warrior, the White Ninja, Mr. Internet, and Spike surround the ring)

matches.note: Moore wins, reaching the fourth and final turnbuckle after Kraven's grip on the bottom rope fails at the last second.
matches.stipulation: Texas Strap Match — win by dragging the opponent to touch all four turnbuckles in succession

matches.note: Randy Cross (filling in for the traveling-delayed Nelson, per Ian Kurt's own in-storyline explanation before the swerve) wins by pinfall, powerbombing Villain onto TJ Donaldson for the cover (Villain's own finisher, Kryptonite, is also landed on TJ earlier in the sequence). After the bell, the masked 'Captain Amazing' removes the mask to reveal Daniel E. Nelson underneath, and Nelson, Villain, Randy Cross, Ian Kurt, and Lois Lame all reveal themselves as a coordinated unit, beating down TJ Donaldson to close the show. FLAG FOR THE COORDINATOR: this reveal recontextualizes the WWA's running 'mystery masked attacker' angle (the 'Dark Amazing' attacks beginning around wwa-2000-12-01) as Nelson in disguise; earlier late-2000/early-2001 shows carrying a genuine captain-amazing appearance were NOT re-audited against this reveal in this lane's pass — a future pass should check whether any of those rows need reattribution to daniel-e-nelson-wwa.
matches.stipulation: Tag team; Daniel E. Nelson wrestles the entire match disguised as Captain Amazing (with Lois Lame at ringside playing along), a ruse the show's own text does not reveal to the viewer until after the bell — the real Captain Amazing does not appear on this show

name: WWA Sunday Extreme — 23 May 1999

date.source: Not directly served — no primary document for this show survives in the recovered corpus. wwa-1999-05-26 (a Wednesday) opens by billing three of its own segments as replays "from last Sunday's Extreme" and later "from Sunday," which pins the date to the Sunday immediately preceding, 23 May 1999.

evidence.note: Five matches replayed on the jumbotron during this broadcast, with full commentary reconstructing each one blow by blow — the only surviving record of this show.

Both men's WWA debuts. Madison wins with a moonsault.

matches.stipulation: The Mimic and Black Scorpion accompany the Crusade team to ringside
matches.note: Billy Coleman ambushes the Mimic and Black Scorpion with chairs before the bell, and the Fraternity (Lazer, Walcott) fights them off; a fourth Fraternity member, Paul Styles, runs in mid-match to help. Walcott pins Master Xaviar with the "Pretty Plex." Styles is invited into the Fraternity on the mic afterward.

A no-show angle: Bruiser appears only via a pre-taped military-base clip, then ambushes Crash live through the crowd. House of Pain runs in and swarms Bruiser after a low blow from Crash; the referee awards Bruiser the match by disqualification.

A long hardcore brawl through the crowd; Steihl wins after New Star misses a New Star Press through a table and Steihl slams his face into the concrete for the pin. Commentary frames the win as reforming Darken and Steihl's own "Overlords of the Dark" tag team, consistent with the pair's own backstage segment on wwa-1999-05-05.

WWA Television Championship. MidCarder wins the title with the Average Man Slam while Flynn Steele is locked out of the cage.

CPE against F.E.A.R., with Lantern as CPE's mystery partner. Lantern wins with a victory roll on Daring.

WWA United States Championship. O'Hara retains with a crucifix pin; Todd Logan is knocked out of the cage trying to interfere. O'Hara, MidCarder and Kasanova then stage the Youthful Rage skit and announce the stable.
